model.description: Partial source reconstruction of Level-0 definitions and scoped physical, optical, retinal, visual and neural records. Formal specifications, computational models, experimental preparations, reported observations and conditional interpretations have distinct meanings and evidence. Reviewed studies retain their own systems, selections, observables, uncertainty limits and unresolved contradictions. Physical records distinguish quantum-field definitions, scattering and decay measurements, Bell tests, vacuum quantities, QED and QCD running, lattice spectra and charge searches. Calibrated masses, detector unloading times, storage-loss rates and intrinsic-lifetime interpretations are separate quantities. Neutron survival studies retain production years, diagnostic controls, shared data and non-decay-loss corrections. Four-flavor QCD+QED mass splittings retain physical-point inputs, finite-volume prescriptions, convention-dependent components and the additional experimental input to a calibrated ratio. Capture-based neutron-mass inference distinguishes campaign angles, crystal calibration, nuclear recoil, unit conversions, adopted isotope masses and recalibration of shared data. Penning-trap inputs distinguish charge-normalized frequency ratios, voltage controls, neutral-atom corrections and correlated mass fits. LIONTRAP separates original acquisition, experimental reanalysis, shared-data controls and conditional electrode-geometry predictions. Proton-decay searches separate selected channel counts, nuclear and detector response, shared exposure, conditional partial-lifetime bounds and printed arithmetic. Magnetic-moment records distinguish electron and proton spin/cyclotron inference from neutron/mercury precession and its external absolute scale. Electron resonance fits, cavity calibration and radiative interpretations retain separate inputs and limits. Shared campaigns, source-specific correction conventions and uncertainty aggregation remain explicit. Cross-domain construction, universal carrier minima, downward causal rules and a derivation of quantum theory from Level 0 remain unestablished. No whole-graph scientific validation is claimed. Light-flavor families retain approximate representation conventions, a conditional historical Omega event and a response-corrected meson transition ratio; these do not establish real-time family formation. Perturbative amplitude and state-boundary conventions are separate from a synthetic kinematic check and from measured particle populations. No universal downward confinement mechanism is admitted. Free-field time evolution, historical electroweak mass relations and reactor-neutrino phase conventions retain specified models. Collider candidates and reactor signals are separated from response, backgrounds and fitted inferences; finite algebra does not reproduce those experiments. Solar active-flavor decomposition, atmospheric angular distributions and Higgs tau-pair evidence retain their original acquisitions and conditional fits. Matter evolution and coupling-rate definitions state their approximation boundaries; reused samples and post-fit displays are not independent experiments. Accelerator tau appearance and historical W/Z observations preserve selected candidates, adopted detector response and conditional original inferences. The single-doublet Higgs background and charged-fermion coupling are formal definitions with supplied parameters, distinct from a measured mass hierarchy or a universal stability mechanism.
model.name: Causal Emergence — Canonical Reconstruction

nodes.name: Test a persistent ensemble
nodes.shortDescription: carrier closure; collective persistence; comparison with uncoupled and alternative couplings; defined collective observables

nodes.name: Admit a mode candidate
nodes.shortDescription: consistent operator and dispersion convention; specified domain, units and boundary conditions; stationarity residual and convergence within declared tolerances

nodes.name: Test localized objecthood
nodes.shortDescription: declared independent variables and equations; localization under domain enlargement; nontrivial concentration; stationarity; specified static and dynamic perturbative persistence

nodes.name: Test a new carrier interface
nodes.shortDescription: explicit forward abstraction map; declared state and intervention domain; macro closure error and uncertainty; substitution/interface test; independent target or analytical certificate

nodes.name: Compare eligible candidates
nodes.shortDescription: fully specified functional; eligible candidate cohort; frozen coefficient and tolerance policy; retain all tied extrema; sensitivity analysis

nodes.name: Test joint triadic closure
nodes.shortDescription: admitted modes; signed frequency and wave-number balance; declared simple-cycle and rank surrogate; removal witnesses for the exact closure predicate

nodes.name: Anisotropy hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed directional criterion whose specific derivation and observables remain unresolved in the reviewed foundation paper.

nodes.name: Carrier promotion contract
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed transition from persistent collective organization to a new state space and admissible operations, tested by a forward abstraction map.

nodes.name: Dispersion parameter m²
nodes.shortDescription: Under the declared case convention ∂²tΨ−∂²xΨ+m²Ψ=0, m²=ω²−k². Reconcile the source action and operator together before using this as a general rule.

nodes.name: Selection among eligible candidates
nodes.shortDescription: A comparison operation on an explicit cohort using a defined functional; retain ties and report sensitivity. Selection is distinct from physical generation.

nodes.name: Compensation relation
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed balance relation between primitive distinctions; a measurable functional remains open.

nodes.name: CRT carrier class — no admitted instance
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed localized persistent carrier, admitted only after every declared objecthood gate passes. The existing expanded case admits none.

nodes.name: Perturbation test candidate
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed perturbation protocol. Perturbative persistence motivates testing but does not establish directional mechanisms.

nodes.name: Directional gradient hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A retained proposal requiring a defined state variable, domain, gradient operator and source-specific derivation.

nodes.name: Discrete scale hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A discrete admissible spectrum is an open hypothesis. E=ℏω and p=ℏk do not force continuous parameters to become discrete.

nodes.name: Distinguishability
nodes.shortDescription: A declared criterion for distinguishing configurations; its domain and equivalence relation remain to be operationalized.

nodes.name: Ensemble carrier class
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed collection of admitted CRT carriers with a specified coupling and demonstrated collective persistence; no such input cohort exists in the current case.

nodes.name: Ensemble action family
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed coupling functional for admitted carriers. Nonzero coupling alone does not establish a stable collective regime.

nodes.name: Promoted carrier class
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed effective carrier with a tested state map, dynamics and intervention interface. No effective next-level dynamics have been derived here.

nodes.name: Assumed hyperbolic analytic frame
nodes.shortDescription: An indefinite bilinear frame within the selected two-direction quadratic model class. The assumptions are explicit and not derived from unrestricted absence of structure.

nodes.name: Integrated density Γ
nodes.shortDescription: Γ=∫ρ dμ on a declared support with measure and normalization. Conservation and finiteness require separate conditions.

nodes.name: Local density ρ
nodes.shortDescription: For a declared complex field, ρ(x)=|Ψ(x)|². This nonnegative quantity alone does not establish localization or irreducible closure.

nodes.name: Nonlinear action family
nodes.shortDescription: A candidate interaction model requiring explicit independent fields, constraints and boundedness analysis. Tested completions have not supplied an object-qualified CRT.

nodes.name: Admissibility context Ω
nodes.shortDescription: The author’s foundational possibility context. It is neither an observed material substrate nor a measured physical field in this release.

nodes.name: Oscillatory mode class
nodes.shortDescription: Candidate solutions under a declared wave operator, domain and boundary conditions. Equation satisfaction is separate from objecthood.

nodes.name: Premetric frame
nodes.shortDescription: A formal context for primitive distinctions before a metric is introduced. Kept separate from an assumed analytic metric.

nodes.name: Quadratic action family
nodes.shortDescription: An assumed quadratic derivative action. The source operator sign must be reconciled, and stationarity does not certify a minimum.

nodes.name: Sequential distinction
nodes.shortDescription: A primitive ordering direction. Identifying it with measured physical time requires an additional model.

nodes.name: Spatial distinction
nodes.shortDescription: A primitive direction of separability. Physical distance and dimension are not supplied by this definition.

nodes.name: Synchronization observable
nodes.shortDescription: A collective observable requiring specified variables, phase convention and tolerance. Agreement alone is not a promoted carrier.

nodes.name: Transport bias hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A retained proposed effect requiring a transport model and evidence of the stated bias.

nodes.name: Triad candidate configuration class
nodes.shortDescription: A class of joint three-mode candidates passing a declared resonance and closure surrogate. Passing this stage does not establish localized objecthood.

nodes.name: Triadic admission predicate
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed joint closure test for three modes. Simple-cycle minimality is conditional on the chosen graph class.

nodes.name: Trial field domain
nodes.shortDescription: The declared class of complex trial fields on which an action and density can be defined before any solution passes admission tests.

nodes.name: Unique neural accumulator hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: The selected behavioral and neural findings do not uniquely identify a LIP-local accumulator as the necessary implementation of all decision making.

nodes.name: Event cascades in jointly activated acute slices
nodes.shortDescription: Acute rat slices under combined NMDA and D1-agonist exposure exhibit sampled event cascades; these are distinct from the culture records.

nodes.name: A1 agonist does not rescue D1-neuron receptor loss
nodes.shortDescription: In Extended Data Figure 8h, CPA co-treatment did not prevent the increased D1-challenge seizure susceptibility of Adora1 flox/Drd1a-Cre mice. Rescue in CD39-deletion mice cannot be transferred to a preparation lacking the relevant neuronal receptor.

nodes.name: D1 challenge after D1-neuron A1-receptor deletion
nodes.shortDescription: Adora1 floxed mice crossed to Drd1a-Cre versus controls, challenged with 5 mg/kg SKF81297.

nodes.name: D1-challenge seizure incidence after neuronal A1 loss
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 4k source counts report seizures in 5/6 Adora1 flox/Drd1a-Cre mice versus 2/12 controls after D1 agonist. This receptor deletion differs from microglial CD39 deletion.

nodes.name: Unified affective property hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A single system-wide evaluative property does not follow from a projection-specific exploration assay; its representation and relation to conscious feeling remain unresolved.

nodes.name: Astrocyte calcium under alpha1B blockade
nodes.shortDescription: Cyclazosin treatment reduced the L-MO radial astrocyte calcium response evoked by NE-MO stimulation. Pharmacology supports alpha1B receptor involvement without proving exclusive astrocyte-specific action.

nodes.name: Genotype whole-cell capacitance null
nodes.shortDescription: The reported whole-cell capacitance comparison did not differ significantly between Arf6 genotypes. This supports the specified current-density comparison without demonstrating equal cell function or membrane lipid abundance.

nodes.name: Control-cell PIP2 current null
nodes.shortDescription: No significant Kir-current change was reported after bath diC16-PIP2 in Arf6fl/fl control cells. This null is separate from the current increase in knockdown cells and is not an equivalence test.

nodes.name: Arf6 genotype with subsequent barium
nodes.shortDescription: Ten Arf6fl/fl and nine Arf6iECKD mice; pre/post 100 micromolar cortical barium laser-Doppler responses, distinct from the PIP2 cohort.

nodes.name: Whisker perfusion after partial Arf6 loss
nodes.shortDescription: Arf6 knockdown mice had lower untreated whisker-evoked perfusion responses than littermate controls in the reported comparison. Subsequent barium reduced both responses, with a smaller reported barium-sensitive fraction in knockdown mice; no exact fraction is calibrated.

nodes.name: Kir current after partial endothelial Arf6 loss
nodes.shortDescription: Capillary endothelial cells from inducible Arf6 knockdown mice had lower barium-sensitive Kir current density than littermate controls. Partial endothelial knockdown is distinct from complete or capillary-restricted deletion.

nodes.name: Arf6 genotype and isolated cEC currents
nodes.shortDescription: Tamoxifen-treated Arf6iECKD and Arf6fl/fl littermates; conventional patch clamp with 60 mM external potassium and barium subtraction.

nodes.name: Microvessel ATP-depletion comparisons
nodes.shortDescription: Separate 0.1 mM GTPgammaS/PBS and 3 micromolar NAV-2729/DMSO comparisons; four to seven male mice and vehicle-normalized assay batches.

nodes.name: Microvessel kinase-activity proxy
nodes.shortDescription: GTPgammaS reduced residual ATP and NAV-2729 increased it relative to their separate vehicle controls in the supplemented microvessel lysate assay. The inverse readout supports altered kinase activity, not direct endothelial membrane PIP2 measurement.

nodes.name: Upstream dilation under NAV-2729
nodes.shortDescription: NAV-2729 reduced upstream arteriole dilation to focal capillary potassium in the ex vivo preparation relative to vehicle. Diameter is the observed endpoint; conducted voltage is inferred rather than directly recorded in this assay.

nodes.name: NAV and concurrent PIP2 during whisker flow recording
nodes.shortDescription: Anesthetized laser Doppler with manual whisker stimulation; twenty-minute 3 micromolar cortical NAV exposure, separate vehicle and NAV plus 0.5 mg/kg intravenous diC16-PIP2 groups.

nodes.name: Whisker perfusion under NAV and concurrent PIP2
nodes.shortDescription: Cortical NAV-2729 reduced whisker-evoked relative perfusion. Concurrent intravenous diC16-PIP2 preserved a larger response relative to NAV alone, but did not restore the higher vehicle-treated response. Groups and pre/post comparisons remain distinct.

nodes.name: NAV-associated Kir current decline and protection
nodes.shortDescription: Pipette NAV-2729 caused a time-dependent reduction of capillary endothelial Kir currents relative to vehicle. Bath diC16-PIP2 present before recording preserved much of the current during NAV exposure; it was not a sequential rescue after current loss in the same cell.

nodes.name: NAV-2729 in potassium-stimulated CaPA
nodes.shortDescription: Capillary 10 mM potassium for ten seconds; 0.1-1 micromolar NAV in the bath, with pressure-induced and U46619-preconstricted preparations pooled.

nodes.name: NAV-2729 with pre-recording PIP2 supplementation
nodes.shortDescription: Three micromolar NAV in the pipette, with or without 10 micromolar bath diC16-PIP2 preincubated for twenty minutes; sixteen-minute whole-cell recording with repeated voltage ramps.

nodes.name: Exclusive Arf6-PIP2 vascular mechanism
nodes.shortDescription: The genetic, pharmacological and supplementation results constrain a PIP2-dependent interpretation. Direct lipid measurements and selective tests of alternative Arf6 pathways are needed to establish exclusive mediation or a general disease-restoring mechanism.

nodes.name: PIP2 supplementation in a separate Arf6 cohort
nodes.shortDescription: Eight Arf6fl/fl and seven Arf6iECKD mice, each measured before and after 0.5 mg/kg intravenous diC16-PIP2.

nodes.name: Perfusion response after PIP2 in Arf6 knockdown
nodes.shortDescription: Intravenous diC16-PIP2 increased the whisker-evoked perfusion response in Arf6 knockdown mice in a separate cohort. The nonsignificant treated-genotype contrast does not establish complete equivalence or restoration of every vascular function.

nodes.name: Kir current after PIP2 in Arf6 knockdown cells
nodes.shortDescription: Bath diC16-PIP2 increased the measured Kir current in capillary endothelial cells from Arf6 knockdown mice relative to untreated knockdown cells. The result supports a supplementation effect without direct measurement of endogenous lipid concentration.

nodes.name: PIP2 supplementation in Arf6 knockdown cECs
nodes.shortDescription: Separate isolated-cell treatment conditions with 10 micromolar bath diC16-PIP2 before patch recording; cells nested within three mice per condition.

nodes.name: Resting tone null under NAV
nodes.shortDescription: The ex vivo comparison reports no significant resting-tone change under the tested NAV-2729 concentrations. Conflicting tone normalization and pooled preconstriction conditions prevent numerical interpretation as exact preserved contractility.

nodes.name: Vehicle-associated perfusion increase
nodes.shortDescription: The Figure 4c vehicle group showed increased whisker-evoked perfusion after treatment relative to its own baseline. Vehicle is therefore not an inert zero-change comparator in this experiment.

nodes.name: Free-swimming controls after astrocyte ablation
nodes.shortDescription: No significant change in free-swimming frequency or velocity was reported after the selected astrocyte ablation. This control differs from the restrained fictive-passivity assay and does not establish full equivalence.

nodes.name: Passivity after astrocyte ablation
nodes.shortDescription: Partial two-photon ablation of hindbrain radial astrocytes reduced time in futility-induced passivity in selected larval zebrafish; it did not abolish all passive behavior.

nodes.name: Swim output after astrocyte GPCR activation
nodes.shortDescription: Light activation of gfap-driven Opto-alpha1-AR in hindbrain radial astrocytes reduced fictive swim power relative to controls.

nodes.name: Passivity after TRPV1 activation
nodes.shortDescription: Capsaicin treatment of fish expressing rat TRPV1 sparsely in radial astrocytes increased passive time in closed loop; transgene-negative and saline controls did not show the same effect.

nodes.name: Stimulus-linked glutamate sensor response
nodes.shortDescription: In the DG slice imaging assay, astrocyte VGLUT1 deletion reduced CNO-evoked glutamate-sensor responses. Responses were detected in a subset of tested astrocytes; exact population proportions remain unresolved.

nodes.name: Astrocyte VGLUT1 deletion during glutamate imaging
nodes.shortDescription: In the DG slice imaging assay, astrocyte VGLUT1 deletion reduced CNO-evoked glutamate-sensor responses. Responses were detected in a subset of tested astrocytes; exact population proportions remain unresolved.

nodes.name: Paired DG field potentiation
nodes.shortDescription: Theta-burst LTP was lower in DG synaptic fields near recombined VGLUT1-deficient astrocytes than in neighboring unrecombined fields. Figure 3 source data contains 16 paired normalized measurements; this does not establish universal astrocyte necessity for LTP.

nodes.name: Sparse astrocyte VGLUT1 deletion in DG
nodes.shortDescription: Theta-burst LTP was lower in DG synaptic fields near recombined VGLUT1-deficient astrocytes than in neighboring unrecombined fields. Figure 3 source data contains 16 paired normalized measurements; this does not establish universal astrocyte necessity for LTP.

nodes.name: AVAR calcium response
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, AVER activation produced increased downstream AVAR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).

nodes.name: AVDR calcium response
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, AVJR activation produced increased downstream AVDR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).

nodes.name: AVER stimulation protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Targeted two-photon activation of AVER during population calcium imaging in the Randi WT-background preparation.

nodes.name: AVJR stimulation protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Targeted two-photon activation of AVJR during population calcium imaging in the Randi WT-background preparation.

nodes.name: Nonrunning affect-assay comparisons
nodes.shortDescription: The reported nonrunning open-field and forced-swim comparisons did not show significant treatment effects on the named outcomes. Novelty-suppressed-feeding reporting contains conflicting significance statements. These tests do not establish equivalent affective states or clinical antidepressant efficacy.

nodes.name: Bicuculline field-LTP comparison
nodes.shortDescription: At eight weeks, field LTP recorded with 10 micromolar bicuculline did not differ significantly between treatment groups. These separate slices do not establish equal single-neuron plasticity or a matched within-cell reversal of the no-bicuculline effect.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and retained BrdU labels
nodes.shortDescription: The day-56 dentate assay found more retained BrdU-labeled cells after the Bax manipulation: reported means 3004 versus 11113, three mice per group. BrdU was given on days 9-18; only a subset expressed NeuN, so the total is not a count of mature functional neurons.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and retained BrdU labels assay
nodes.shortDescription: NCff mice, tamoxifen 2 milligrams intraperitoneally daily for five days versus equal-volume vehicle, beginning at at least eight weeks; BrdU 150 milligrams per kilogram daily on days 9-18, terminal dentate counting on day 56.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and context discrimination
nodes.shortDescription: In the nine-day similar-context task, male NCff mice given tamoxifen had higher discrimination ratios than vehicle controls (11 versus nine mice; reported treatment P=0.023). This supports a task-specific behavioral effect; it does not directly measure neural pattern separation or general memory improvement.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and context discrimination assay
nodes.shortDescription: NCff mice, tamoxifen 2 milligrams intraperitoneally daily for five days versus equal-volume vehicle, beginning at at least eight weeks; male-only testing eight weeks later, shock-associated A and similar nonshock B, nine days, ratio (A-B)/(A+B). Figure 2c and Methods disagree on context order; the per-animal schedule remains unresolved.

nodes.name: Single-trial context comparison
nodes.shortDescription: NCff groups showed no significant difference in next-day freezing in the trained context or in the very different context C (14 mice per group). Separate Cre-negative controls address tamoxifen exposure. This null does not negate the distinct similar-context discrimination result.

nodes.name: Neuron-count mediation hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: An increase in surviving dentate neurons is a candidate mediator of the Bax manipulation’s task-specific effects. Nestin-lineage breadth, altered cell properties and other cohort differences require selective mediation and rescue tests before neuron count alone becomes a causal construction rule.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and DCX population
nodes.shortDescription: Eight weeks after tamoxifen, NCff mice had more dentate DCX-positive cells and more DCX-positive cells with tertiary dendrites than vehicle controls (three mice per group). This is a marker-population response to the Bax manipulation, not a direct neuron birth-rate measurement.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and DCX population assay
nodes.shortDescription: NCff mice, tamoxifen 2 milligrams intraperitoneally daily for five days versus equal-volume vehicle, beginning at at least eight weeks; day-56 dentate DCX immunohistochemistry and separate total/tertiary-dendrite counts.

nodes.name: Four-week DCX comparison
nodes.shortDescription: At four weeks, the total DCX-positive population comparison was nonsignificant; the tertiary-dendrite subset was reported at P=0.05, with four mice per group. The eight-week increase cannot be assigned unchanged to this earlier assay.

nodes.name: Discrimination protocol variants
nodes.shortDescription: Two supplementary contextual-discrimination variants report treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06, with interactions or selected day-specific differences. Their schedules and contrasts differ from the main task; they do not constitute uniformly significant treatment main effects.

nodes.name: Task-specific learning and retention nulls
nodes.shortDescription: Named recognition, water-maze, active-avoidance, extinction and memory-clearance endpoints showed no significant treatment benefit in their separate cohorts. These are not equivalence findings or evidence that all behavior is unchanged; novel-object habituation locomotor responses included a significant interaction.

nodes.name: Bax proliferation-marker nulls
nodes.shortDescription: Reported Ki67 proliferation-marker comparisons were nonsignificant at four and eight weeks after tamoxifen (four and five mice per group, respectively). These samples do not establish an exactly unchanged birth rate or make survival the only possible mediator.

nodes.name: Running comparison-specific nulls
nodes.shortDescription: In running-housed mice, reported light-dark, novelty-suppressed-feeding and forced-swim comparisons were nonsignificant in ten vehicle and eleven treated mice. The separate home-cage activity sample used seven per group and was also nonsignificant; open-field exploration is a different result.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and exploration during running
nodes.shortDescription: In the running-housed comparison, tamoxifen-treated NCff mice showed greater open-field path length, rearing and center exploration than vehicle controls (11 versus ten mice). Changed locomotion prevents an isolated anxiety interpretation and does not establish a human therapeutic effect.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and exploration during running assay
nodes.shortDescription: NCff mice, tamoxifen 2 milligrams intraperitoneally daily for five days versus equal-volume vehicle, beginning at at least eight weeks; shared-cage wheel access from five weeks after treatment; Figure 4 shows behavioral testing on days 64-84, with ten vehicle and eleven treated mice.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and dentate field LTP
nodes.shortDescription: At eight weeks, the Bax manipulation increased the weak-tetanus dentate field-LTP response without bicuculline (reported treatment P=0.039). This population assay does not identify the contribution of each birthdated neuron or prove a complete cell-number mediation route.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and dentate field LTP assay
nodes.shortDescription: NCff mice, tamoxifen 2 milligrams intraperitoneally daily for five days versus equal-volume vehicle, beginning at at least eight weeks; eight-week medial-perforant-path field recordings, four one-second 100-Hz trains spaced 15 seconds apart, without bicuculline; eight slices/six controls and eleven slices/seven treated mice.

nodes.name: Alternate bracketing mismatch
nodes.shortDescription: For Alternate, post-experimental brackets in the pooled 42-person sample do not significantly correlate with the proposed language parse (reported r=0.08, P=0.77). Participants favor repeated AB pairs rather than the model-predicted series of alternations.

nodes.name: Binary sequence bracketing agreement
nodes.shortDescription: Post-experimental visual bracketing agrees with the proposed language for nine of ten templates in the reported group correlations. Seven shared templates pool the 23 fMRI and 19 MEG participants; three fMRI-only templates use 23 participants.

nodes.name: Binary description model comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Among twelve reported models, combining LoT-chunk cost with first-order transition surprise has the lowest reported AIC for sensitivity and correct-response time. The comparison comprises six complexity measures, each with and without surprise, using participant random intercepts.

nodes.name: Binary sequence violation detection
nodes.shortDescription: In the 23-person fMRI behavioral sample, all tested template/violation-position conditions have above-chance detection. Across the ten template means, sensitivity decreases with assigned description cost (reported R squared 0.95), while correct-response time increases (R squared 0.85).

nodes.name: Binary sound detection task
nodes.shortDescription: Twenty-three adults detect single-tone violations in ten 16-tone templates during fMRI. Tones last 50 ms with 250 ms SOA. Each template and its swapped A/B version has ten habituation sequences and eighteen test sequences, six containing a violation; button responses are required during test blocks. Twenty mini-sessions span five runs. Post-experimental visual bracketing allows repeated auditory re-exposure.

nodes.name: Binary deviant fMRI association
nodes.shortDescription: BOLD responses to all deviants decrease with assigned complexity across a broad network, and all nine selected task ROIs have a negative linear complexity effect. A small medial superior frontal region has the opposite whole-brain association.

nodes.name: Binary habituation fMRI association
nodes.shortDescription: In the 22-person imaging sample, habituation BOLD responses covary positively with assigned description cost in a broad frontal, parietal, temporal and cerebellar network. All nine selected task ROIs have a positive linear effect; seven have a negative quadratic term, with right precentral and right superior temporal regions as exceptions.

nodes.name: Detected-deviant fMRI controls
nodes.shortDescription: Restricting the fMRI model to correctly detected deviants retains a narrower negative complexity map. Four of nine task ROIs retain corrected negative effects: bilateral superior temporal cortex, left intraparietal sulcus and right cerebellar lobule VIII; the other five do not reach the stated corrected threshold.

nodes.name: Binary task and functional localizer
nodes.shortDescription: In the same imaging sample, all seven independently localized mathematics ROIs show positive habituation complexity effects, while four show negative deviant effects. Most language ROIs have weak or absent positive modulation, but left IFG pars opercularis shows positive habituation and negative deviant effects, and posterior STS shows a negative deviant effect.

nodes.name: Binary standard-trial fMRI association
nodes.shortDescription: For standard test items, positive complexity associations occupy a narrower parietal, precentral and cerebellar network than during habituation, alongside negative associations in other regions.

nodes.name: Binary violation decoder readout
nodes.shortDescription: A classifier trained on standard versus deviant MEG item epochs across the seven templates shows stronger violation readout for simpler sequences. The reported average decision-vector contrast and temporal-generalization analysis are nonsignificant for Shrinking and Complex, while the five simpler templates show significant violation readout.

nodes.name: Binary sequence evoked field power
nodes.shortDescription: In the separate 19-person MEG sample, evoked global field power has a positive complexity association during habituation (reported 108-208 ms), no significant standard-item association, and negative deviant associations (116-300 and 312-560 ms).

nodes.name: Position-specific binary violation signals
nodes.shortDescription: Despite nonsignificant average temporal-generalization results for Shrinking and Complex, Figure 8 reports significant violation signals at position 15 for both; their other tested positions are nonsignificant. Pairs&Alt.1 also shows context-dependent responses inconsistent with the tested first-order transition account alone.

nodes.name: Binary MEG transition-statistics controls
nodes.shortDescription: Sensor regressions report complexity-related clusters in habituation, standard and deviant trials after the specified controls for current/next repetition or alternation and first-order transition surprise. The transition observer uses a decaying history of approximately 100 observations.

nodes.name: Binary sequence description language
nodes.shortDescription: The study describes A/B sequences using stay (+0), switch (b), repetition, variation and nested composition. Its LoT-chunk model forbids descriptions that split a contiguous run of identical items. Figure 1 assigns costs 4, 6, 6, 6, 12, 15, 16, 18, 21 and 28 to its ten selected templates. These are grammar-dependent description scores, not measured bits, neural counts or a physical minimum.

nodes.name: Direct BLA somatic activation
nodes.shortDescription: Somatic ChR2 illumination in the high-stress comparison; distinguish this recruitment from the CeA terminal field.

nodes.name: BLA terminal activation in CeA
nodes.shortDescription: Unilateral ChR2 terminal illumination in the high-stress cohort; 20 Hz, 5 ms pulses; off/on/off exploration assays.

nodes.name: BLA-to-CeA terminal inhibition
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral eNpHR3.0 terminal illumination with continuous amber light in a separate low-stress cohort.

nodes.name: RGC-input engulfment after C3 loss
nodes.shortDescription: P5 microglia in C3 knockout mice engulfed less labeled RGC input than WT littermate controls. The developmental knockout does not isolate microglial C3 production or an exclusive complement pathway.

nodes.name: Developmental C3 loss in the engulfment assay
nodes.shortDescription: Whole-animal C3 knockout versus WT littermates, CTB tracing at P4 and microglial volume reconstruction in P5 dLGN.

nodes.name: CA1 plasticity under astrocytic Gq stimulation
nodes.shortDescription: In the reviewed SC-CA1 slice assays, MrgA1 agonist or endothelin stimulation of astrocytic Gq pathways produced calcium elevations without significant modulation of the reported transmission, PTP or LTP readouts.

nodes.name: CA1 plasticity in IP3R2 knockout slices
nodes.shortDescription: IP3R2 knockout and WT littermate slices showed no significant difference in the reported SC-CA1 PPF, PTP and LTP assays; this is a pathway- and preparation-scoped null result.

nodes.name: NMDA-sensitive CA1 potentiation induction
nodes.shortDescription: DL-APV prevents potentiation induction at doses that spare basal evoked field responses in the reported assay.

nodes.name: Pro-inflammatory cytokines after Calca-cre activation
nodes.shortDescription: Calca-cre nodose hM3Dq activation reduced circulating IL-6 and IL-1beta after LPS. IL-10 did not differ significantly and is represented separately; this population does not inherit the TRPA1-associated three-analyte profile.

nodes.name: Calca-cre nodose activation with LPS
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral nodose hM3Dq versus mCherry with CNO; eleven treated and nine control mice, with two-hour cytokine sampling.

nodes.name: IL-10 null after Calca-cre nodose activation
nodes.shortDescription: The Calca-cre nodose hM3Dq versus mCherry comparison reported no significant circulating IL-10 difference after LPS (P=0.88), despite reduced IL-6 and IL-1beta. This is not an equivalence test or the TRPA1 IL-10 effect.

nodes.name: Upstream dilation after capillary potassium
nodes.shortDescription: Focal capillary 10 mM potassium dilated the attached upstream arteriole ex vivo. Barium treatment and endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 deletion suppressed this response in the specified comparisons.

nodes.name: Feed arteriole dilation in vivo
nodes.shortDescription: Capillary 10 mM potassium increased upstream feed-arteriole diameter in the in vivo paired comparison. This does not imply that the stimulated capillary itself dilated.

nodes.name: Capillary stimulation with upstream diameter imaging
nodes.shortDescription: Acute anesthetized cranial window; eight paired upstream-diameter experiments in seven mice.

nodes.name: Focal capillary potassium and RBC passage
nodes.shortDescription: Anesthetized cranial-window line scans; 200-300 ms pressure ejection, paired baseline and peak flux. Wild type eleven mice, knockout nine and barium-treated wild type six.

nodes.name: High-potassium capillary response boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Capillary 25 or 60 mM potassium failed to sustain the upstream dilation elicited by 10 mM potassium in the same ex vivo dose comparison. Transient traces and the stimulated vessel segment constrain interpretation.

nodes.name: Stimulated capillary diameter null
nodes.shortDescription: No significant local capillary diameter change was detected after focal potassium in eighteen capillaries from seven mice. The measured sites lacked pericytes according to the Discussion; this is not a general test of pericyte control.

nodes.name: Capillary potassium in pressurized CaPA
nodes.shortDescription: Forty mmHg CaPA, focal capillary stimulation and upstream diameter; six wild-type preparations from six mice and five knockout preparations from five mice, with 30 micromolar bath barium in wild type.

nodes.name: Control-ejection flux and velocity nulls
nodes.shortDescription: Pressure ejection of 3 mM potassium aCSF did not significantly change RBC flux or velocity in the six-mouse paired control. This bounds the injection artifact under that protocol, without proving equivalence.

nodes.name: Capillary RBC flux after focal potassium
nodes.shortDescription: Focal capillary 10 mM potassium increased peak RBC flux in wild-type mice. The response was attenuated in endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 knockout and barium-treated wild-type groups; flux counts RBC passages per second.

nodes.name: Capillary RBC velocity after focal potassium
nodes.shortDescription: Focal capillary 10 mM potassium increased RBC velocity in the wild-type comparison; no significant increase was detected in the knockout or barium-treated comparisons. Velocity was measured in the peak-flux bin and is distinct from flux.

nodes.name: Upstream smooth-muscle hyperpolarization
nodes.shortDescription: Focal capillary 10 mM potassium hyperpolarized upstream arteriolar smooth muscle in the isolated CaPA recording. This is a direct voltage measurement at the sampled upstream cell, not along every intervening endothelial contact.

nodes.name: Potassium-evoked RBC flux under TTX
nodes.shortDescription: Focal capillary potassium still increased RBC flux under cortical tetrodotoxin, while whisker-evoked flux was suppressed in the separate control comparison. Ejected potassium bypasses the physiological release step.

nodes.name: Capillary potassium after sodium-channel blockade
nodes.shortDescription: Three micromolar cortical TTX; five paired experiments from five mice for the potassium-evoked flux comparison.

nodes.name: Focal potassium and RBC line-scan slopes
nodes.shortDescription: The Figure 3 imaging cohorts; RBC velocity extracted from line-scan angles in the selected peak-flux interval.

nodes.name: Capillary potassium with upstream microelectrode
nodes.shortDescription: Pressurized CaPA with 800 nM wortmannin to prevent movement; paired upstream smooth-muscle voltage before and during capillary potassium in five preparations from five mice.

nodes.name: Loss of conducted dilation after separation
nodes.shortDescription: Separating the capillary tree from its feed arteriole removed the upstream dilatory response to capillary 10 mM potassium, while direct arteriolar potassium still evoked dilation. Continuity is supported; a particular connexin is not identified.

nodes.name: Attached and severed CaPA stimulation
nodes.shortDescription: Six preparations from six mice; capillary stimulation before and after separation, followed by direct arteriole stimulation.

nodes.name: Targeted cortical capillary lesion
nodes.shortDescription: Within-animal baseline imaging followed by a localized laser lesion of an SR101-outlined cortical capillary, through thinned skull or a small cranial window.

nodes.name: A1 agonist with D1 challenge after CD39 loss
nodes.shortDescription: The CD39-deletion preparation received 5 mg/kg SKF81297 with 0.1 mg/kg CPA; compare the separate D1-only and co-treatment cohorts in Figure 4i.

nodes.name: A1 agonist rescue of the CD39 seizure phenotype
nodes.shortDescription: CPA co-treatment reduced the reported D1-challenge seizure incidence in the CD39-deletion preparation: 1/9 co-treated mice versus 9/11 in the D1-only cohort. The co-treated control cohort had 0/5 seizures.

nodes.name: D1 agonist challenge after CD39 loss
nodes.shortDescription: Inducible Cd39 flox/Cx3cr1-CreERT2 versus control mice challenged with 5 mg/kg SKF81297; behavioral stage IV-V seizures monitored over one hour.

nodes.name: D1-challenge seizure incidence after CD39 loss
nodes.shortDescription: After D1 agonist challenge, Figure 4i source counts report seizures in 9/11 CD39-deletion mice and 1/11 controls. This is a challenge-specific incidence comparison.

nodes.name: No significant striatal microglial density change
nodes.shortDescription: Extended Data Figure 8c reports no significant striatal microglial density difference after conditional CD39 deletion (four mice per group). Gene deletion and cell depletion are therefore different interventions; the null does not prove identical cell physiology.

nodes.name: Striatal adenosine-assay fluorescence after CD39 loss
nodes.shortDescription: The CD39-deletion cohort had lower striatal adenosine-assay fluorescence after D1 agonist than controls. Figure 4h source data are relative fluorescence units, not extracellular adenosine concentrations.

nodes.name: CD39 loss in the striatal tissue assay
nodes.shortDescription: Cd39 flox/Cx3cr1-CreERT2 versus control mice after 5 mg/kg SKF81297; dissected striatum was weighed, sonicated in PBS and analyzed with a fluorometric adenosine assay.

nodes.name: Accessibility response under c-Fos knockdown
nodes.shortDescription: AAV c-Fos shRNA attenuated ECS-associated chromatin opening at regions annotated with c-Fos binding sites compared with control shRNA. This supports a contribution to the induction response under this perturbation.

nodes.name: Dentate c-Fos shRNA with ECS or sham
nodes.shortDescription: AAV2/9 c-Fos shRNA or control shRNA delivered to dentate gyrus one week before ECS/sham; ATAC and RNA responses sampled separately. One knockdown sequence and unequal ATAC replicate counts limit inference.

nodes.name: RNA response under c-Fos knockdown
nodes.shortDescription: c-Fos shRNA attenuated induction of RNA for genes associated with the selected activity-responsive regions compared with control shRNA. Parallel accessibility and RNA effects do not uniquely establish that accessibility mediates the RNA response.

nodes.name: No detected late c-Fos enrichment at selected loci
nodes.shortDescription: Selected-locus ChIP-qPCR reported c-Fos enrichment at one hour but no significant enrichment at baseline or four hours, while c-Fos protein was barely detectable at four hours. The null is detection- and locus-dependent, not proof that c-Fos is absent or unnecessary for maintenance.

nodes.name: c-Fos-independent maintenance of chromatin opening
nodes.shortDescription: The proposal that c-Fos initiates opening while other mechanisms maintain it is compatible with the reviewed induction and late-binding measurements. Necessity during maintenance requires a temporally selective perturbation after opening has occurred.

nodes.name: Accessibility response to c-Fos overexpression
nodes.shortDescription: AAV c-Fos overexpression without ECS partially mimicked activity-associated opening at c-Fos-associated regions compared with EYFP control. It does not establish sufficiency for all activity-dependent chromatin changes.

nodes.name: Dentate c-Fos overexpression without ECS
nodes.shortDescription: AAV2/9 c-Fos expression compared with EYFP control one week after delivery, in the absence of ECS; separate ATAC and RNA assays.

nodes.name: RNA response to c-Fos overexpression
nodes.shortDescription: Without ECS, c-Fos overexpression increased RNA abundance for genes associated with c-Fos-induced chromatin opening. Similar distributions of selected expression changes do not establish molecular or functional equivalence to ECS.

nodes.name: Unique structure-to-function mapping hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: The proposed derivation of functional dynamics from anatomical topology remains a model-selection question.

nodes.name: Conscious-experience emergence hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: The historical conscious-experience card was already a hypothesis. A generative explanation of subjective experience remains unresolved by these neural readouts.

nodes.name: CR3 contralateral-territory control
nodes.shortDescription: At P30, the contralateral projection territory showed no significant increase in CR3 knockout mice despite increased eye overlap and broader ipsilateral territory. The anatomical readouts remain distinct.

nodes.name: RGC-input engulfment after CR3 loss
nodes.shortDescription: P5 microglia in CR3/CD11b knockout mice engulfed less labeled RGC input than WT littermate controls. Engulfment persisted, so CR3 is not established as the sole route of input removal.

nodes.name: Developmental CR3 loss in the engulfment assay
nodes.shortDescription: Whole-animal CR3/CD11b knockout versus WT littermates, CTB tracing at P4 and microglial volume reconstruction in P5 dLGN.

nodes.name: Eye-specific projection overlap after CR3 loss
nodes.shortDescription: Ipsilateral and contralateral RGC projection territories overlapped more in CR3 knockout dLGN at P10 and P30. This is an anatomical refinement endpoint, not a direct measurement of synaptic transmission.

nodes.name: Developmental CR3 loss in the puncta assay
nodes.shortDescription: CR3 knockout and WT littermates at P32-35; array tomography of VGlut2-positive RGC terminals and GluR1-positive postsynaptic sites in dLGN.

nodes.name: Developmental CR3 loss in the segregation assay
nodes.shortDescription: CR3 knockout and WT littermates; distinct-eye CTB tracing and blinded projection-overlap analysis at P10 and P30.

nodes.name: Structural synaptic puncta after CR3 loss
nodes.shortDescription: Juxtaposed VGlut2/GluR1 puncta and total VGlut2-positive puncta were more densely represented in CR3 knockout dLGN. These structural markers do not directly measure electrical efficacy or prove a unique engulfment mechanism.

nodes.name: Critical mechanism for neural avalanches hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Avalanche scaling alone does not identify a critical neural mechanism, self-organization or universal information-processing optimality.

nodes.name: Sampled cortical-culture event avalanches
nodes.shortDescription: Cultured rat cortical LFP events, thresholded and grouped into consecutive occupied time bins, have the reported avalanche-size statistics.

nodes.name: Picrotoxin exposure in cortical cultures
nodes.shortDescription: GABA-A antagonist picrotoxin, 2 micromolar in three cultures, with before/during and 24-hour washout observations.

nodes.name: Aortic endothelial electrical coupling readouts
nodes.shortDescription: Arterial endothelial Gja4/Gja5 deletion increased apparent input resistance and decreased apparent capacitance in the aortic whole-cell assay. These coupled-network measurements do not establish brain endothelial conduction velocity.

nodes.name: Aortic endothelial electrical coupling readouts comparison
nodes.shortDescription: En face aortic patch clamp; six cells from two mice per genotype; a ten-millivolt step from minus forty millivolts at room temperature.

nodes.name: Aortic neurobiotin spread
nodes.shortDescription: Neurobiotin loaded through a patch pipette reached fewer neighboring aortic endothelial cells after arterial Gja4/Gja5 deletion. Residual multicell fills occurred; the result is not complete elimination in every measurement.

nodes.name: Aortic neurobiotin spread comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Ten-minute intracellular neurobiotin loading; six control and eight mutant fills from two mice per genotype, followed by fixation and counting.

nodes.name: Local diving-arteriole response null
nodes.shortDescription: No significant genotype difference was detected for focal visual dilation of diving arterioles within mapped active regions, using seven controls and four mutants. This local null does not establish whole-network equivalence.

nodes.name: Cerebral gap-junction signal carrier
nodes.shortDescription: Arterial deletion, aortic electrical recordings and cortical response timing constrain an electrical interpretation. Direct brain endothelial voltage and selective carrier tests are required to distinguish current from other gap-junction-mediated signals.

nodes.name: Focal visual pial diameter response
nodes.shortDescription: Pial arterial diameter responses to focal visual stimulation were smaller and more spatially restricted in arterial connexin mutants. This two-photon endpoint retains a separate local diving-arteriole null.

nodes.name: Focal visual pial diameter response comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Awake focal eighteen-degree visual stimulation for four seconds; direct two-photon diameter measurements in ten controls and nine mutants, with blank-screen subsets of seven and four.

nodes.name: Focal visual optical vascular response
nodes.shortDescription: The widefield HbT-related arterial response to focal visual stimulation showed reduced spatial extent in connexin mutants. The optical response and its fitted decay are not calibrated blood flow or a graph edge length.

nodes.name: Focal visual optical vascular response comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Awake four-second focal visual stimulation; interleaved GCaMP/IOS imaging in nine controls and eight mutants, with distance assigned from thresholded GCaMP activity.

nodes.name: Distant full-field time-to-peak null
nodes.shortDescription: The 800-1200-micrometer full-field visual bin had no significant genotype difference in optical-response time-to-peak. More proximal delays do not support an all-distances rule.

nodes.name: Full-field visual optical vascular response
nodes.shortDescription: Full-field visual stimulation evoked a more spatially restricted arterial HbT-related response in connexin mutants. The assay does not directly measure ATP demand, oxygen use or adequacy of metabolic supply.

nodes.name: Full-field visual optical vascular response comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Awake four-second full-screen noise covering more than eighty-three degrees; GCaMP/IOS imaging in three controls and five mutants.

nodes.name: Full-field vascular time-to-peak
nodes.shortDescription: Connexin mutants had longer optical-response time-to-peak in the three full-field distance bins extending through 400-800 micrometers. The 800-1200-micrometer bin did not show a significant genotype difference.

nodes.name: Full-field vascular time-to-peak comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Three controls and five mutants; full-field visual stimulation, optical trajectories and distance-stratified mixed-model comparisons.

nodes.name: Distant optogenetic time-to-peak null
nodes.shortDescription: The 1600-2000-micrometer optogenetic distance bin had no significant genotype difference in optical-response time-to-peak. This null limits generalization of the nearer-bin delays and does not prove equivalence.

nodes.name: Optogenetic optical vascular response
nodes.shortDescription: ChRmine stimulation produced smaller, more spatially restricted arterial HbT-related responses in connexin mutants. Distance is measured from opsin expression, and the zero-laser trials can retain vascular responses.

nodes.name: Optogenetic optical vascular response comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Awake somatosensory ChRmine stimulation at ten milliwatts per square centimeter for two seconds; IOS imaging in six mice per genotype; zero-laser and lower-power comparison trials.

nodes.name: Optogenetic vascular time-to-peak
nodes.shortDescription: Connexin mutants had longer optical-response time-to-peak in the five reported distance bins extending through 1200-1600 micrometers from ChRmine expression. The 1600-2000-micrometer bin is a separate nonsignificant result.

nodes.name: Optogenetic vascular time-to-peak comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Six mice per genotype; high-power two-second optogenetic stimulation, optical response trajectories and distance-stratified mixed-model comparisons.

nodes.name: Optically derived vascular propagation speed
nodes.shortDescription: The response-onset-versus-distance calculation yielded slower arterial propagation in connexin mutants. This velocity is derived from optical vasomotion trajectories; it is neither RBC velocity nor directly measured electrical conduction.

nodes.name: Optically derived vascular propagation speed comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Six mice per genotype; selected pial branch sampled at forty-five-micrometer intervals; sigmoid ten-percent onset and inverse time-versus-distance slope. Trial-subset reporting requires reconciliation.

nodes.name: Vascular connexin reporter organization
nodes.shortDescription: Reporter distributions distinguish Cx37/Cx40 arterial territories, Cx43 transition/capillary territories and Cx45 capillary/venous territories. Cx40 does not extend to the smallest terminal arterioles; reporter patterns alone do not specify functional signal routing.

nodes.name: Resting pial diameter distribution
nodes.shortDescription: The sampled resting pial arteries were larger in connexin mutants. The reported rank-sum comparison treats vessels as independent despite nesting within six mutant and four control mice; retain the observation without a calibrated genotype effect.

nodes.name: Resting capillary RBC velocity null
nodes.shortDescription: Median resting capillary RBC velocity did not differ significantly between six mutants and three controls near one hundred micrometers below the pia. This is a sampled velocity control, not a demonstration of unchanged whole-brain perfusion.

nodes.name: Retinal large-artery tracer spread
nodes.shortDescription: Retinal large-artery serotonin fills were restricted to single probe cells in the sampled connexin mutants. Spreading events in controls depended on favorable loading and were observed in only two of four mice.

nodes.name: Retinal large-artery tracer spread comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Four mice per genotype, six to nine weeks after tamoxifen; viral SERT overexpression and terminal transcardial serotonin loading.

nodes.name: Small-vessel tracer persistence
nodes.shortDescription: Small-arteriole and capillary serotonin fills were observed in all examined retinal animals of both genotypes. This qualitative persistence does not establish equal conductance, complete sparing or a numerical coupling index.

nodes.name: Tail-cuff pressure nulls
nodes.shortDescription: No significant systolic or diastolic tail-cuff pressure difference was detected between the five mice of each genotype. Awake warmed and restrained tail measurements do not establish equal cerebral pressure or complete systemic equivalence.

nodes.name: Connexin zonation as a routing rule
nodes.shortDescription: Vascular connexin zonation is a candidate constraint on signal propagation. The reporter maps and joint arterial deletion do not establish that a specific isoform arrangement uniquely generates directional routing or a minimal vascular graph.

nodes.name: Cyclazosin during NE-MO activation
nodes.shortDescription: Cyclazosin treatment reduced the L-MO radial astrocyte calcium response evoked by NE-MO stimulation. Pharmacology supports alpha1B receptor involvement without proving exclusive astrocyte-specific action.

nodes.name: Cytokines after Dbh-cre cNST activation
nodes.shortDescription: Dbh-cre cNST hM3Dq activation reduced circulating IL-6, IL-1beta and TNF and increased IL-10 after LPS. The four-analyte endpoint does not demonstrate that norepinephrine is the required mediator.

nodes.name: Dbh-cre cNST activation with LPS
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral cNST hM3Dq versus matched mCherry with CNO, four mice per group and two-hour blood ELISA after 0.1 mg/kg LPS.

nodes.name: Corticosterone null after Dbh-cre activation
nodes.shortDescription: At two hours after LPS, the Dbh-cre cNST hM3Dq versus mCherry comparison reported no significant circulating corticosterone difference (four mice per group). A single concentration null does not exclude every hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal contribution.

nodes.name: Dbh-cre activation in endotoxaemia
nodes.shortDescription: cNST hM3Dq versus mCherry with repeated CNO around 12.5 mg/kg intraperitoneal LPS; nine mice per group.

nodes.name: Survival after Dbh-cre activation and endotoxin
nodes.shortDescription: In the separate high-dose LPS assay, Dbh-cre cNST activation improved survival relative to mCherry controls through the plotted nine-day window. This does not establish treatment efficacy against bacterial infection or an interchangeable nodose protocol.

nodes.name: Task-related neural choice correlations
nodes.shortDescription: LIP firing carries stronger choice correlations than MT in the recorded task; correlation alone does not establish necessity.

nodes.name: Adult rhesus dentate neuronal-label detection null
nodes.shortDescription: The four adult autoradiography cases contained no reported heavily labeled profile with typical granule-neuron morphology. The five-year-old seven-injection case had small labeled SGZ profiles at three months. Sixteen injections remain four animals; the oldest collection retains a label given six years earlier.

nodes.name: Separate committed dentate precursor lines
nodes.shortDescription: Separate neuronal and glial precursor lines are proposed from developmental phenotypes and later GFAP/ultrastructural findings. The study does not trace ancestry and does not exclude common multipotent founders, additional glial lines or conditional neuronal potential.

nodes.name: Rhesus developmental dentate labeling profiles
nodes.shortDescription: Early developmental short-interval animals have labeled SGZ profiles, with fewer profiles reported at later sampled ages. Separate longer-survival animals provide retained-label observations. The text reports one-hour short survival while Table 1 prints one day, so neither exact timing nor a common quantitative production rate is resolved.

nodes.name: Rhesus early neuronal-appearing birth-label profiles
nodes.shortDescription: Early longer-survival preparations contain labeled profiles with granule-neuron morphology. About 150 sections across three later postnatal preparations yielded eight profiles classified as definitive granule neurons, only one in P90-P155. Morphological identity and regional location do not trace a common founder or continuous migration.

nodes.name: Rhesus SGZ GFAP composition without birth-label selection
nodes.shortDescription: GFAP microscopy of small SGZ cells gives age-specific tissue-composition observations. The E144 specimen was not thymidine-labeled; its approximately half-positive fraction and later higher fractions do not measure the phenotype distribution of adult newborn cells.

nodes.name: Rhesus retained-label and GFAP colabels
nodes.shortDescription: Combined light microscopy identifies both GFAP-positive and GFAP-negative thymidine-labeled SGZ cells at juvenile ages and in the five-year-old animal. Adult Figure 6B-C is separate from juvenile Figures 4C-D and 5B. GFAP negativity alone does not establish neuronal identity or precursor potential.

nodes.name: Rhesus labeled-cell ultrastructure
nodes.shortDescription: Combined electron microscopy found a dozen reliably radiolabeled cells across three animals aged six months, one and a half years, and five years; six were GFAP-positive. No examined labeled profile had reported neuronal ultrastructure or synapses. This is a pooled three-age subset, with unresolved glial subtype wording for Figure 12B.

nodes.name: Dentate population potentiation
nodes.shortDescription: Perforant-path conditioning can produce persistent changes in dentate population responses.

nodes.name: Developmental chemical connectivity
nodes.shortDescription: Developmental samples retain broadly similar neurite geometry while chemical connectivity changes.

nodes.name: Dentate chromatin accessibility one hour after ECS
nodes.shortDescription: One hour after ECS, bulk dentate ATAC-seq identified gained-open and gained-closed regions relative to sham. Supplementary Table 4 lists 11,438 gained-open and 1,739 gained-closed regions under the publication analysis; these are genomic region counts, not neuron counts.

nodes.name: Shared dentate accessibility regions through 24 hours
nodes.shortDescription: Across independent post-ECS cohorts, the published region lists retain 4,175 early gained-open and 484 gained-closed regions at four hours, and 597/22 respectively across one, four and 24 hours. The shared genomic regions define a sampled window; most early changes are not retained through every sampled timepoint.

nodes.name: Association between accessibility and RNA changes
nodes.shortDescription: Genomic annotations link activity-associated opening preferentially to upregulated genes and closing to downregulated genes. Overlap across bulk assays is an association; it does not demonstrate a unique enhancer-to-transcript causal relation in the same cell.

nodes.name: ECS or sham with dentate sampling
nodes.shortDescription: One-second ECS or identically handled sham in adult male mice; separate bulk dentate-gyrus cohorts sampled at baseline and one, four or 24 hours. RNA and ATAC assays use independent samples.

nodes.name: Dentate RNA abundance one hour after ECS
nodes.shortDescription: Independent dentate RNA-seq samples showed increased and decreased transcript abundance one hour after ECS relative to sham. This is an RNA-abundance response, not a direct measurement of transcription rate, protein production or learning.

nodes.name: Distributed empathy architecture hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Decety and Jackson propose interacting shared representations, self-other awareness, perspective flexibility and emotion regulation. These components supply a hypothesis for dissociable functions in empathy, without establishing a single necessary circuit.

nodes.name: Empathy outcome and instrument identity
nodes.shortDescription: Emotion recognition, perspective taking, self-reported affect, autonomic response, interpersonal accuracy and helping are distinct observables. An empathy measure must identify its instrument and version; the author-described thirty-item BEES is distinct from the earlier 1972 scale.

nodes.name: Empathy with self-other distinction
nodes.shortDescription: In Decety and Jackson's account, empathy involves an affective experience related to another person's state while distinguishing whose experience it is. This definition separates empathic experience from undifferentiated emotional contagion and from helping behavior.

nodes.name: Accessibility shared across sampled memory phases
nodes.shortDescription: Pooled ATAC-seq profiles showed early accessibility differences and a subset of gained regions shared with Late and Reactivated samples five days later. Shared genomic regions across selected cohorts support persistence at the population-profile level, not continuous opening in the same cell or an inherited memory state.

nodes.name: Chromatin priming as a memory mechanism
nodes.shortDescription: Early accessibility followed by altered contact and RNA profiles motivates a chromatin-priming model of later recall responses. These cross-sectional associations do not establish that enhancer opening or a specific loop is necessary for memory, nor that the measured stages form a unique causal chain.

nodes.name: Inferred chromatin compartments after conditioning
nodes.shortDescription: Hi-C profiles in Basal, Early and Late populations supported population-level A/B compartment assignments and changes for some genomic segments. These profiles summarize contact frequencies; they do not measure unique spatial coordinates or include a Reactivated whole-genome Hi-C cohort.

nodes.name: Context-dependent Arc/eYFP co-label counts
nodes.shortDescription: Five days after conditioning, exposure to the changed environment B yielded fewer Arc+/eYFP+ labeled cells per DG slice than re-exposure to training environment A. This is an effect of the environmental comparison on a marker readout, not a selective intervention establishing that the labeled cells cause memory.

nodes.name: Freezing under same or changed context
nodes.shortDescription: The changed-context A-B group showed less freezing than the A-A group in the five-day re-exposure assay. Freezing is a behavioral readout under a multi-cue protocol; its covariance with neuronal labels does not establish a molecular mediator.

nodes.name: Five-day same or changed context re-exposure
nodes.shortDescription: After tone/footshock conditioning in environment A, mice encounter A again or a changed environment B five days later. Several environmental cues change. Figure 1f marker counts and Extended Data 1e freezing are separate assays with unresolved animal/section accounting.

nodes.name: No detected context difference in persistent eYFP counts
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 1f reports no significant A-A versus A-B difference in the Activated-late eYFP+ cell count, although Arc/eYFP co-label counts differed. This null constrains the interpretation of the labeling assay; it does not establish equivalent ensembles or equal memory.

nodes.name: eIF4E protein puncta in labeled neurite shafts
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 5f reports more eIF4E-positive puncta per shaft length in Reactivated than Early or Late samples. This is protein immunoreactivity in the source-defined shaft region, not a direct translation-rate measurement; axonal versus dendritic source labels require reconciliation.

nodes.name: No detected eIF4E soma-puncta difference
nodes.shortDescription: The soma eIF4E puncta comparison in Figure 5f was nonsignificant across Early, Late and Reactivated populations. The shaft finding cannot be extended to all cellular compartments, and the soma null is not evidence of equivalence.

nodes.name: GRIA1 protein puncta in labeled neurite shafts
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 5g reports more GRIA1-positive puncta per shaft length in Reactivated than Early or Late samples. The immunostaining assay does not measure AMPA receptor current, new protein synthesis or synaptic efficacy.

nodes.name: No detected H3K4me1 difference at enhancers 1 and 2
nodes.shortDescription: The H3K4me1 comparisons at selected putative enhancers 1 and 2 were nonsignificant across the four populations. This does not generalize to enhancers 3 and 4, which showed different outcomes, or prove the mark functionally irrelevant.

nodes.name: H3K27ac at selected putative enhancers
nodes.shortDescription: ChIP-qPCR at putative enhancer 1 reported higher H3K27ac signal in Late and Reactivated populations than Basal; enhancer 2 showed a significant Late contrast. These selected-locus histone measurements are distinct from accessibility, contact frequency and enhancer necessity.

nodes.name: Marker-defined hippocampal sampling populations
nodes.shortDescription: The molecular comparison sorts post-training Basal NeuN+/eYFP- and Early NeuN+/eYFP+ nuclei, tagged Late nuclei five days later without recall, and NeuN+/eYFP+/Arc+ nuclei after recall in another cohort. Basal is a post-training label-negative population, not an untrained control.

nodes.name: Nuclear RNA differences among tagged populations
nodes.shortDescription: Pairwise nuclear RNA analysis reported differences among the selected populations, including 88 listed Basal/Early genes. Early transcription was therefore not universally unchanged. Table 8 contains unresolved contrast-direction conventions; no signed gene-specific relation is assigned from those cells.

nodes.name: Promoter-capture contact profiles across four populations
nodes.shortDescription: Promoter-capture Hi-C identified population-associated contact sets and stronger reported interaction scores in Reactivated samples. This targeted assay covers selected promoters in four populations; a threshold-defined unique contact is not proof that a physical contact is absent from every other cell.

nodes.name: Non-pattern-completion recruitment null
nodes.shortDescription: Stimulation of non-pattern-completion Go cells did not produce the reported improvement in ensemble recruitment or reliability seen with selected pattern-completion cells.

nodes.name: Nonselective V1 ensemble disruption protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Holographic activation of 6-13 nonselective cells during the normal-contrast Go stimulus; sizes chosen to compare similarly sized ensembles, not as a universal carrier count.

nodes.name: Behavior during ensemble disruption
nodes.shortDescription: Activation of nonselective cells during the normal-contrast Go stimulus disrupts the measured Go ensemble and reduces task performance.

nodes.name: Universal functional-assembly hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A calcium-defined task ensemble or a modularity partition does not establish one universal, anatomically fixed minimum unit for neural function.

nodes.name: Behavior conditional on rare gray-screen recall
nodes.shortDescription: In the gray-screen condition, successful ensemble recall occurred in about 5% of stimulation trials; the reported behavioral comparison separates this successful subset from partial recall.

nodes.name: Perceptual-state interpretation of recalled ensembles
nodes.shortDescription: An induced learned licking response does not uniquely identify subjective perception or the recurrent synaptic mechanism proposed for an assembly.

nodes.name: Selected-cell V1 ensemble recall protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Holographic activation of selected pattern-completion neurons during low-contrast Go stimulation; CRF-based target selection is statistical and condition-specific.

nodes.name: Behavior during selected ensemble recall
nodes.shortDescription: Activation of selected pattern-completion cells during low-contrast Go stimulation increases ensemble reliability and hit-minus-false-choice task performance.

nodes.name: External force during unseen-hand movement
nodes.shortDescription: Planar constrained hand movement without arm vision, randomized null/assistive/resistive force and subsequent trackball localization; GAM accounts for final position.

nodes.name: Calcium dynamics under probabilistic feedback
nodes.shortDescription: After closed loop was replaced by probabilistic swim-triggered visual feedback, mean radial astrocyte calcium rose faster with less reliable feedback. This readout supports temporal integration without identifying a unique algorithm.

nodes.name: Reaching practice in an imposed force field
nodes.shortDescription: Robot-generated force field during reaching; practice and subsequent field removal, as described in the abstract.

nodes.name: Removal of a practiced reaching force field
nodes.shortDescription: Robot-generated force field during reaching; practice and subsequent field removal, as described in the abstract.

nodes.name: Relative engulfment after retinal forskolin
nodes.shortDescription: Microglia contained more labeled input from the vehicle eye than from the forskolin-treated eye. The measured comparison concerns relative input engulfment within the sampled dLGN, not all neural activity or all glial cells.

nodes.name: Retinal forskolin in the engulfment assay
nodes.shortDescription: P4 CX3CR1/EGFP mice: 10 mM forskolin in the left eye and DMSO vehicle in the right, followed 4-5 h later by CTB tracing; engulfment analyzed at P5.

nodes.name: Foster-care effect on GR promoter CpG site 16
nodes.shortDescription: After cross-fostering within 12 hours of birth, adult hippocampal bisulfite readouts at the 5-prime NGFI-A-site CpG (site 16) followed foster-mother care class. The comparison supports a postnatal environmental contribution rather than an effect fixed solely by biological-mother class.

nodes.name: No detected cross-fostering effect at CpG site 17
nodes.shortDescription: The reported cross-fostering effect at CpG site 16 was not detected at neighboring site 17. This constrains the locus-specific interpretation and does not prove site 17 is functionally irrelevant.

nodes.name: Fast-spiking cell activation
nodes.shortDescription: Cell-specific optogenetic manipulation in barrel cortex; LFP and unit recordings; anesthetic state not verified.

nodes.name: Sensory input phase intervention
nodes.shortDescription: Vary whisker-stimulus phase relative to induced gamma in the Cardin 2009 assay.

nodes.name: Induced barrel-cortex gamma response
nodes.shortDescription: Optogenetic activation of fast-spiking cells selectively amplifies local gamma in the reported barrel-cortex preparation.

nodes.name: Geometric comparison noise estimates
nodes.shortDescription: The supplement reports split-half participant correlations of 0.99 and 0.90 for the quadrilateral and shape-memory group readouts, respectively, and leave-one-subject-out correlations of 0.77 and 0.41. Group-to-group agreement and individual-to-group agreement have different statistical targets.

nodes.name: Cross-format model ranks
nodes.shortDescription: Across 144 directed image-matching queries, the lowest of 43 deposited selected-model mean ranks is DINOv3-large layer 25 at 2.215278. DINOv3-base layer 13 gives 2.368056. These model identities and ranks are independently reproduced; the main text names base for its approximately 2.2 result.

nodes.name: Inverse-distance distraction readout
nodes.shortDescription: For one target and five distractors, the specified readout is the sum of the five inverse target-to-distractor embedding distances. Averaging this quantity across the task trials gives a target-level predictor of choice time.

nodes.name: Ideal object-identity benchmark
nodes.shortDescription: A theoretical cross-format identity benchmark assigns the correct object rank one for every query. Its mean rank one is a stipulated target, not an observed human matching score or a neural measurement.

nodes.name: Quadrilateral model dissimilarity
nodes.shortDescription: For 55 unordered quadrilateral pairs, the deposited average-pair-distance branch gives a best selected correlation of 0.888717 for convnext_xxlarge.clip_laion2b_soup, layer 3, against the group behavioral matrix. The stored symbolic matrix gives r=0.667960. In this branch 21 of 45 models have a last-layer optimum, agreeing with the paper rounded 47 percent.

nodes.name: Conditional quadrilateral symbolic coefficient
nodes.shortDescription: Using the average-pair-distance DINOv3-huge layer 29, CORnet layer 3 and symbolic vectors, the independently recomputed standardized-predictor OLS coefficients are 0.107164, -0.020177 and 0.005080, with R squared 0.729055. The paper reports P<1e-8, P=0.042 and P=0.726 respectively, matching the independent numerical calculation.

nodes.name: Shape-memory description and visual fits
nodes.shortDescription: Across 68 target means after grey-level response residualization, assigned description cost correlates with choice time at r=0.432428. DINOv3-small layer 13 inverse-distance readout gives r=0.544201. With eight response controls, the independently recomputed cost correlation is 0.302867; the best selected neural readout is DINOv3-base at r=0.415755.

nodes.name: Joint visual and description fit
nodes.shortDescription: For the same DINOv3-small layer 13, combining inverse-distance readout with description cost gives a fitted multiple correlation of 0.707675, compared with 0.544201 for that layer alone. For CLIP giant layer 24 the corresponding values are 0.671963 and 0.511333; the deposited joint value 0.589392 instead comes from its last layer 39.

nodes.name: Associations with model training factors
nodes.shortDescription: The publication associates performance most strongly with training dataset size in the first two tasks, while training method is the dominant reported factor for cross-format ranks. Architecture, training method, dataset and parameter count are compared across available pretrained configurations.

nodes.name: Glial evidence-accumulation mechanism
nodes.shortDescription: A unique glial evidence-accumulation mechanism and its generalization beyond the tested larval fish remain hypotheses; measured calcium dynamics and behavioral effects constrain but do not determine the algorithm.

nodes.name: Universal global neuromodulation hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Named LC perturbations do not establish one transmitter-independent global control property with invariant anatomy.

nodes.name: Glutamatergic astrocyte transcript signatures
nodes.shortDescription: Transcriptomic analysis identified a mouse astrocyte cluster expressing glutamatergic machinery, with related signatures in human datasets. Transcript-label transfer does not establish human glutamate release or behavioral function.

nodes.name: Global neuronal workspace interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: The GNWT conscious-access interpretation and its biological predictions require an explicit theory version and measurement mapping; the status of offset and maintenance assumptions is disputed.

nodes.name: Global workspace conceptual architecture
nodes.shortDescription: Baars' global-workspace diagram is a conceptual information-processing architecture, not an observed anatomical graph or a demonstrated generator of consciousness.

nodes.name: Force-dependent hand-localization errors
nodes.shortDescription: Assistive and resistive forces change hand-localization bias differently; the study reports no significant corresponding variance difference.

nodes.name: Hcrt-R1 blockade before Hcrt-cell stimulation
nodes.shortDescription: SB334867 pretreatment, 45 minutes before recording and 20-Hz stimulation; systemic administration with vehicle and mCherry controls. This does not isolate receptor location.

nodes.name: Wake-latency response with Hcrt-R1 blockade
nodes.shortDescription: Systemic Hcrt-R1 antagonist pretreatment reduced the 20-Hz stimulation-related shortening of post-stimulation wake latency in the reported comparison.

nodes.name: Post-stimulation sleep-to-wake latency
nodes.shortDescription: Hcrt-neuron photostimulation with specified trains shortens post-stimulation wake latency from SWS and REM relative to control mice; the distribution shifts rather than fixing the transition time.

nodes.name: Repeated-Hcrt-stimulation state-duration null
nodes.shortDescription: Repeated Hcrt stimulation increased SWS-to-wake transitions without a detected change in total wake, SWS or REM time in the reported hour-long assay.

nodes.name: Low-frequency wake-latency null
