nodes.shortDescription: The 1-Hz Hcrt-neuron stimulation condition showed no detected sleep-to-wake latency change against its controls.

nodes.name: Hcrt-neuron photostimulation during sleep
nodes.shortDescription: Ten-second unilateral trains after 15 seconds of stable sleep during 12:00-18:00; SWS 5-30 Hz and REM 5-20 Hz reported comparisons, 15-ms pulses, with mCherry controls.

nodes.name: Visual-haptic height judgments
nodes.shortDescription: Changing visual reliability shifts combined height judgments; observed cue weights and thresholds resemble the declared maximum-likelihood predictions.

nodes.name: Action-response differentiation as an agency hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Mukamel et al. propose that some observation/execution responses may contribute to motor suppression and distinguishing actions performed by self and others. The recordings supply candidate response patterns rather than a measured agency mechanism.

nodes.name: Human observation and execution matching units
nodes.shortDescription: The human recording study reports 90 matching units across eight sampled regions. Its detailed four-region subset comprises 18 hippocampal, 14 entorhinal, 19 parahippocampal and 17 SMA units: 68 in total, with 40 single and 28 multiunit recordings. Within that subset, Table S2 classifies 14 units as broadly congruent and 54 as matching without its additional effector-selectivity criterion.

nodes.name: Regional action-matching reference comparisons
nodes.shortDescription: The authors report matching-unit counts above their shuffled reference in hippocampus, entorhinal cortex, parahippocampal gyrus and SMA, including a single-unit analysis. Amygdala, pre-SMA, dorsal ACC and rostral ACC do not exceed that reference under the reported analysis.

nodes.name: Human matching excitation and inhibition profiles
nodes.shortDescription: Within the 68-unit subset, the paper describes 33 units with excitation in both matched conditions, 21 with inhibition in both and 14 with opposite response directions. Population excitation and inhibition plots combine 41 and 26 matched-action responses respectively, from 33 and 21 units.

nodes.name: Human regional BrdU density profile
nodes.shortDescription: BrdU-positive densities varied across sampled SGZ, granule-layer and hilar sections from five patients. Each patient supplied a different labeling interval. The profile does not identify a longitudinal death rate, a causal age effect or total neuronal production.

nodes.name: Human adult-born neuron function hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Adult-born human cells could become functional circuit members, but BrdU histology and radiocarbon dating in different autopsy series do not test electrical integration or cognitive contribution. Matched human functional measurements and selective mediation remain necessary for a birth-to-memory mechanism.

nodes.name: Human dentate BrdU and neuronal markers
nodes.shortDescription: In the five labeled patients, sampled dentate BrdU-positive cells included neuronal-marker-positive cells. Reported GCL fractions were 22.0% NeuN, 22.7% NSE and 7.9% calbindin, each relative to BrdU-positive cells in its assay. These are marker-associated observations, not neuron birth rates or measured functional integration.

nodes.name: Human BrdU staining controls
nodes.shortDescription: No BrdU-reactive profiles were detected in the uninfused control. Confocal optical sections, separate wavelengths and brightfield staining supported the reported dentate colocalization. These controls address detection specificity; they do not make the control patient a demonstrated neurogenesis-negative individual.

nodes.name: Human subventricular BrdU marker profile
nodes.shortDescription: The reported subventricular samples contained BrdU-positive cells without detectable NeuN or GFAP colabeling. This region-specific marker result does not establish their neuronal fate, actual migration or absence of neurogenesis elsewhere.

nodes.name: Human molecular-label abundance comparisons
nodes.shortDescription: The reported normalized-count analysis finds more NSC-labeled nuclei in PCI and AD than HA, and fewer neuroblast and immature-neuron labels in AD than HA. Immature-neuron labels are higher in SA than HA and AD. These are observational, sample-normalized comparisons with an unresolved cohort denominator, not rates of neuron production.

nodes.name: Human candidate neurogenic cell profiles
nodes.shortDescription: Reference-assisted RNA and chromatin analysis identified candidate neural stem, neuroblast and immature-neuron populations with inferred trajectories. Molecular labels and latent time support an interpretation of cell state; they do not directly observe cell birth, lineage progression or electrical integration.

nodes.name: Human cohort and analysis census
nodes.shortDescription: The original cohort sheets and abundance metadata contain 39 sample IDs, including nine healthy agers, while the main text reports 38 participants including eight healthy agers. Table 8 contains 153530 retained nuclei across those 39 samples. Sample identity and the relation to 355997 sequenced nuclei require a complete manifest.

nodes.name: SuperAger comparison-specific nulls
nodes.shortDescription: For immature-neuron labels, the reported SA/YA and SA/PCI comparisons do not meet adjusted P < 0.05 (approximately 0.066 and 0.055). Significant SA/HA and SA/AD comparisons therefore do not support a claim covering every reference group; these nonsignificant results are not equivalence findings.

nodes.name: Human hippocampal neuronal DNA radiocarbon
nodes.shortDescription: NeuN-positive hippocampal nuclear fractions show genomic-DNA carbon-14 profiles consistent with postnatal DNA synthesis, including bomb-derived carbon in older subjects. Under the stated DNA-stability and progenitor assumptions this supports postnatal neuron production; bulk dating does not identify the birth or function of each cell.

nodes.name: Human hippocampal nonneuronal DNA radiocarbon
nodes.shortDescription: NeuN-negative hippocampal fractions show radiocarbon profiles consistent with postnatal DNA synthesis. The mixed marker-negative population cannot supply a turnover rate for a particular glial, immune or vascular cell type, and isotope differences do not establish a neural regulatory intervention.

nodes.name: Human hippocampal two-population renewal model
nodes.shortDescription: Scenario 2POP represents a renewing subset alongside a nonrenewing subset. Its human neuronal fraction near 0.35 and individual median renewal of 1.75% per year are conditional fitted summaries. Sample exclusions, the distinction between individual and global estimates, and unresolved model-selection reporting prevent a unique biological renewal law or universal graph parameter.

nodes.name: Human hippocampal age-dependent survival model
nodes.shortDescription: Scenario 2POPEd illustrates age-dependent death within a renewing population and loss from a nonrenewing population, combined with external anatomical counts. Its fitted survival schedule and Figure 6 age distribution are candidate reconstructions, not observed single-cell lifetimes, demonstrated replacement of function or an emergent population-control mechanism.

nodes.name: Information-integration hypothesis (2004)
nodes.shortDescription: The 2004 information-integration proposal remains a version-specific theoretical interpretation; neither the historical thresholds nor a measured Phi value follow from the selected experiments.

nodes.name: A1 agonist with D1 challenge after Il34 deletion
nodes.shortDescription: Il34 flox/Drd1a-Cre preparation challenged with 5 mg/kg SKF81297 plus 0.1 mg/kg CPA; compare separate D1-only and co-treated cohorts.

nodes.name: A1 agonist rescue in the Il34-deletion preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 4m source counts show no seizures in 10 co-treated Il34-deletion mice or 11 co-treated controls, versus 8/9 and 2/11 in their respective D1-only cohorts. The caption and workbook give inconsistent co-treatment sample counts; the stated counts are the workbook values.

nodes.name: D1 challenge after D1-neuron Il34 deletion
nodes.shortDescription: Developmental Il34 flox/Drd1a-Cre versus controls, with reduced striatal microglia and 5 mg/kg SKF81297 challenge.

nodes.name: D1-challenge seizure incidence after Il34 deletion
nodes.shortDescription: The Figure 4m D1-only cohort had seizures in 8/9 Il34 flox/Drd1a-Cre mice versus 2/11 controls. Neuronal ligand deletion with reduced microglia is not a direct, acute microglial ablation.

nodes.name: Challenge-specific nulls after striatal Il34 deletion
nodes.shortDescription: The Il34/Drd1a-Cre and Il34/Drd2-Cre comparisons did not show a significant genotype difference in seizure incidence after 18 mg/kg kainic acid or 1 mg/kg picrotoxin (Figure 2k and Extended Data Figure 4h). These assays differ from D1 challenge and from brain-wide PLX5622 depletion.

nodes.name: Transcript-defined cNST cell clusters
nodes.shortDescription: The cNST atlas and mapped LPS-TRAPed cells identify transcript-defined clusters, including Dbh-enriched excitatory groups. The atlas pools tissue from five animals; its UMAP layout is not anatomical geometry or a uniquely inferred causal network.

nodes.name: LPS-TRAP2 and FOS co-labels
nodes.shortDescription: More than 80% of the sampled LPS-TRAPed cNST neurons were FOS-positive on a later LPS challenge in the reported four-mouse comparison. Marker co-labeling validates sampled targeting; it does not prove exact identity with the Dbh-cre population.

nodes.name: Exploration during BLA projection inhibition
nodes.shortDescription: Selective BLA-to-CeA terminal inhibition reduces open-arm and center exploration in a separate low-stress cohort.

nodes.name: Injected cytokines in nodose imaging
nodes.shortDescription: Vagal GCaMP6s imaging with saline and 100 micrograms/kg cytokine injections in five-minute trials; 423 cells from five mice in Figure 4a.

nodes.name: Nodose calcium after injected cytokines
nodes.shortDescription: Intraperitoneal TNF or IL-1beta and IL-10 evoked calcium responses in different observed nodose neurons during the short recording trials. The response classifier and sampled cells define the claim; direct neuronal cytokine-receptor binding is not established.

nodes.name: Unique internal state-estimator hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A tuned state estimator can explain the reported localization pattern; its unique biological implementation and necessity remain unresolved.

nodes.name: Hippocampal irradiation and DCX depletion
nodes.shortDescription: The separately irradiated Bax-floxed cohort had fewer dentate DCX-positive cells than sham controls: reported means 144 versus 3120, three mice per group. This regional intervention does not selectively isolate newborn-neuron function or by itself prove cognitive necessity.

nodes.name: Hippocampal irradiation and DCX depletion assay
nodes.shortDescription: Separate ten-week-old Bax-floxed mice; hippocampal-field irradiation with three 5 Gy exposures on days 1, 4 and 8 versus sham, followed by terminal DCX counting.

nodes.name: Irradiation discrimination limits
nodes.shortDescription: The irradiated-versus-sham discrimination-ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3, despite late within-group differences and a conflicting day-five F/P pair. This mixed evidence does not establish newborn-neuron necessity from the reported overall between-group test.

nodes.name: Capillary endothelial Kir2.1 current
nodes.shortDescription: Constitutive Tek-Cre Kcnj2 deletion removed the measured barium-sensitive inward-rectifier current in isolated capillary endothelial cells relative to wild type. The record identifies Kir2.1, not a general glial potassium-uptake process.

nodes.name: Preparation-specific capillary potassium series
nodes.shortDescription: The ex vivo 6-10 mM potassium series shows an apparent onset between 6 and 7 mM under the tested conditions. Sample-count and degrees-of-freedom discrepancies prevent precise calibration; the series is not a universal minimal carrier rule.

nodes.name: Selected LFP-band nulls under barium
nodes.shortDescription: Surface barium did not significantly alter the reported peak frequency or amplitude in selected whisker-evoked LFP bands. These measures do not establish complete neural equivalence or selective endothelial pharmacology.

nodes.name: Kcnj2 genotype and cEC patch clamp
nodes.shortDescription: Whole-cell voltage ramps in 60 mM external potassium; eight wild-type cells from eight mice and seven knockout cells from seven mice; 100 micromolar barium subtraction.

nodes.name: No detected capillary SK/IK activation
nodes.shortDescription: Under the specified NS309 and intracellular-calcium protocols, sampled capillary endothelial cells lacked the SK/IK-like currents observed in pial endothelial controls. This does not establish universal absence of calcium-sensitive channels.

nodes.name: Pial smooth-muscle current null
nodes.shortDescription: Pial smooth-muscle inward-rectifier current density did not differ significantly between wild-type and endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 knockout groups in the reported assay. Cells are nested within three and four mice; the result is not proof of complete vascular equivalence.

nodes.name: Relative perfusion after surface potassium
nodes.shortDescription: Cortical 15 mM potassium increased relative perfusion, with a smaller response after endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 deletion. Surface barium further reduced responses; this cortical exposure is distinct from focal capillary injection.

nodes.name: Whisker perfusion response after Kcnj2 deletion
nodes.shortDescription: Whisker stimulation evoked a smaller relative cortical perfusion response after endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 deletion, with residual responses present. Barium reduced responses further and is not restricted to capillary endothelium.

nodes.name: Whisker stimulation and Kcnj2 flow comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Anesthetized somatosensory laser Doppler; contralateral whiskers approximately 4 Hz for sixty seconds; seven wild-type and six knockout mice, with subsequent surface barium.

nodes.name: Early field potentiation after Kir4.1 deletion
nodes.shortDescription: Posttetanic potentiation over 0-2 min and short-term potentiation over 0-15 min were greater in Kir4.1 cKO slices than controls. The study does not uniquely assign this effect to potassium handling rather than glutamate handling or developmental changes.

nodes.name: Glutamate-transporter current
nodes.shortDescription: Kir4.1 cKO passive astrocytes had smaller TBOA-sensitive inward-current magnitudes in the presence of Ba2+ than controls. The developmental intervention and subtraction assay do not isolate a unique molecular mechanism of clearance.

nodes.name: Late potentiation and basal transmission controls
nodes.shortDescription: The P20-25 field assay reported no significant genotype difference in basal input-output responses, paired-pulse facilitation or late potentiation measured 30-45 min after the train. Early potentiation findings cannot be generalized to these endpoints.

nodes.name: Potassium-associated uptake current
nodes.shortDescription: Kir4.1 cKO passive astrocytes had smaller Ba2+-sensitive inward-current magnitudes during the stated Schaffer stimulation protocol than controls. This is an electrical uptake proxy, not a direct extracellular potassium measurement.

nodes.name: Kir4.1 deletion in the field assay
nodes.shortDescription: P20-25 hippocampal slices at 30 C; developmental Kir4.1 cKO versus controls; field recording before and after a single 1 s, 100 Hz train.

nodes.name: Kir4.1 deletion in the uptake assay
nodes.shortDescription: Developmental hGFAP/gfa2-Cre Kir4.1 cKO versus controls; P15-20 CA1 passive astrocytes at -90 mV, five Schaffer collateral pulses at 50 Hz, with sequential Ba2+ and TBOA subtraction.

nodes.name: LC inhibition during the active period
nodes.shortDescription: Continuous bilateral eNpHR illumination for one hour during the dark period; eYFP and baseline comparisons.

nodes.name: LC-evoked sleep-to-wake response
nodes.shortDescription: Brief bilateral LC photostimulation promotes EEG/EMG-defined sleep-to-wake transitions in the inactive-period assay.

nodes.name: Brief LC activation during sleep
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral ChR2 stimulation: 10 ms pulses, 5 Hz for 5 s, starting 15 s after a stable NREM or REM event; inactive period.

nodes.name: No detected inactive-period sleep-duration effect
nodes.shortDescription: Hour-long LC photoinhibition produced no detected difference in total sleep/wake durations during the inactive-period comparison.

nodes.name: Wake duration during LC inhibition
nodes.shortDescription: Hour-long LC photoinhibition reduces active-period wakefulness and wake-episode duration while leaving sleep-to-wake transitions possible.

nodes.name: Cue training retained-label null
nodes.shortDescription: Visible-platform cue training did not produce the reported place-training increase in dentate BrdU labels relative to naive controls. The null concerns this task and labeling window, without establishing biological equivalence or a universal learning classification.

nodes.name: Delay conditioning retained-label null
nodes.shortDescription: Delay-paired and unpaired conditions showed no detected dentate BrdU-count increase relative to naive controls at the reported endpoint. This protocol changes stimulus durations and response scoring as well as the trace gap; its null does not establish that all hippocampal activity or learning lacks an effect.

nodes.name: Late-labeling trace-conditioning null
nodes.shortDescription: When BrdU was given on the final training day after learning criterion, the dentate labeled-cell count 24 hours later did not differ detectably among trace-paired, unpaired and naive groups. This window-specific null does not exclude all effects on cell proliferation during training.

nodes.name: Post-training BrdU marker profiles
nodes.shortDescription: The later endpoint reports approximately 57% TOAD-64, 11% GFAP and 71% calbindin colabeling among BrdU-positive cells, with no detected between-group differences in these proportions. These are separate overlapping marker assays, not disjoint fractions or a measured synaptic integration rate.

nodes.name: Place training with pretraining BrdU labeling
nodes.shortDescription: Adult male rats labeled one week earlier performed four days of fixed submerged-platform training, changing visible-platform cue training or time-yoked swimming without a platform, alongside naive controls. Separate terminal cohorts were examined 24 hours or seven days later.

nodes.name: Place training and subgranular pyknosis
nodes.shortDescription: The place-trained group had fewer morphologically pyknotic subgranular profiles than naive, cue and time-yoked swimming groups. Counts of all degenerating profiles do not establish survival of individually tracked newborn neurons, and the exact terminal cohort for this paragraph is unresolved.

nodes.name: Place training and retained dentate labels
nodes.shortDescription: At 24 hours after training, the place group had more dentate BrdU-labeled cells than naive, cue and time-yoked swimming groups, with six animals per group. This is an effect of the specified training comparison on previously labeled cells; a unique survival mechanism was not isolated.

nodes.name: Seven-day post-training retained-label observations
nodes.shortDescription: The text reports elevated dentate BrdU counts seven days after trace and place training in separate terminal cohorts. It supplies no separate numerical endpoint table or figure for this claim. Persistence of a group difference is not continuous tracking of individual labeled neurons.

nodes.name: Learning-related survival mechanism
nodes.shortDescription: Enhanced survival is proposed to explain increased pretraining labels, reduced total pyknosis and a late-labeling null. These converging observations constrain the interpretation but do not exclude proliferation, label kinetics or alternate mediators, identify a unique sensitive period, or prove newborn-cell necessity for memory.

nodes.name: Sampled SVZ retained-label null
nodes.shortDescription: The sampled SVZ counts showed no reported training effect in either trace or maze comparisons. Sampling excludes the anterior SVZ. The trace F/P pair is inconsistent in the printed paper, so neither exact numerical reproduction nor a whole-SVZ absence claim is supported.

nodes.name: Time-yoked swimming retained-label null
nodes.shortDescription: Rats swimming for the place-group duration without a platform had no detected dentate BrdU-count difference from naive controls. Matching swim time does not match all psychological or endocrine exposures and does not establish that stress never changes neuronal survival.

nodes.name: Trace conditioning with pretraining BrdU labeling
nodes.shortDescription: Adult male rats received BrdU one week before four days of trace eyeblink conditioning, explicitly unpaired stimulation or naive control conditions. Separate cohorts were collected 24 hours or seven days after training. The protocol includes stimulus timing, electrode preparation and conditioned-response measurement.

nodes.name: Trace conditioning and subgranular pyknosis
nodes.shortDescription: The trace-paired group had fewer morphologically pyknotic subgranular profiles than naive and unpaired groups. These are total degenerating profiles, not an identified newborn-neuron survival fraction. The printed ANOVA degrees of freedom and terminal-cohort allocation remain unresolved.

nodes.name: Trace conditioning and retained dentate labels
nodes.shortDescription: At 24 hours after four training days, trace-paired rats had more dentate BrdU-labeled cells than unpaired and naive controls, with six animals per group. BrdU preceded training by one week. The measured endpoint is retained labeled cells, not a separately identified increase in division rate.

nodes.name: Granule-cell-layer volume null
nodes.shortDescription: No group difference was detected in granule-cell-layer volume in the trace or maze comparison. This regional volume null is separate from retained BrdU counts and cannot establish a preserved neuron population, replacement mechanism or statistical equivalence.

nodes.name: LIP-sensitive spatial free-choice response
nodes.shortDescription: LIP silencing shifts free choices away from contralateral targets and increases contralateral saccade endpoint error in the control task.

nodes.name: Mapped LIP suppression in the Jeurissen motion task
nodes.shortDescription: Functionally mapped unilateral LIP muscimol in motion-task monkeys; trial- and session-resolved choices with sustained electrophysiological silencing.

nodes.name: LIP inactivation in the Katz protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Verified MT or LIP muscimol silencing; fixed-duration motion followed by delayed saccade; spatial free-choice control.

nodes.name: LIP microstimulation during motion choice
nodes.shortDescription: Response-field-selected LIPv clusters; electrical stimulation on random half of reaction-time motion trials; single-target delayed-saccade controls.

nodes.name: No detected motion-choice effect in the Katz LIP assay
nodes.shortDescription: Verified LIP silencing produced no detectable motion sensitivity or choice-bias change under the reported task and observation window.

nodes.name: Bulk cNST calcium after peripheral LPS
nodes.shortDescription: The main 0.5 mg/kg LPS challenge increased bulk Vglut2-cre cNST calcium-response area relative to the preceding saline session. Fixed session order and a population fluorescence measurement limit causal and cellular interpretation.

nodes.name: cNST FOS after peripheral LPS
nodes.shortDescription: Peripheral LPS produced more cNST FOS-positive neurons than saline at two hours in the specified counting region. The marker response does not establish DBH-specific firing or identify the peripheral mediator.

nodes.name: Peripheral LPS for FOS histology
nodes.shortDescription: Intraperitoneal LPS at 50 micrograms/kg versus saline; five mice per condition and a matched cNST counting region two hours later.

nodes.name: Sequential saline and LPS photometry
nodes.shortDescription: Awake Vglut2-cre mice with cNST GCaMP6s; saline on day four and LPS on day five, six mice in the main comparison.

nodes.name: Adult macaque BrdU and neuronal marker colabels
nodes.shortDescription: At 32 days after five daily injections, BrdU-positive cells colabel with NeuN or TuJ1 in the dentate GCL and SGZ. Confocal marker combinations and cellular morphology support adult neuronal production under the birth-label assumptions; electrical integration, migration paths and cognitive contribution were not measured.

nodes.name: Adult macaque BrdU and oligodendroglial marker colabels
nodes.shortDescription: BrdU-labeled nuclei with O4- or CNP-positive cytoplasm were reported in the adult macaque hilus and GCL, including 27-day single-injection examples. These marker-defined observations support oligodendroglial production; they do not measure myelin formation, conduction or a shared neuronal and glial ancestor.

nodes.name: Adult macaque hippocampal BrdU profiles
nodes.shortDescription: BrdU-positive nuclei occur in the dentate region of all ten injected adult macaques. Early observations include the hilus, molecular layer and SGZ; later observations additionally include the GCL. These are regional labeling observations in different sacrificed animals, not tracked migration or neuron-specific long-term survival.

nodes.name: Macaque birth-label staining controls
nodes.shortDescription: Switching fluorescence labels preserved the reported neuronal colabeling pattern; primary-antibody omission eliminated cell labeling, and an illustrated BrdU-positive, NeuN-negative cell addresses channel bleed-through. These controls concern the assay, without proving cell ancestry or biological absence of neurogenesis.

nodes.name: Shared macaque neural progenitor hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A common multipotent progenitor could generate neuronal and glial progeny near the adult SGZ. Spatially nearby phenotypes and astrocyte evidence from other studies do not distinguish that possibility from separate committed progenitors or demonstrate self-renewal.

nodes.name: Conditional macaque neuronal production estimate
nodes.shortDescription: A retained-profile extrapolation suggests roughly 1,000 BrdU/TuJ1-positive cells per hippocampus after five injections and 32 days of survival. The derived 0.004% per day depends on external anatomy, a total-neuron denominator and division by five; production and survival are not separately identified.

nodes.name: Adult macaque neuron migration hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Bipolar neuronal-marker-positive cells could migrate from the SGZ into the GCL, potentially using radial glial processes. Static morphology and regional labeling at different survival times do not establish trajectories, origin or a necessary guidance mechanism.

nodes.name: Adult macaque neuronal replacement hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Adult neuron production could replace existing neurons or add to the population. Separate anatomical counts motivate a balanced replacement interpretation, but this study does not measure matched births and deaths, state-dependent feedback, replacement identity or preservation of memory.

nodes.name: Adult macaque hippocampal PCNA profiles
nodes.shortDescription: PCNA-positive nuclei and occasional apposed pairs were reported in the hilus, molecular layer and SGZ of the same brains, but not the GCL proper. This separate assay supports local proliferative activity; it does not establish the neuronal fate or common ancestry of each labeled cell.

nodes.name: Chromatin mediation of maternal-care effects
nodes.shortDescription: A pathway connecting maternal care, GR-promoter chromatin, GR expression and endocrine feedback is a mechanistic proposal constrained by these experiments. The exact causal ordering and mediation among measured outcomes remain unresolved.

nodes.name: Cross-fostering between maternal-care classes
nodes.shortDescription: Long-Evans pups exchanged within 12 hours of birth; adult CpG assays compared cross-class and same-class foster groups. High:High and Low:Low controls were fostered to other mothers of the same class; Figure 1d reports five animals/group.

nodes.name: Maternal-care association with GR promoter ChIP signals
nodes.shortDescription: The publication reports greater acetyl-H3K9- and NGFI-A-associated GR promoter signals in high-care offspring. This observational contrast retains unresolved sample-size and t/P inconsistencies and supplies no independently reproduced effect size or confidence level.

nodes.name: Developmental profile of the maternal-care CpG contrast
nodes.shortDescription: Separate age cohorts showed a site-16 maternal-group contrast at postnatal days 6, 21 and 90, but not embryonic day 20 or postnatal day 1. These cross-sectional observations do not follow the same animal or cell through time.

nodes.name: Maternal-care association with GR promoter methylation
nodes.shortDescription: Adult high- and low-care offspring differed in bulk hippocampal bisulfite readouts at selected GR promoter CpGs, including NGFI-A-site CpG 16. The unmanipulated group contrast is an association and is distinct from the cross-fostering experiment.

nodes.name: Hippocampal MCT2 antisense
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral hippocampal MCT2 antisense versus scrambled ODN 1 h before inhibitory-avoidance training; long-term retention tested at 24 h and 7 days.

nodes.name: Lactate and glucose in the MCT2 rescue assay
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 6 and its Results report no rescue of the MCT2-ODN retention deficit by 100 nmol L-lactate or 50 nmol glucose. A conflicting Discussion sentence listing MCT2 among lactate-rescued knockdowns does not establish a positive rescue.

nodes.name: Retention after MCT2 knockdown
nodes.shortDescription: MCT2 antisense reduced inhibitory-avoidance retention latency at 24 h and 7 days relative to scrambled controls. This regional knockdown is not a cell-restricted neuronal intervention.

nodes.name: MCT2 acquisition and short-term retention
nodes.shortDescription: Acquisition and the separate 1 h retention assay showed no significant difference after MCT2 antisense versus scrambled controls. Nonsignificance is not proof of equivalence across every memory phase.

nodes.name: Hippocampal MCT4 antisense
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral hippocampal MCT4 antisense versus scrambled ODN 1 h before inhibitory-avoidance training; transporter knockdown checked in separate tissue samples.

nodes.name: Equicaloric glucose in the MCT4 rescue assay
nodes.shortDescription: The stated 50 nmol glucose condition did not rescue the MCT4-ODN retention deficit. This dose-specific null does not establish that glucose can never support memory or substitute under another protocol.

nodes.name: L-lactate with MCT4 knockdown
nodes.shortDescription: MCT4 antisense 1 h before training, followed by 100 nmol L-lactate 15 min before training; comparison with the MCT4-ODN plus vehicle condition.

nodes.name: Retention with MCT4 lactate rescue
nodes.shortDescription: L-lactate rescued the reported MCT4-ODN-associated retention deficit at the tested 24 h and 7 day endpoints. Rescue supports a lactate-related contribution without uniquely establishing an exclusive fuel pathway.

nodes.name: Retention after MCT4 knockdown
nodes.shortDescription: MCT4 antisense treatment reduced inhibitory-avoidance retention latency at 24 h and 7 days relative to scrambled controls. Acquisition latency was not significantly changed. The behavioral result does not directly measure astrocyte-to-neuron lactate flux.

nodes.name: Visual deprivation in the cell-count assay
nodes.shortDescription: C57BL/6 monocular eyelid closure approximately P15-P32; deprived and open-eye optic nerve/tract compared by CC1 immunostaining.

nodes.name: Compound action potentials after deprivation
nodes.shortDescription: Deprived optic nerves had lower CAP-derived conduction velocity and broader length-normalized CAP responses than paired controls. The experiment changes visual experience, not only myelin internode length.

nodes.name: Visual deprivation in the nerve assay
nodes.shortDescription: Isolated P32 optic nerves from deprived and control eyes after approximately P15-P32 eyelid closure; room-temperature suction-electrode recordings.

nodes.name: Visual deprivation in the internode assay
nodes.shortDescription: NG2-CreERT2/tau-mGFP mice deprived approximately P15-P32, tamoxifen at P19; labeled optic-nerve internodes traced between Caspr-positive ends at P32.

nodes.name: Internode lengths after deprivation
nodes.shortDescription: Myelin internodes generated during deprivation were reported shorter than open-eye controls. Text and caption disagree on the deprived median, so no exact median or quantitative geometry rule is assigned.

nodes.name: Oligodendrocyte counts after deprivation
nodes.shortDescription: The deprived optic nerve and tract had more CC1-positive mature oligodendrocytes than the respective controls. This endpoint does not establish increased total myelin thickness or a universally stabilizing glial property.

nodes.name: Deprivation paired-pulse control
nodes.shortDescription: The isolated-nerve paired-pulse assay did not show a significant difference in recovery from inactivation over the tested interstimulus intervals. This null does not identify internode length as the unique mediator of the CAP changes.

nodes.name: Deprivation ultrastructure controls
nodes.shortDescription: The P32 electron-microscopy assay reported no significant differences in myelinated-axon fraction, myelin thickness, axon-size distribution or density. Conflicting fraction labels in the text and caption preclude exact numerical reuse.

nodes.name: Constituent-opening anticipation null
nodes.shortDescription: The reported anticipation contrast between constituent-opening and internal items is nonsignificant. It is restricted to four-segments and two-squares after exclusions; two-rectangles is omitted because its anticipation score is not significant.

nodes.name: MEG spatial-location readout
nodes.shortDescription: A decoder trained on unpredictable localizer items and first items of primitive pairs identifies locations in the sequence task. Mean location-decoding performance has a reported association with empirical behavioral complexity, but its association with formal description cost is nonsignificant (one-tailed P=0.1).

nodes.name: Matched sequence primitive-decoding null
nodes.shortDescription: For the sequence task, the balanced rotation-versus-symmetry test using matched visual pairs does not exceed chance, despite positive 11-way transition-label decoding. The positive matched-pair result from the separate primitive task cannot be assigned to this sequence contrast.

nodes.name: MEG within-group ordinal readout
nodes.shortDescription: Ordinal-label decoding generalizes between four-segments and four-diagonals for groups of two, and between two-arcs and two-squares for groups of four. Decoder projections have published spectral peaks at the corresponding grouping frequencies; intermediate positions contribute, while fourth-position cross-sequence transfer in Figure S3 is nonsignificant (P=0.065).

nodes.name: Geometric-pair recognition and misses
nodes.shortDescription: In the subsequent primitive-pair task, every tested geometric rule has shorter reported recognition time and fewer missed violations than the unrelated-pair control. Rotations by three steps are harder on selected measures than some other primitives, contradicting equal behavioral cost as a general assumption for this task.

nodes.name: Primitive-pair context decoding
nodes.shortDescription: MEG distinguishes the 11 primitive conditions in the pair task. A balanced rotation-versus-symmetry decoder also performs above chance when the two visible locations are matched, supporting condition-sensitive information beyond those endpoints within this task.

nodes.name: MEG geometric-pair task
nodes.shortDescription: The primitive part follows the sequence part in the same 20 adults: four runs of 12 conditions, each with 32 pairs, including 11 geometric rules and an unrelated-pair control. Items within a pair have 433 ms SOA; the inter-pair interval is reported as 1100 ms. Participants report rule recognition and detect late pair violations. The unpredictable-location localizer follows.

nodes.name: Primitive-to-sequence transfer null
nodes.shortDescription: The primitive decoder trained on the pair task does not show significant generalization to the sequence task; the cross-task RSA primitive predictor is also nonsignificant after correction. Both task parts use the same participants, with different timing and fixed order.

nodes.name: MEG next-location anticipation
nodes.shortDescription: The published next-location decoding contrast is positive before item onset and decreases with formal sequence complexity in a one-tailed analysis (P=0.025). The contrast compares the upcoming location with its equally distant alternative around the previous location; four-diagonals and two-crosses are excluded because antipodal transitions make that comparison degenerate.

nodes.name: Sequence recognition and violation behavior
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected adult sample, recognition repetitions, violation-response time and missed violations increase with assigned sequence complexity, including analyses excluding the irregular template. Published AIC selection also retains the presence of rotation by three steps for recognition and response time, and spatial distance for misses; description cost alone is not a complete behavioral account.

nodes.name: Sequence transition-label decoding
nodes.shortDescription: Within the sequence task, MEG permits above-chance classification of the 11 primitive labels assigned to local transitions by the proposed grammar. RSA retains a primitive-identity contribution after the specified visuospatial regressors; the stricter matched-pair contrast and transfer between task parts remain distinct null results.

nodes.name: MEG sequence-learning task
nodes.shortDescription: The sequence part comes first: four runs of nine analyzed eight-location templates, with 12 successive repetitions per block at 433 ms SOA. Participants report recognition and detect a displaced item during repetition 11 or 12. Prior slower training repeats sequences until correct continuation; the later primitive and localizer blocks use the same participants.

nodes.name: Microglial proximity to activated thalamocortical boutons
nodes.shortDescription: CNO exposure in the hM3Dq thalamocortical preparation increased microglial fluorescence near labeled cortical boutons relative to control conditions. This is a morphological proximity readout, not direct synaptic inhibition.

nodes.name: Culture adenosine under CD39 inhibition
nodes.shortDescription: In the neonatal microglial culture assay, ARL67156 treatment reduced measured medium adenosine after ATP exposure relative to the vehicle condition. This is a pharmacological culture contrast, not a cell-exclusive adult mechanism.

nodes.name: CD39 inhibition in neonatal microglial culture
nodes.shortDescription: ARL67156 at 200 micromolar for 30 minutes before 100 micromolar ATP, versus 0.04% DMSO vehicle; culture medium sampled 60 minutes after ATP.

nodes.name: Culture adenosine under CD73 inhibition
nodes.shortDescription: In the neonatal microglial culture assay, APCP treatment reduced measured medium adenosine after ATP exposure relative to the vehicle condition. This is a pharmacological culture contrast, not a cell-exclusive adult mechanism.

nodes.name: CD73 inhibition in neonatal microglial culture
nodes.shortDescription: APCP at 10 micromolar for 30 minutes before 100 micromolar ATP, versus 0.04% DMSO vehicle; culture medium sampled 60 minutes after ATP.

nodes.name: CD73 surface signal on adult forebrain microglia
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 4b reports CD73 surface signal on adult forebrain CD39-positive microglia above the Nt5e-knockout control and below CD39-negative cells. Surface expression is an observation, not a measurement of adenosine flux or proof that microglia are its only source.

nodes.name: CNO and viral-expression control nulls
nodes.shortDescription: Extended Data Figure 6j reports no significant baseline microglial velocity or bouton-contact effect of DREADD expression alone or CNO without DREADD activation (three mice per condition). These controls constrain off-target explanations but are not equivalence proofs.

nodes.name: Chemogenetic thalamocortical activation with microglial imaging
nodes.shortDescription: hM3Dq/tdTomato-labeled thalamocortical neurons in Cx3cr1-EGFP mice, CNO 5 mg/kg and cortical microglial imaging; administration route remains conflicting in Methods and caption.

nodes.name: Microglial tip velocity during neuronal activation
nodes.shortDescription: CNO exposure in the hM3Dq thalamocortical preparation reduced microglial process-tip velocity while bouton proximity increased. Lower tip velocity and directed recruitment are different measurements.

nodes.name: Microglial process recruitment to capillary injury
nodes.shortDescription: After a targeted capillary lesion, nearby microglial processes switched toward the injured site and accumulated around it. This measures a local morphological response, not demonstrated neuronal protection.

nodes.name: Baseline microglial process remodeling
nodes.shortDescription: In the imaged adult neocortex, microglial processes repeatedly extended, retracted and formed protrusions on a minutes timescale. Somata generally stayed in place. Tissue-coverage and immune-protection interpretations are separate from these observations.

nodes.name: Purinergic microglial feedback mechanism
nodes.shortDescription: The proposed ATP/ADP sensing, CD39/CD73 metabolism and neuronal A1-receptor feedback model is constrained by the selected experiments. A uniquely identified, quantitative feedback mechanism across brain regions and states remains untested.

nodes.name: RGC material within developing microglia
nodes.shortDescription: Confocal reconstruction, 3D-SIM and immunoEM in P5 dLGN identified RGC-associated presynaptic material within microglial cytoplasm or lysosomes. This anatomical observation does not by itself establish the temporal order of synapse weakening, removal and degradation.

nodes.name: No observed soma migration toward injury
nodes.shortDescription: Microglial somata became rounder after capillary injury but were not observed migrating toward the lesion during recordings lasting up to 5.5 hours. Process recruitment does not imply soma migration or permanent immobility.

nodes.name: Protective function of microglial surveillance
nodes.shortDescription: Continuous process sampling and lesion recruitment may contribute to immune protection and tissue maintenance. Their causal contribution to clearance, neuronal survival and long-term maintenance is not established by morphology alone.

nodes.name: F5 discharge during execution without hand vision
nodes.shortDescription: All 14 formally tested mirror neurons discharged during monkey execution in both light and darkness. This subset supports a motor-associated response that does not require seeing the executing hand in that protocol.

nodes.name: Separate EMG control during action observation
nodes.shortDescription: In the displayed control sessions, the monitored hand and mouth muscles show no EMG change during observed actions and clear activity during the monkey's active grasping.

nodes.name: Sampled F1 action-observation null
nodes.shortDescription: The paper reports no action-observation discharge in 49 recorded hand-field F1 neurons. This control concerns the specified primary motor sample and observed actions.

nodes.name: Macaque F5 observation and execution responses
nodes.shortDescription: In the sampled F5 population, 92 of 532 neurons discharged during both observed experimenter actions and monkey execution. Object-directed hand actions were effective; object presentation alone, tool actions and pantomime were ineffective or weaker in the specified tests.

nodes.name: Mirror matching as an action-recognition hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Observation/execution matching is proposed to contribute to recognizing another agent's actions. The reviewed macaque responses make this a candidate mechanism; they do not establish its necessity, sufficiency or unique implementation.

nodes.name: F5 observation-only action responses
nodes.shortDescription: The Results describe 25 F5 neurons responsive to observed actions without the tested motor properties. The eight rows of Table 2 also sum to 25. These mirror-like units are distinct from the 92 units with both response properties.

nodes.name: Macaque visuomotor response congruence
nodes.shortDescription: Within the 92 F5 mirror units, the authors classify 29 as strictly congruent, 56 as broadly congruent and seven as non-congruent. Strict correspondence includes action type and manner of execution; the broader category permits different effective observed and executed actions.

nodes.name: Motion-choice bias across trials and sessions
nodes.shortDescription: Motion-task choices show an early contraversive bias after LIP suppression, with reported attenuation over trials and sessions.

nodes.name: Stimulated motion-choice and response-time effects
nodes.shortDescription: LIP microstimulation shifts choices toward the selected response field and changes response times directionally.

nodes.name: Persistent spine-size comparison during a new task
nodes.shortDescription: In 29 surviving spines, the calibrated head-diameter change during four days of adult capellini training was nonsignificant (paired-test P>0.08). Calibration divided head diameter by adjacent shaft diameter; this selected ratio does not establish unchanged synaptic strength.

nodes.name: Novel task after earlier reaching
nodes.shortDescription: Adults pretrained in adolescent reaching showed increased formation and elimination during a new capellini task compared with general adult controls: 8.7 versus 3.7 percent formation and 9.0 versus 4.0 percent elimination, five versus six mice. This is a compound task-history comparison.

nodes.name: Novel task after earlier reaching assay
nodes.shortDescription: Adolescent reaching training for eight to sixteen days, four months in control cage conditions, then four days of capellini handling in adults; 620 sampled spines versus 743 in general adult controls. There is no separately specified pretrained no-task control in this contrast.

nodes.name: Terminal dendrite motility comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Terminal dendrite extension and retraction over sixteen days did not differ significantly: 3.0 micrometers in controls and 2.8 in trained mice (P>0.5; 39 tips in three controls and 63 tips in four trained mice). Complete single-neuron arbors were not traced, so this null does not establish unchanged total branching.

nodes.name: First-day filopodial turnover comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Reported first-day filopodial formation and elimination comparisons were nonsignificant (P>0.2), despite the distinct spine-formation result. Filopodia and spines are separate morphological categories; pooling protrusions changes the denominator.

nodes.name: Selected first-session spine response
nodes.shortDescription: The first-session sample contained four trained mice with more than ten successful reaches, versus eight general controls. Formation was higher (10.6 versus 4.7 percent), while elimination was nonsignificant (P>0.9). The previous-day baseline and post-session image delimit the observed interval; they do not timestamp every spine birth within one hour.

nodes.name: Terminal motor-map sampling
nodes.shortDescription: Terminal microstimulation placed five imaged regions within the forelimb map, six at its border and three outside but within 300 micrometers. The fourteen maps constrain anatomical sampling; they do not show longitudinal map reorganization or uniquely identify the circuit carrying the learned behavior.

nodes.name: Homeostatic remodeling hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Formation, elimination and selective retention suggest candidate remodeling mechanisms. A unique homeostatic construction rule requires an explicit target, allowable replacements, measured dynamics and competing-model predictions; these observations do not establish a globally minimal or optimally organized circuit.

nodes.name: Later learning-phase spine comparisons
nodes.shortDescription: The day-eleven-to-twelve formation comparison was nonsignificant (P>0.6), as was survival of that new-spine subset to day sixteen (P>0.1). Earlier acquisition intervals showed different outcomes. Learning phase and imaging interval cannot be pooled into one constant formation or retention rule.

nodes.name: Long-term retention of newly appearing spines
nodes.shortDescription: Of spines first seen between days zero and four, 42.3 percent persisted to the reported approximately 120-day follow-up in mice trained for sixteen days, versus 13.5 percent in controls, five mice per group. Survival of this selected new-spine subset supports finite structural persistence, not permanence or memory necessity.

nodes.name: Long-term retention of newly appearing spines assay
nodes.shortDescription: Adolescent YFP-H mice imaged at days zero and four to classify new spines, with a third image at approximately day 120; sixteen-day reaching training versus general controls. The long follow-up measures survival of classified new spines, not total spine density.

nodes.name: Adult novel capellini handling and spine turnover
nodes.shortDescription: Naive adults learning capellini handling had greater four-day formation and elimination than controls: reported formation 7.8 versus 3.7 percent and elimination 8.2 versus 4.0 percent, five trained versus six control mice. This task is separate from single-seed reaching.

nodes.name: Adult novel capellini handling and spine turnover assay
nodes.shortDescription: Previously naive adult YFP-H mice, four days of capellini handling versus general adult controls; 552 versus 743 sampled spines.

nodes.name: Adult novel reaching and spine turnover
nodes.shortDescription: Naive adults learning the reaching task had greater four-day formation and elimination than controls: reported formation 7.9 versus 3.7 percent and elimination 9.5 versus 4.0 percent, five trained versus six control mice. The result does not supply an age-independent remodeling rate.

nodes.name: Adult novel reaching and spine turnover assay
nodes.shortDescription: YFP-H mice older than four months, novel reaching over four days versus general adult controls; 806 versus 743 sampled spines, normalized within each mouse to its initial count.

nodes.name: Regional and unsuccessful-learning controls
nodes.shortDescription: Four-day ipsilateral motor and contralateral sensory samples showed no significant turnover increase, with four mice per regional group. Five mice classified as failing to learn also showed no significant increase. These controls constrain the sampled contrasts without demonstrating all-brain specificity or isolating successful learning by random assignment.

nodes.name: Adult familiar-task turnover comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Adults retrained on the previously learned reaching task showed no significant formation or elimination increase versus general adult controls at four and eight days (reported P>0.1). The four-day spine cohorts used five retrained and six control mice; the eight-day groups used four each. This is not an equivalence result or proof that all synaptic physiology is unchanged.

nodes.name: Persistent-spine memory hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Retained newly appearing spines are a candidate substrate of durable motor memory. Selective perturbation of identified retained spines, matched behavioral testing and alternative-circuit comparisons are needed before claiming necessity or disjoint synaptic storage of different skills.

nodes.name: Spine count relative to the initial image
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 2c shows total spine counts approaching control levels by day sixteen, with both groups below their initial normalized count. Formation followed by increased elimination does not establish exact restoration of the original count, a fixed density setpoint or one-for-one replacement of particular connections.

nodes.name: Task success and spine-formation association
nodes.shortDescription: First-session reaching success and the percentage of newly appearing spines were associated, with reported squared correlation 0.77. This relationship does not establish that the measured new spines selectively cause learning or encode individual memories.

nodes.name: Adolescent reaching and spine turnover
nodes.shortDescription: Over four days, reaching-trained adolescent mice had greater spine formation and elimination than controls. Table S1 reports formation 13.3 versus 6.0 percent and elimination 13.7 versus 9.0 percent, with 25 trained and 18 control mice. These are interval-specific morphological responses in sampled dendrites.

nodes.name: Adolescent reaching and spine turnover assay
nodes.shortDescription: One-month-old YFP-H mice, four days of single-seed reaching versus general littermate controls; repeated contralateral motor-cortex dendrite imaging, 3881 versus 2510 counted spines, analyzed as mouse-level percentages.

nodes.name: Retinotopically matched MT inactivation
nodes.shortDescription: Verified MT or LIP muscimol silencing; fixed-duration motion followed by delayed saccade; spatial free-choice control.

nodes.name: MT-sensitive motion-discrimination response
nodes.shortDescription: Retinotopically matched MT silencing impairs motion direction sensitivity; moving the stimulus outside the affected field restores performance in the reported control.

nodes.name: NE-MO optogenetic activation
nodes.shortDescription: Optogenetic NE-MO activation increased L-MO radial astrocyte calcium fluorescence in the selected larval fish preparation.

nodes.name: Astrocyte calcium after NE-MO activation
nodes.shortDescription: Optogenetic NE-MO activation increased L-MO radial astrocyte calcium fluorescence in the selected larval fish preparation.

nodes.name: NE-MO activation after astrocyte ablation
nodes.shortDescription: After radial astrocyte ablation, NE-MO activation did not significantly suppress fictive swimming in the reported comparison; nonsignificance does not prove a zero effect.

nodes.name: Swim output after NE-MO activation
nodes.shortDescription: NE-MO activation reduced fictive swimming in fish with intact radial astrocytes, following a possible brief increase in swim vigor. The glia-ablated condition is a separate null result.

nodes.name: Persistent gene regulation by physiological neural activity
nodes.shortDescription: Physiological neural activity may establish persistent gene-regulatory states that alter later responses. ECS, maternal-care and five-day conditioning observations constrain this broader hypothesis but do not establish a universal downward-causation mechanism, inherited memory rule or minimal generating structure.

nodes.name: Neural communication-model hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: An explicit mapping between a formal communication model and measured neural variables remains to be tested.

nodes.name: Complete neuroimmune feedback mechanism
nodes.shortDescription: The experiments constrain a reciprocal neuroimmune model, but the full descending route, immune effector cells and receptor-level mediation remain untested here. Anatomical inputs and parallel intervention outcomes do not establish a uniquely closed causal circuit.

nodes.name: General neuroimmune regulation across states
nodes.shortDescription: Neural, endocrine, humoral and vascular routes motivate a broader model of neuroimmune regulation. The reviewed mouse assays do not establish one universal stabilizing process, a depression mechanism, minimal carrier counts or all proposed cross-level dependencies.

nodes.name: Neuroligin contact intervention
nodes.shortDescription: Neuroligin expression in contacting cells, with soluble beta-neurexin interference.

nodes.name: Complete neural-to-vascular conduction route
nodes.shortDescription: Capillary potassium sensitivity and arterial connexin perturbation constrain successive portions of neurovascular signaling in distinct preparations. The physiological potassium source, segment transitions and complete matched sequence remain unresolved; the evidence does not identify a unique whole route.

nodes.name: Neural activity inferred from perfusion
nodes.shortDescription: The mapping from neural activity to regional hemodynamic signals depends on preparation, vascular segment and physiological state. Reviewed evidence does not identify a universal invertible map from blood flow or BOLD to firing, energy use or a unique structural geometry.

nodes.name: Birth-labeled neuronal spiking
nodes.shortDescription: Somatic current injection evoked action potentials in selected GFP-labeled dentate neurons four to eight weeks after retroviral injection. This demonstrates excitability in a sampled neuron, not its necessary contribution to memory.

nodes.name: Birth-labeled neuronal spiking assay
nodes.shortDescription: Runner hippocampal slices; whole-cell current steps of 20-400 picoamperes for 500 milliseconds in selected GFP-positive cells, with post hoc neuronal identification.

nodes.name: Selected neuronal electrical comparisons
nodes.shortDescription: Selected labeled neurons had shorter membrane time constants and lower derived capacitance than unlabeled comparison neurons. Resting potential, input resistance, threshold, firing and spontaneous-input comparisons were nonsignificant in the reported samples; these nulls do not establish equivalence.

nodes.name: Recorded birth-label population
nodes.shortDescription: Thirteen of 58 recorded GFP-positive cells showed neuronal physiology, while 45 were nonexcitable. The latter population was not exhaustively identified, and this selected recording yield is not the probability that an adult-born cell becomes a neuron.

nodes.name: Birth-label and neuronal-marker profile
nodes.shortDescription: Mature neuronal markers were absent from sampled GFP-positive cells at 48 hours and present in a subset at four weeks. Marker fractions differed between housing groups, but variable retroviral capture and GFP expression prevent an absolute generation-rate comparison.

nodes.name: Neurogenesis and cognitive preservation
nodes.shortDescription: A complete neuron-birth-to-memory route remains a hypothesis. Mouse physiology and a Nestin-lineage Bax intervention constrain parts of the route; macaque histology has no matched functional assay. Rat training changes retained birth labels without isolating survival or testing newborn-cell necessity. These findings do not establish general cognitive necessity, unique neuron-count mediation or a causal human memory-preservation mechanism. Earlier autoradiographic nulls likewise do not establish that stable neuron populations are necessary for memory.

nodes.name: Birth-labeled neuronal morphology
nodes.shortDescription: Four-month labeled-cell samples had larger somata, longer and more branched dendrites and greater spine density than four-week samples. These cross-sectional measurements do not trace the same cell through maturation or define a universal maturation time.

nodes.name: Pattern separation measurement definition
nodes.shortDescription: Computational pattern separation concerns reduced overlap between output representations relative to input representations. Its operational use requires an explicit representation and similarity measure. Behavioral discrimination and regional activity are related assays with distinct observables.

nodes.name: Birth-labeled neuronal input
nodes.shortDescription: Perforant-path stimulation evoked postsynaptic responses in four sampled birth-labeled neurons. Spontaneous input was also observed in six cells. These afferent responses do not establish functional axonal output to the downstream circuit.

nodes.name: Birth-labeled neuronal input assay
nodes.shortDescription: Runner hippocampal slices four to eight weeks after labeling; extracellular perforant-path pulses of 100 microamperes for 0.2 milliseconds, paired at a 50-millisecond interval.

nodes.name: Neurogenic regulatory graph interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: RNA velocity, regulatory trios and inferred ligand/receptor networks provide model-dependent constraints for candidate graphs. Their constructed associations and embeddings do not identify a unique causal regulatory network, physical tissue geometry or minimal set of generative rules.

nodes.name: Running-associated BrdU count
nodes.shortDescription: Running-housed mice had more BrdU-labeled dentate cells than standard-housed mice in the separate 48-hour assay. BrdU incorporation does not itself count mature neurons or show that learning is necessary for neurogenesis.

nodes.name: Running-associated BrdU count assay
nodes.shortDescription: Separate BrdU cohorts: five runners and four controls, a single intraperitoneal dose of 100 micrograms per gram and counting after 48 hours.

nodes.name: Adult neurogenesis developmental stages
nodes.shortDescription: A review-based staging vocabulary distinguishes precursor expansion, early survival, postmitotic maturation and late survival. Its six milestones are type 1, type 2a, type 2b, type 3, early postmitotic and late postmitotic states. They describe developmental features rather than six disjoint populations.

nodes.name: Birth-labeled synaptic morphology
nodes.shortDescription: Spines, synaptophysin labeling and electron-microscopic contacts support synaptic organization of labeled dentate neurons. Morphological contacts and electrophysiological input are distinct evidence; neither alone demonstrates the full output-to-behavior route.

nodes.name: DL-APV induction intervention
nodes.shortDescription: Hippocampal slice CA1 recordings under Schaffer collateral-commissural stimulation and ionophoretic compounds.

nodes.name: Sampled nodose response specificity and overlap
nodes.shortDescription: Response heatmaps distinguish several cytokine- and nutrient-responsive subsets, but Extended Data 8e also displays two neurons responding to both IL-10 and fat among 63 recorded TRPA1-labeled neurons. Selectivity is conditional on the tested stimuli and classifier, not universal zero overlap.

nodes.name: OLLR calcium response
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, SAADL activation produced decreased downstream OLLR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).

nodes.name: D1 challenge in P2ry12 knockout mice
nodes.shortDescription: Whole-animal P2ry12 knockout versus control mice challenged with 5 mg/kg SKF81297; Figure 4f combines two cohorts.

nodes.name: D1-challenge seizure incidence after P2ry12 loss
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 4f source counts report seizures in 9/11 P2ry12 knockout mice versus 3/13 controls after D1 agonist. The genotype contrast is not a cell-selective perturbation of microglial sensing.

nodes.name: Stronger self-pain sensory BOLD contrasts
nodes.shortDescription: The self-by-pain interaction identifies stronger self-pain contrasts in contralateral SI/MI, SII/posterior insula and a caudal ACC focus under the specified stimulation task.

nodes.name: Shared affective representation hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Singer et al. interpret the shared ACC/insula response as recruitment of affective representations for another person's pain. This is an interpretation of task-related imaging and reported experience, rather than direct identification of a common neural code.

nodes.name: Shared self and partner-pain BOLD locations
nodes.shortDescription: In the sixteen scanned participants, conjunction and masking of pain-minus-nonpain contrasts identify shared ACC, bilateral middle/anterior insula, brainstem and lateral cerebellar BOLD locations during self stimulation and cues indicating partner stimulation.

nodes.name: Partner-pain BOLD and reported empathy traits
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 4 reports positive associations of partner-pain BOLD contrasts with Empathic Concern and BEES scores in selected ACC and left anterior-insula foci. The text does not find the corresponding trait covariation in right anterior insula.

nodes.name: Universal perceptual optimality hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A successful height cue-combination model does not establish one optimal algorithm for every perceptual process.

nodes.name: Perforant-path conditioning protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Urethane anesthesia; perforant-path conditioning and dentate extracellular recordings.

nodes.name: Extraintestinal cytokine perfusion and nodose imaging
nodes.shortDescription: The connected intestinal segment receives cytokines at 1 microgram/ml for three minutes in fifteen-minute trials, with interleaved saline and two trials per stimulus.

nodes.name: Nodose calcium during intestinal cytokine perfusion
nodes.shortDescription: Extraintestinal cytokine perfusion evoked repeatable calcium responses in sampled nodose neurons. Repeated responses in this preparation support stimulus sensitivity but do not establish direct receptor binding or a complete immune feedback loop.

nodes.name: Event-size distribution during inhibition blockade
nodes.shortDescription: Picrotoxin exposure changes the culture event-size distribution toward a bimodal form, with recovery after washout.

nodes.name: Plasticity-to-learning hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: The historical learning interpretation remains a separate hypothesis; the adopted potentiation assays do not measure learned behavior.

nodes.name: No significant calcium-event magnitude difference
nodes.shortDescription: The reported calcium-event magnitude comparisons did not differ significantly between PLX5622 and control cohorts at baseline or after 3 mg/kg SKF81297 (Extended Data Figure 6c). These cell-based comparisons are not an equivalence test.

nodes.name: PLX5622 in the striatal calcium assay
nodes.shortDescription: Systemic PLX5622 chow versus matched control after striatal GCaMP6s/GRIN-lens preparation; head-fixed baseline saline sessions, seven control and nine treated male mice.

nodes.name: PLX5622 with anesthetized striatal microdialysis
nodes.shortDescription: Five male mice per group; PLX5622 or control chow for one week before cannula placement, followed by one week recovery. Dialysate was collected under isoflurane, not awake baseline conditions.

nodes.name: Unresolved diet effect on D1-evoked calcium rate
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 3d reports a treatment effect on calcium-event frequency but no significant diet main effect or diet-by-treatment interaction (interaction P=0.08). Different within-group significance results do not establish a significant difference between treatment responses.

nodes.name: Extracellular striatal adenosine after PLX5622
nodes.shortDescription: Striatal dialysate adenosine was lower in the PLX5622 group than in controls in the anesthetized microdialysis assay. The source workbook supplies five independent mouse rows per group in ng/mL and a separate nM conversion.

nodes.name: Striatal calcium synchrony after microglial depletion
nodes.shortDescription: PLX5622-treated mice showed increased distance-dependent correlations and thresholded synchrony of striatal calcium events at baseline relative to controls. Correlated activity is the measured outcome; it does not identify direct neuronal connections.

nodes.name: Contact-induced presynaptic differentiation
nodes.shortDescription: Neuroligin-expressing nonneuronal contacts induce local presynaptic differentiation in the reported assay.

nodes.name: Neuronal production in the oldest macaques
nodes.shortDescription: Completed neuronal production at 23 years remains an interpretation of separate proliferation and immature-marker observations. Every 23-year-old animal was examined only two hours after BrdUrd; no matched longer-interval birthdated neuronal differentiation is supplied for that age.

nodes.name: Macaque regional BrdUrd labeling census
nodes.shortDescription: All eleven macaques had BrdUrd profiles in the dentate gyrus, SVZ and a region corresponding to the rostral migratory stream. Five two-hour animals localize S-phase labeling; later animals provide retained-label observations. Table 1 estimates do not directly measure a daily neuronal birth rate.

nodes.name: Developmental cessation of primate neurogenesis
nodes.shortDescription: A universal cessation of neuronal production after early development is an interpretation of the autoradiographic nulls. Eckenhoff and Rakic suggest tapering by four to six months. Neither study identifies an exact statistical cessation age or proves absence throughout primate or human adulthood.

nodes.name: Glucocorticoid mediation of macaque neuronal aging
nodes.shortDescription: Elevated glucocorticoids are proposed to mediate age-related reductions in hippocampal neurogenesis and their control to restore it. This macaque study contains no hormone assay or intervention identifying that mechanism.

nodes.name: Macaque neuronal colabels after longer labeling intervals
nodes.shortDescription: Young and middle-aged animals examined after longer intervals had dentate BrdUrd colabels with neuronal markers. The four five-injection animals provide TOAD-64, NSE and calbindin estimates, while NeuN is illustrated separately. These findings do not establish differentiated newborn neurons in the two-hour aged cohort.

nodes.name: Macaque precursor-to-olfactory-bulb route
nodes.shortDescription: Migration and addition of new olfactory-bulb neurons are proposed from regional BrdUrd and immature-marker profiles. A birthdated lineage traced to its destination, with functional integration, is not demonstrated.

nodes.name: Putative macaque migratory-stream profiles
nodes.shortDescription: BrdUrd and TOAD-64 profiles are reported in a region corresponding anatomically to the rodent rostral migratory stream. Figure 1B shows labeled profiles from animal 4. Location and phenotype do not themselves observe a migration trajectory or olfactory-bulb integration.

nodes.name: Macaque TOAD-64 age profiles
nodes.shortDescription: The paper reports fewer TOAD-64-positive dentate profiles at older ages. This cross-sectional marker result is separate from BrdUrd birthdating. Unreconciled group sizes in PMC Table 2 and analysis degrees of freedom prevent numerical reproduction of the age effect.

nodes.name: Probabilistic visual feedback during swimming
nodes.shortDescription: After closed loop was replaced by probabilistic swim-triggered visual feedback, mean radial astrocyte calcium rose faster with less reliable feedback. This readout supports temporal integration without identifying a unique algorithm.

nodes.name: Exploration during BLA projection activation
nodes.shortDescription: Selective BLA terminal activation in CeA increases open-arm and center exploration in the reported high-stress mouse preparation.

nodes.name: PV activation suppresses markers during isolation
nodes.shortDescription: Within the isolated housing condition, PV activation lowers EdU-positive density, MCM2-positive density and the MCM2-positive RGL fraction compared with isolated no-light controls. This treatment contrast is distinct from comparing the two housing groups under light.

nodes.name: MCM2 housing contrasts under PV activation
nodes.shortDescription: Under PV light stimulation, isolated and group-housed mice have no significant difference in MCM2-positive RGL density or fraction in Figure 5c (reported P > 0.1). This null is not equivalence and does not erase the significant EdU residual in the same figure.

nodes.name: Social housing crossed with PV activation
nodes.shortDescription: Group housing or at least six weeks of post-weaning isolation is crossed with the five-day PV light protocol or sham. Figure 5c compares terminal EdU-positive density, MCM2-positive density and MCM2-positive fraction across these four groups.

nodes.name: Residual isolation effect on EdU under PV activation
nodes.shortDescription: Under PV light stimulation, isolated mice retain higher EdU-positive RGL density than group-housed mice in Figure 5c, with reported P < 0.05. This residual housing contrast prevents a claim that PV activation abolishes every measured isolation effect.

nodes.name: Five-day PV activation
nodes.shortDescription: PV-Cre mice expressing ChR2 receive 472-nm, 5-ms pulses at 8 Hz for 30 seconds every five minutes, eight hours daily for five days, compared with no-light sham. Terminal EdU and MCM2 assays score nestin-positive radial cells.

nodes.name: PV inhibition increases RGL cycle markers
nodes.shortDescription: Five-day PV inhibition increases EdU-positive RGL density, MCM2-positive RGL density and the MCM2-positive fraction relative to no-light sham. Increased marker counts do not establish successful maturation, integration or a universal neural-activity requirement.

nodes.name: PV activation suppresses RGL cycle markers
nodes.shortDescription: Five-day PV activation lowers EdU-positive RGL density, MCM2-positive RGL density and the MCM2-positive fraction relative to no-light sham. The endpoint is suppression of the measured cycle markers, not reduced mature-neuron production measured across the full lineage.

nodes.name: Five-day PV inhibition
nodes.shortDescription: PV-Cre mice expressing eNpHR receive continuous 593-nm light for eight hours daily over five days, compared with no-light sham. Day-five EdU labeling and terminal MCM2 staining assess nestin-positive radial cells.

nodes.name: PV stimulation in dentate slices
nodes.shortDescription: Cre-dependent ChR2 stimulation of dentate PV interneurons is paired with whole-cell recording from GFP-labeled RGLs in acute slices. The RGL train is 8 Hz; the illustrated mature-granule-cell synaptic control uses 1 Hz.

nodes.name: PV-evoked RGL tonic current
nodes.shortDescription: PV photostimulation evokes a tonic RGL current that is blocked by bicuculline and enhanced by vigabatrin in the tested slices. This is a GABA-sensitive clamp-current response, not RGL spiking, cell-cycle entry or a measured one-to-one synapse.

nodes.name: Partial radial astrocyte ablation
nodes.shortDescription: Partial two-photon ablation of hindbrain radial astrocytes reduced time in futility-induced passivity in selected larval zebrafish; it did not abolish all passive behavior.

nodes.name: Radial astrocyte Opto-alpha1-AR activation
nodes.shortDescription: Light activation of gfap-driven Opto-alpha1-AR in hindbrain radial astrocytes reduced fictive swim power relative to controls.

nodes.name: Sparse astrocyte TRPV1 activation
nodes.shortDescription: Capsaicin treatment of fish expressing rat TRPV1 sparsely in radial astrocytes increased passive time in closed loop; transgene-negative and saline controls did not show the same effect.

nodes.name: No detected rapid nodose calcium response to LPS
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 4b reports no detected rapid nodose calcium response to 0.5 mg/kg LPS under the sampled short recording protocol. This does not exclude delayed responses, responses outside the sampled cells or indirect immune signaling.

nodes.name: Task-specific reaching adaptation
nodes.shortDescription: Practice in the imposed force field brings reaching paths toward their baseline shape in the reported task.

nodes.name: Post-exposure reaching aftereffects
nodes.shortDescription: Removing the practiced force field produces reaching deviations approximately opposite to initial exposure errors.

nodes.name: Resting-state attractor mechanism hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: The fitted resting-state attractor model is a candidate explanation, not a uniquely identified biological construction mechanism.

nodes.name: Diazepam suppresses RGL cycle markers
nodes.shortDescription: The five-day systemic diazepam comparison lowers EdU-positive and MCM2-positive RGL densities and the MCM2-positive fraction. Systemic treatment does not by itself identify a selective RGL receptor mechanism or measure completed neuron production.

nodes.name: Diazepam response across gamma2 genotypes
nodes.shortDescription: In the separate six-day post-tamoxifen drug comparison scored at seven days, diazepam reduces control clone activation and selected symmetric or astrocytic classes, while the corresponding cKO drug effects are not significant. This response pattern supports a receptor-related interpretation without establishing exclusive mediation.

nodes.name: Five-day systemic diazepam
nodes.shortDescription: Adult wild-type mice receive systemic diazepam at 5 mg/kg intraperitoneally once daily for five days, followed by six EdU injections two hours apart and tissue collection two hours after the last injection. Vehicle is the comparator.

nodes.name: Gamma2 deletion and early clone activation
nodes.shortDescription: Conditional gamma2 deletion increases assigned activated clones at two and seven days. At seven days, R+R and R+astrocyte classes increase while the R+intermediate-progenitor comparison is nonsignificant. The class distribution is not a uniform increase in neuronal production.

nodes.name: Sparse RGL-lineage gamma2 deletion
nodes.shortDescription: Sparse tamoxifen induction in nestin-CreERT2;Z/EG mice with conditional gamma2 alleles is compared with control alleles. Fixed-tissue GFP-positive clone assignments are evaluated at two, seven and thirty days under the specified morphological and marker rules.

nodes.name: Gamma2 deletion and thirty-day clone composition
nodes.shortDescription: At thirty days, conditional gamma2 deletion changes the assigned clone composition, including more R+R and no-R clones and fewer single-R and neuronal or multilineage classes. Later lineage effects and unresolved denominators prevent conversion to founder transition probabilities.

nodes.name: Adaptive RGL-circuit feedback hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: PV-dependent regulation of RGL cycling could contribute to adaptation of the dentate circuit. A closed path from circuit demand through new-neuron production and integration back to restored circuit function remains a hypothesis; the reported experiments test selected parts of that path.

nodes.name: RGL synaptic-current null
nodes.shortDescription: No spontaneous or field-evoked synaptic currents were detected in the 25 sampled GFP-positive RGLs, while tonic responses were observed. The assay does not establish an anatomical absence of every synaptic input.

nodes.name: Rhesus adult neuronal-label detection null
nodes.shortDescription: Rakic reports no heavily labeled cell with neuronal morphology in the examined adult brain samples. Occasional weak neuronal grains were excluded by case-specific criteria. This is a sampling- and threshold-dependent null, not a proof that every adult primate lacks neurogenesis.

nodes.name: Rhesus glial and endothelial labeling
