nodes.shortDescription: Heavily labeled glial and endothelial profiles were observed under the autoradiographic protocol. The illustrated brain profiles are juvenile, and oligodendroglial labeling was mostly reported at six and eighteen months. These observations do not measure balanced glial turnover or adult neuronal replacement.

nodes.name: Juvenile rhesus profiles with uncertain neuronal identity
nodes.shortDescription: Some labeled cells in the caudate and dentate gyrus of six-month-old animals could not be classified securely using routine cresyl-violet autoradiograms. This acknowledged identity ambiguity is separate from the reported adult neuronal null.

nodes.name: Rhesus offspring and peripheral labeling controls
nodes.shortDescription: Neuronal labeling in offspring of nine animals pregnant at injection and labeling of renewing peripheral tissues support isotope incorporation under those conditions. They do not quantify sensitivity for rare adult neuronal births.

nodes.name: General rhythm-coding hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A local rhythm intervention does not establish a general code or necessary hierarchy for cognition.

nodes.name: SAADL stimulation protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Targeted two-photon activation of SAADL during population calcium imaging in the Randi WT-background preparation.

nodes.name: Phase-dependent sensory response
nodes.shortDescription: Whisker-evoked responses depend on sensory-input phase relative to the experimentally induced gamma cycle.

nodes.name: Sequence algebraic pattern
nodes.shortDescription: An algebraic pattern describes relations between sequence elements across substitutions of their identities; AAB specifies two equal items followed by a different item.

nodes.name: Sequence chunk representation
nodes.shortDescription: A chunk groups a recurring set of contiguous sequence elements so that the group can be treated as a unit.

nodes.name: Nested constituent representation
nodes.shortDescription: A nested constituent description groups elements into units that can themselves occupy positions within larger constituents.

nodes.name: Sequence ordinal representation
nodes.shortDescription: An ordinal sequence description assigns an item to a position such as first or third, separately from its exact occurrence time.

nodes.name: Sequence transitions and timing
nodes.shortDescription: A sequence description can encode conditional transitions between particular items together with their temporal intervals.

nodes.name: Shared manifold hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Gallese proposes embodied simulation as a common basis for imitation, empathy and intention understanding. His shared manifold has phenomenological, functional and subpersonal descriptions, while retaining a distinction between self and other. This is an attributed hypothesis about social understanding.

nodes.name: Measured neural signal-propagation atlas
nodes.shortDescription: A publication-reported map of downstream calcium responses in immobilized TWISP nematodes, with measurement and response-test boundaries.

nodes.name: Synaptic-homeostasis sleep-function hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: The synaptic-homeostasis interpretation of sleep function remains separate from the experimentally measured transition and duration endpoints.

nodes.name: Homeostatic-circadian sleep model hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: The historical homeostatic/circadian model remains a proposed organizing account; its original equations and their mapping to the admitted interventions are unreviewed.

nodes.name: Exploration during BLA somatic activation
nodes.shortDescription: Direct BLA somatic activation decreases open-arm exploration in the reported comparison; it is not interchangeable with projection activation.

nodes.name: Common-founder multipotency and serial renewal
nodes.shortDescription: The mixed-cluster findings support the hypothesis that some adult Sox2-positive founders can retain a precursor descendant while producing differentiated progeny. Joint serial self-renewal and neuronal plus astrocytic output from the same fully tracked in vivo founder remain unestablished by these distinct terminal clusters.

nodes.name: Sparse retroviral cluster census
nodes.shortDescription: At twenty-one days, Table 2 reports 363 clusters across fifty-four hemispheres from twenty-seven mice: 301 neuron-only, seven astrocyte-only, ten Sox2-only, fifteen Sox2-plus-neuron, one neuron-plus-astrocyte and twenty-nine undetermined. Cluster categories preserve uncertainty and nested sampling; they are not independent animal-level fate probabilities.

nodes.name: Expansion of selected Sox2 reporter cultures
nodes.shortDescription: The reported live-cell GFP fraction rises from about six percent after isolation to about seventy percent after four weeks in FGF2/EGF culture. FACS-selected cultures can be expanded through repeated passages while retaining GFP. These results show culture selection and expansion, without measuring an in vivo renewal rate.

nodes.name: Sox2 culture differentiation under distinct conditions
nodes.shortDescription: Forskolin-treated Sox2-GFP cultures exhibit neuronal and astrocytic markers. A separate coculture with neonatal rat hippocampal neurons yields donor-labeled RIP-positive cells. The different assay conditions support culture differentiation potential without establishing in vivo tripotency of one tracked founder.

nodes.name: Lentiviral targeting and the BrdU selection gate
nodes.shortDescription: The seven-day targeting control reports SOX2 in seventy percent of GFP-positive cells and differentiated neuronal off-target labeling of 26 +/- 3% among eight hundred sampled cells. The population fate experiment adds BrdU selection to exclude nondividing off-target neurons; reporter labeling alone is insufficient to identify a Sox2 progenitor lineage.

nodes.name: Mixed phenotypes in sparse labeled clusters
nodes.shortDescription: Fifteen clusters contain a Sox2-positive cell and a neuron; one contains a neuron and an astrocyte. One illustrated Sox2-plus-neuron cluster has a radial GFAP-positive process. These observations support common-founder and self-renewal interpretations conditional on clonal assignment, while the optical-depth series does not observe division through time.

nodes.name: Marker profiles after population fate labeling
nodes.shortDescription: Lentiviral reporter-positive, BrdU-positive cells include neuronal, astroglial and Sox2- or BLBP-retaining phenotypes in separate marker assays. This supports heterogeneous population outcomes. Table 1 percentages cannot be pooled into a fate distribution, and its S-100beta count and printed percentage conflict.

nodes.name: Population maintenance through balanced lineage output
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 6B proposes that increased progenitor production can coexist with maintenance of the Sox2-positive pool. This is a population-level interpretation, explicitly distinct from asymmetric division of individual cells. Endpoint density nulls do not identify a feedback controller or a complete birth-and-loss balance.

nodes.name: Radial and nonradial lineage-cycle hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 6A proposes relationships between radial and nonradial Sox2-positive populations. A rare radial-process mixed cluster motivates possible nonradial-to-radial production, but a reversible lineage cycle and radial self-renewal are not directly traced. Basal marker differences do not identify both transition directions.

nodes.name: Sox2 reporter phenotypes in the adult SGZ
nodes.shortDescription: Radial and nonradial Sox2-GFP cells have distinct morphologies. In the sampled basal SGZ, proliferation-marker colabeling is observed in nonradial cells, while radial processes carry nestin, GFAP and BLBP. This is a regional reporter phenotype, not a universal identity test for stem cells or permanent radial quiescence.

nodes.name: Reported cycling profiles in the wheel comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 5 reports higher BrdU, Ki67, DCX and selected reporter-colabeled densities in the wheel-access group, including cycling radial reporter cells. The Methods control-genotype conflict prevents admission as a matched GFP-reporter intervention effect. These are cycle-related and precursor-marker profiles, not completed neuronal lineages.

nodes.name: GFP-density nulls in the wheel comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The reported wheel-access comparisons are nonsignificant for total GFP-positive density (P=0.1724, n=7) and radial GFP-positive density (P=0.1125, n=5). These endpoint nulls do not establish a conserved stem-cell population, equivalence or homeostatic feedback; control-genotype identity remains unresolved.

nodes.name: Adult rectangle-boundary limitation
nodes.shortDescription: In Experiment 1, two-rectangles positions 5, 9 and 13 do not have lower error than the irregular baseline, and the reported across-boundary improvement test is nonsignificant (P=0.13). The position-9 comparison is worse than baseline. Overall sequence benefit does not show successful acquisition of every deeper boundary.

nodes.name: Adult geometric-sequence continuation
nodes.shortDescription: In 23 French adults, every selected regular category has lower mean error than the irregular baseline, including the first presentation's positions 6-8. The effect concerns these stimulus contrasts under corrective feedback, not recovery of a complete unseen program from one exposure.

nodes.name: Adult geometric-sequence continuation task
nodes.shortDescription: Experiment 1: mouse-click predictions on an eight-location octagon, starting with two shown locations and continuing through 16 positions with correction after errors. A repeat sequence is always first; subsequent blocks are randomized.

nodes.name: Preschool complex-sequence limitations
nodes.shortDescription: In Experiment 2, four-diagonals, two-rectangles and two-crosses show no significant overall error advantage over the irregular baseline. Four-point irregular memory also shows no significant within-phase improvement. These task outcomes do not prove missing recursion or a universal four-item capacity.

nodes.name: Preschool geometric-sequence continuation
nodes.shortDescription: In the 24-child Experiment 2 cohort, repeat, repeat+2, two-arcs, two-squares and four-segments sequences have lower mean error than the irregular baseline. This is task-specific success with selected patterns; it does not establish possession of every proposed primitive.

nodes.name: Preschool geometric-sequence continuation task
nodes.shortDescription: Experiment 2: children point to animal locations and the experimenter clicks. Show five locations then predict three; after a break show three then predict five. Errors trigger correction. One exemplar per category except four axial-symmetry exemplars.

nodes.name: fMRI association with sequence description cost
nodes.shortDescription: BOLD activity covaries positively with assigned sequence description cost in frontal, parietal and occipital regions. Bilateral IFG remains in the complexity map after the specified exclusive masks for saccade distance or a four-points versus two-points memory contrast.

nodes.name: Spatial task and functional localizer overlap
nodes.shortDescription: In the same twenty imaging participants, the nesting-associated map largely overlaps calculation-relative-to-sentence regions and shows little overlap with sentence-relative-to-rest regions. Independently localized mathematics ROIs respond broadly during the spatial task; language ROI responses are generally weak or deactivated, with condition-specific exceptions in Figure 5.

nodes.name: Regional memory-control responses
nodes.shortDescription: Across one-point, two-point, four-point and irregular controls, PMd has a significant memory-demand effect. The corresponding IFG, mid-DLPFC and anterior-caudate tests are nonsignificant (reported P=0.08, 0.8 and 0.6 respectively).

nodes.name: fMRI association with a gaze boundary regressor
nodes.shortDescription: A fixed sequence contrast derived from anticipation index at position 5 minus its mean at positions 3 and 7 is associated with activity including right mid-DLPFC and bilateral anterior caudate. Right mid-DLPFC remains after excluding voxels exceeding the specified threshold in the complexity map.

nodes.name: Learning-related fMRI pattern differentiation
nodes.shortDescription: Multivoxel similarity changes over repeated sequences. The reported interaction between learning group and repetition is significant in IFG and mid-DLPFC but not in PMd, IPS or SPL; Figure S7 preserves the group-specific profiles rather than a universal monotonic change.

nodes.name: Spatial sequence gaze anticipation
nodes.shortDescription: In the separate 44-adult behavioral experiment, average anticipation index increases with assigned sequence description cost (reported R squared 0.86, P<0.001): simpler templates have less normalized gaze error at target onset. Repeat and alternate patterns show an advantage over irregular from the fourth and seventh locations of the first presentation respectively.

nodes.name: Position-specific gaze learning
nodes.shortDescription: For two-arcs and two-squares in the 44-adult experiment, internal positions show lower anticipation index than boundaries 1 and 5. Those boundaries differ from the irregular baseline only during repetitions three and four, supporting slower acquisition at the specified boundaries under this task.

nodes.name: Deep sequence boundary nulls
nodes.shortDescription: In the 44-adult experiment, positions 1 and 5 of two-rectangles and two-crosses do not significantly differ from irregular even after four repetitions (reported P>0.1). At the last repetition, the two-crosses position-7 comparison has P=0.052 despite surrounding text calling the second-level comparisons significant.

nodes.name: Normalized gaze anticipation index
nodes.shortDescription: For a nonzero target displacement, Wang et al. define anticipation index as gaze-to-current-target distance at target onset divided by previous-to-current-target distance. Zero means gaze at the upcoming target; gaze at the previous target gives one, although other gaze positions can also give one. Lower values indicate greater anticipation. This ratio is not the percentage of anticipatory movements and is not generally bounded above by one.

nodes.name: Spatial sequence saccade task
nodes.shortDescription: Forty-four adults follow a flashing target among eight octagon locations. Nine sequence categories are presented in randomized blocks, each eight-location sequence repeated four times without a pause: 1000 ms target display plus 150 ms interstimulus interval (1150 ms SOA). Six runs are reported; the four segment-axis variants are averaged in the behavioral summaries.

nodes.name: Munduruku geometric-sequence continuation
nodes.shortDescription: In the 20-participant Munduruku cohort, all tested regular categories except two-crosses have lower overall error than the irregular baseline. The two-arcs boundary at position 13 is below baseline; two-squares and diagonal-position contrasts remain uneven. The cohort combines adolescents and adults.

nodes.name: Munduruku two-crosses limitation
nodes.shortDescription: In Experiment 4, two-crosses has no significant mean-error advantage over the irregular baseline. Four-diagonals has an overall advantage but its individual position tests do not establish consistently better performance after correction. Neither outcome identifies a missing cognitive primitive or a causal schooling effect.

nodes.name: Munduruku geometric-sequence continuation task
nodes.shortDescription: Experiment 4: the shorter Experiment 3 task, including two full previews, collected during 2014 and 2015 field trips. Participants have limited access to schooling; this is not an age-, schooling- or task-matched comparison with the French college cohort.

nodes.name: Finite octagon sequence language
nodes.shortDescription: S1 Text defines programs over the eight states 0 through 7, with primitive output maps, concatenation and three loop forms: chaining from the previous output, transforming each output point, and rerunning a body from transformed input states. These loop meanings and the fixed input used to define cost must be explicit before using shortest programs to construct candidate sequences.

nodes.name: Between-cohort preview comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The paper reports no significant position-by-position improvement in Experiment 3 compared with Experiment 2 despite two additional full previews. The comparison uses separate cohorts with different age ranges, not a randomized within-person exposure intervention. It does not establish equivalence or exclude an exposure contribution.

nodes.name: Complex-sequence limitations after previews
nodes.shortDescription: In Experiment 3, the overall two-squares, four-diagonals, two-rectangles and two-crosses contrasts are nonsignificant against the irregular baseline. Two-squares therefore differs from the significant overall result in Experiment 2; the experiments are not identical in every outcome.

nodes.name: Geometric continuation after two previews
nodes.shortDescription: In the separate 23-child Experiment 3 cohort, repeat, repeat+2, two-arcs and four-segments sequences have lower mean error than the irregular baseline. Two complete previews precede each block, followed by the same corrective task.

nodes.name: Geometric continuation after two previews task
nodes.shortDescription: Experiment 3: the Experiment 2 task begins each block with two complete previews of its eight-location sequence. The comparison with Experiment 2 uses different children with a different age range; random allocation to preview conditions is not reported.

nodes.name: Probabilistic geometric-resource use
nodes.shortDescription: The published model represents variable use of point symmetry and nested loops through fitted availability probabilities. This can describe selected group error profiles, but it does not uniquely identify which individuals possess a resource or why they fail to use it. In the Munduruku fit, full nesting with reduced point-symmetry use performs comparably to the two-resource fit.

nodes.name: Scanner gaze outcomes and boundary nulls
nodes.shortDescription: The scanner gaze summary reports a positive association between anticipation index and assigned cost (R squared 0.74, P<0.001). Figure S3 reports no significant advantage over irregular at positions 1, 3, 5 and 7 of both two-rectangles and two-crosses (all P>0.1).

nodes.name: SST manipulation and RGL cycle-marker nulls
nodes.shortDescription: The tested five-day SST-interneuron activation and inhibition comparisons show no significant change in the RGL EdU/MCM2 endpoints. Slice controls show mature-granule-cell responses while RGL responses to the tested SST stimulation are not detected.

nodes.name: Poststroke capillary-velocity comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Capillary velocity did not differ significantly across control, pooled one-to-two-week and six-week groups (F(2,11)=1.97, P=0.19). This optical plasma-motion readout is not volumetric perfusion, equivalent blood supply or proof of complete vascular recovery.

nodes.name: Later spine-density comparisons
nodes.shortDescription: The two-week density sample did not differ significantly from the one-week sample (1.88 versus 1.81 spines per ten micrometers; P=0.2). The six-week value, 2.08, was nonsignificantly different from the 2.23 control value (reported P=0.09). These separate cohorts do not establish exact restoration or continuous recovery of the same dendrites.

nodes.name: Spine-imaging control limits
nodes.shortDescription: The main text reports nonsignificant changes in adjacent dendritic fluorescence and in shaft fluorescence around six spine-appearance cases. These controls constrain brightness and rotation artifacts, but pooled cases, finite axial resolution and excluded transient protrusions limit an exhaustive census of true synaptic formation.

nodes.name: Infarct extent and interval comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The reported lesion-volume sample averaged 0.97 cubic millimeters in nine mice. One- versus two-week lesion volumes were nonsignificantly different (0.975 versus 0.974 cubic millimeters; P=0.49). This does not establish identical lesions, absence of later tissue deformation or full recovery.

nodes.name: Near and distant cortical spine comparison
nodes.shortDescription: At two weeks, the three-mouse regional comparison reported higher formation near than far from the infarct (0.85 versus 0.22 percent; P<0.01), while elimination was nonsignificant (0.68 versus 0.18 percent; P=0.08). The statistical units remain unresolved; this anatomical comparison does not isolate distance as a causal mechanism.

nodes.name: Neurovascular alignment mechanism hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Parallel dendritic and vascular orientations may reflect mechanical tissue deformation, coordinated growth or a mixture of processes. Longitudinal three-dimensional identity and selective perturbations are needed to distinguish them before alignment can define a generative graph-construction law.

nodes.name: Peri-infarct sensory reflectance maps
nodes.shortDescription: Peri-infarct tissue exhibited stimulus-associated intrinsic optical responses at two and six weeks. The 635-nanometer reflectance maps locate responsive tissue but do not directly record neuronal spikes or establish restored forelimb behavior or the function of individual new spines.

nodes.name: Projected dendrite and vessel alignment
nodes.shortDescription: At six weeks, sampled dendritic and vascular segment orientations near the infarct were more concentrated than control distributions, while the farther orientation comparisons were nonsignificant. These are projected angle distributions from three mice per group; bin-variance tests do not establish a unique growth trajectory or network topology.

nodes.name: Remodeling-mediated recovery hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Increased peri-infarct spine formation is a candidate contributor to functional recovery. This study lacks a selective test connecting its measured new spines to recovered behavior; matched functional measurements and perturbation or rescue are required before assigning mediation or a universal therapeutic window.

nodes.name: Early peri-infarct spine density
nodes.shortDescription: At one week, sampled dendrites had lower spine density than controls: reported 1.81 versus 2.23 spines per ten micrometers, four versus six mice. This spatial density is distinct from the increased percentage of new protrusions during the acute six-hour assay.

nodes.name: Early peri-infarct spine density assay
nodes.shortDescription: One-week poststroke versus control cohort; lateral-spine counting per ten micrometers of selected superficial dendrites, four versus six mice, without a pre-injury measurement of those same branches.

nodes.name: Poststroke spine-elimination comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The overall control and one-, two- and six-week comparison did not show a significant increase in six-hour spine elimination (F(3,13)=2.11, P=0.148). Increased formation cannot be assigned automatically to elimination or interpreted as a proven balanced replacement rule.

nodes.name: Spine formation 1 week after stroke
nodes.shortDescription: At one week after photothrombosis, the reported six-hour spine-formation percentage was 1.37, versus 0.14 in controls; 4 poststroke mice and six controls. The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

nodes.name: Spine formation 1 week after stroke assay
nodes.shortDescription: Acute imaging one week after photothrombosis versus sham controls: 1590 versus 4266 counted spines; hourly stacks under urethane, new lateral protrusions retained at the six-hour endpoint.

nodes.name: Spine formation 2 weeks after stroke
nodes.shortDescription: At 2 weeks after photothrombosis, the reported six-hour spine-formation percentage was 0.93, versus 0.14 in controls; 4 poststroke mice and six controls. The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

nodes.name: Spine formation 2 weeks after stroke assay
nodes.shortDescription: Acute imaging 2 weeks after photothrombosis versus sham controls: 1566 versus 4266 counted spines; hourly stacks under urethane, new lateral protrusions retained at the six-hour endpoint.

nodes.name: Spine formation 6 weeks after stroke
nodes.shortDescription: At 6 weeks after photothrombosis, the reported six-hour spine-formation percentage was 0.75, versus 0.14 in controls; 3 poststroke mice and six controls. The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

nodes.name: Spine formation 6 weeks after stroke assay
nodes.shortDescription: Acute imaging 6 weeks after photothrombosis versus sham controls: 1788 versus 4266 counted spines; hourly stacks under urethane, new lateral protrusions retained at the six-hour endpoint.

nodes.name: Late peri-infarct vascular volume fraction
nodes.shortDescription: Six weeks after photothrombosis, fluorescent vascular volume fraction was higher than in controls: reported 7.25 versus 4.36 percent, t(8)=3.14, P<0.01. This volume-occupancy result does not count new vessels or establish a selectively tested angiogenesis mechanism.

nodes.name: Late peri-infarct vascular volume fraction assay
nodes.shortDescription: Texas Red dextran plasma labeling and two-photon imaging of selected peri-infarct cortex at six weeks versus controls; volume occupied by labeled vasculature. The total vascular cohort has fourteen mice, with exact per-assay membership unresolved.

nodes.name: Cortical potassium and laser Doppler
nodes.shortDescription: Surface 15 mM potassium, with and without 100 micromolar barium; six wild-type and five knockout mice in Figure 5a.

nodes.name: Conceptual bootstrapping proposal
nodes.shortDescription: Carey proposes that initially partial symbol structures acquire content through mappings to available representations, analogy and induction, enabling a changed conceptual repertoire.

nodes.name: Symbols in a compositional system
nodes.shortDescription: In the scoped mental-program framework, a symbol participates in rules for combining representations into structured expressions; recognizing an arbitrary sign alone does not establish this capacity.

nodes.name: Description cost in a specified language
nodes.shortDescription: For the geometric-program model, description cost is the length of the shortest program that produces the target in a specified language under its stated cost convention.

nodes.name: Representational development contrast
nodes.shortDescription: A developmental explanation must specify the starting representational resources, the target capacities and a learning process connecting them; individual learning, cultural construction and evolution require separate accounts.

nodes.name: Mental program induction for geometry
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed account of geometric cognition infers a compact program from an observed form; composition and repeated use of expressions can generate further forms within the chosen language.

nodes.name: Vector binding of roles and contents
nodes.shortDescription: A candidate neural representation binds a content vector to a role vector and combines the results so that a composite can participate in further binding.

nodes.name: Synchronization-criticality equivalence hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Phase synchronization, sampled event avalanches and criticality at a specified transition require distinct measurements and do not entail one another.

nodes.name: Task-associated calcium co-activation ensembles
nodes.shortDescription: Thresholded calcium activity grouped within imaging frames defines task-associated co-activation ensembles; their identity is operational and mouse-specific.

nodes.name: Bicuculline-sensitive output profile
nodes.shortDescription: Of five targets tested with bicuculline, three showed little or no change and two showed substantial blockade. Kynurenic acid then blocked the remaining response. This pharmacological profile supports mixed routes, including an indirect inhibitory component, rather than uniformly direct excitatory output.

nodes.name: CA3 bouton and contact profiles
nodes.shortDescription: Later birth-labeled CA3 bouton samples were larger than the 17-day sample. Contact censuses shifted from predominantly shaft contacts to shared and then individual thorny excrescences across 17, 28 and 75 days. These cross-sectional samples do not observe the same bouton replacing a pre-existing input.

nodes.name: DCG-IV response suppression
nodes.shortDescription: The group-II metabotropic glutamate receptor agonist DCG-IV suppressed light-evoked postsynaptic responses in two experiments, consistent with mossy-fiber involvement. This does not locate every synaptic hop or establish a universal connection strength.

nodes.name: DCG-IV response suppression assay
nodes.shortDescription: Light-evoked target recordings with 1 micromolar DCG-IV; two pharmacological experiments, including an increased-failure example.

nodes.name: Hilar bouton size null
nodes.shortDescription: The reported hilar bouton-area comparison across ages was nonsignificant (P=0.65). The 75-day adult-born versus early-postnatal CA3 comparison was also nonsignificant (P=0.18). Neither result establishes equivalent morphology or a common universal maturation schedule.

nodes.name: Kynurenic-acid response blockade
nodes.shortDescription: Kynurenic acid blocked light-evoked postsynaptic responses in eight tested targets. Dependence on glutamatergic transmission can occur upstream of an inhibitory relay, so blockade does not make every recorded response a direct excitatory synapse.

nodes.name: Kynurenic-acid response blockade assay
nodes.shortDescription: Light-evoked target recordings with bath-applied 4-10 millimolar kynurenic acid; eight tested responses and selected washout examples.

nodes.name: Birth-labeled light-evoked spiking
nodes.shortDescription: Light pulses evoke spikes in selected ChR2-labeled dentate neurons. Opsin expression and age affect capture and latency; this is an imposed activation protocol, not endogenous firing or a universal maturation threshold.

nodes.name: Birth-labeled light-evoked spiking assay
nodes.shortDescription: Whole-cell recordings from retrovirally ChR2-labeled granule cells in slices; supplementary pulse and frequency protocols, with most recordings using barium and retinal supplementation.

nodes.name: Output latency and route classification
nodes.shortDescription: Seven of 14 responses were classified as probably monosynaptic and two as probably polysynaptic; five were unresolved. Light-to-current latency includes opsin-dependent spike timing and cannot supply an exact synaptic delay, route length or unique circuit topology.

nodes.name: Birth-labeled neuronal output
nodes.shortDescription: Illumination of labeled granule-cell populations evoked postsynaptic currents in 14 of 107 sampled target cells. This supports functional output in selected slices; the yield is not a connection probability, and the illustrated CA3 pyramidal response includes a polysynaptic inhibitory route.

nodes.name: Birth-labeled neuronal output assay
nodes.shortDescription: Hippocampal slices with 10-millisecond light pulses at 0.2-4 Hz and target voltage clamp at -60 or -70 millivolts; responding targets were sampled 13.4-20.4 weeks after retrovirus.

nodes.name: Existing-target recruitment hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Recruitment of pre-existing postsynaptic structures is a candidate mechanism consistent with the age-specific bouton samples. Competition, addition and replacement require longitudinal contact identity and selective perturbations before becoming a generative construction rule.

nodes.name: Cytokines after LPS-TRAPed cNST activation
nodes.shortDescription: Under LPS challenge, hM3Dq activation of the LPS-TRAPed cNST population reduced circulating IL-6 and IL-1beta and increased IL-10 relative to CNO-treated mCherry controls. These effects do not identify the descending efferent pathway.

nodes.name: LPS-TRAP2 cNST activation protocol
nodes.shortDescription: LPS-TRAP2 cNST hM3Dq versus mCherry, six mice per group; at least four weeks after labeling, with the standard LPS/cytokine protocol.

nodes.name: Cytokines after LPS-TRAPed cNST inhibition
nodes.shortDescription: Under LPS challenge, hM4Di inhibition of the LPS-TRAPed cNST population increased circulating IL-6 and IL-1beta and reduced IL-10 relative to CNO-treated mCherry controls. This is a three-analyte blood profile, not an immune-cell-specific production assay.

nodes.name: LPS-TRAP2 cNST inhibition protocol
nodes.shortDescription: LPS-TRAP2 cNST hM4Di versus mCherry, six mice per group; rechallenge at least four weeks after labeling and blood sampling two hours after LPS.

nodes.name: Cytokine nulls without the LPS challenge
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 2c and Extended Data 3 report no significant IL-6, IL-1beta or IL-10 changes from LPS-TRAPed cNST activation in the saline condition. Replotted data do not add an independent replication, and the null is limited to these measurements.

nodes.name: Cytokines after Trpa1-cre nodose activation
nodes.shortDescription: Trpa1-cre nodose hM3Dq activation reduced circulating IL-6 and IL-1beta and increased IL-10 after LPS relative to mCherry controls. The intervention targets a neuronal population, not the TRPA1 channel protein alone.

nodes.name: Trpa1-cre nodose activation with LPS
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral nodose hM3Dq versus mCherry with CNO; seven treated and four control mice, sampled two hours after 0.1 mg/kg LPS.

nodes.name: Corticosterone null after Trpa1-cre activation
nodes.shortDescription: At two hours after LPS, the Trpa1-cre nodose hM3Dq versus mCherry comparison reported no significant circulating corticosterone difference (five mice per group). This is a separate cohort from the bacterial-load assay and does not establish pathway equivalence.

nodes.name: Trpa1-cre activation in endotoxaemia
nodes.shortDescription: Nodose hM3Dq versus mCherry with repeated CNO around 12.5 mg/kg intraperitoneal LPS; eight treated and nine control mice.

nodes.name: Survival after Trpa1-cre activation and endotoxin
nodes.shortDescription: In the high-dose LPS assay, the Trpa1-cre nodose activation group had greater survival than mCherry controls through the plotted nine-day window. This endpoint concerns endotoxaemia, not clearance of a live infection.

nodes.name: Bacterial tissue load after Trpa1-cre activation
nodes.shortDescription: Sustained Trpa1-cre nodose hM3Dq activation during oral Salmonella infection increased bacterial colony counts per gram in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes relative to mCherry controls. Lower inflammation cannot be generalized to improved host defense.

nodes.name: Trpa1-cre activation during live Salmonella infection
nodes.shortDescription: Oral S. enterica serovar Typhimurium, 1-2 x 10^7 CFU; nodose hM3Dq versus mCherry, four mice per group. Eight CNO injections begin twelve hours before inoculation; tissue CFU measured at day five.

nodes.name: Adult TSA infusion with hippocampal ChIP
nodes.shortDescription: TSA or DMSO vehicle infused intracerebroventricularly once daily for seven days; bulk hippocampal ChIP assayed acetyl-H3K9 and NGFI-A association. Figure 3 reports four animals/group; supplementary fixed-tissue methods specify six.

nodes.name: Hippocampal GR protein signal after TSA
nodes.shortDescription: TSA increased hippocampal GR protein immunoreactivity normalized to alpha-tubulin in adult low-care offspring relative to vehicle. This is a protein readout, separate from promoter methylation, RNA abundance and the restraint-stress cohort.

nodes.name: GR promoter CpG site 16 readout after TSA
nodes.shortDescription: TSA reduced the hippocampal bisulfite methylation readout at NGFI-A-site CpG 16 in adult low-care offspring relative to vehicle. The broad drug intervention does not establish locus-specific demethylation as the unique mediator of later outcomes.

nodes.name: GR promoter CpG site 17 readout after TSA
nodes.shortDescription: TSA reduced the CpG site-17 bisulfite readout in both high- and low-care offspring. Maternal-care class and cross-fostering did not show that site-17 effect, so TSA does not exactly recreate the maternal-care methylation pattern.

nodes.name: H3K9-acetylation-associated GR promoter signal after TSA
nodes.shortDescription: In adult offspring of low-care mothers, repeated intracerebroventricular TSA increased acetyl-H3K9-associated ChIP signal at the GR exon 1_7 promoter relative to vehicle. The signal is a bulk chromatin assay, not single-cell accessibility or DNA methylation.

nodes.name: No detected TSA stress-response effect in high-care offspring
nodes.shortDescription: The restraint-associated corticosterone response of high-care offspring showed no significant TSA effect in the reported assay. This group-specific null does not establish equivalence or a universal lack of drug effects.

nodes.name: Adult TSA infusion with hippocampal bisulfite assay
nodes.shortDescription: Seven daily intracerebroventricular TSA or vehicle infusions in adult maternal-care groups, followed by GR exon 1_7 promoter bisulfite mapping. Figure 4 reports five animals/group; cloned molecules are nested within animals.

nodes.name: NGFI-A-associated GR promoter signal after TSA
nodes.shortDescription: Repeated TSA increased NGFI-A-associated ChIP signal at the GR exon 1_7 promoter in adult low-care offspring relative to vehicle. This effect does not independently identify which chromatin modification caused the binding change.

nodes.name: Adult TSA infusion with hippocampal GR immunoblot
nodes.shortDescription: Adult male maternal-care groups received TSA or vehicle. Hippocampal GR protein was normalized to alpha-tubulin; Figure 5a reports five animals/group while Western methods specify six. Technical triplicates do not increase the animal count.

nodes.name: Restraint-associated corticosterone after TSA
nodes.shortDescription: In a separate adult low-care offspring cohort, TSA reduced the plasma corticosterone response associated with a 20-minute restraint challenge relative to vehicle. Samples extended to 90 minutes after restraint onset; this is an endocrine response, not direct evidence of subjective stress or a unique neural mechanism.

nodes.name: Adult TSA infusion followed by restraint challenge
nodes.shortDescription: A separate adult male cohort received TSA or vehicle and a 20-minute restraint challenge. Figure 5b reports ten animals/group; baseline and post-onset blood sampling continued through 90 minutes. Corrected corticosterone units are micrograms/dL.

nodes.name: Relative engulfment after retinal TTX
nodes.shortDescription: Microglia contained more labeled RGC input from the TTX-treated eye than from the vehicle eye in the selected P5 dLGN regions. This supports activity-dependent selection without identifying the exact synapse-tagging sequence.

nodes.name: Retinal TTX in the engulfment assay
nodes.shortDescription: P4 CX3CR1/EGFP mice: 0.5 micromolar TTX in the left eye and saline in the right, followed 4-5 h later by distinct CTB tracers; selected dLGN regions analyzed at P5.

nodes.name: Vagal input labeling from Dbh-cre cNST
nodes.shortDescription: The reported monosynaptic retrograde labeling co-localizes with Calca or Trpa1 transcripts in nodose neurons, supporting an anatomical input interpretation. Conflicting reporter and quantitative caption labels remain unresolved; no numerical tracing fraction or functional coupling weight is assigned.

nodes.name: Reduced cNST calcium after vagotomy
nodes.shortDescription: The separately vagotomized group showed lower LPS-evoked cNST calcium-response area than intact animals. The published figure reports an approximately 80% reduction with residual signal; it does not demonstrate complete elimination of every immune-to-brain route.

nodes.name: Subdiaphragmatic vagotomy and LPS
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral vagal transection with two weeks of recovery, compared with the intact LPS photometry group; six mice per group.

nodes.name: Cytokine nulls after Vgat-cre cNST activation
nodes.shortDescription: The specified Vgat-cre cNST activation experiment reported nonsignificant IL-6, IL-1beta and IL-10 differences after LPS, with four treated and five control mice. This does not establish that all inhibitory neurons are irrelevant to immune regulation.

nodes.name: Analysis-dependent regional detection times
nodes.shortDescription: With the main 100 ms smoothing procedure, conventional-band contrasts are reported at 120-310 ms for AI beta, 180-320 ms for ACC beta, 370-470 ms for amygdala beta, and 60-340 plus 380-470 ms for IFG high gamma.

nodes.name: Classifier performance after ordered feature removal
nodes.shortDescription: The paper reports 76.28 percent classification accuracy using thirteen pooled features. Removing any one feature retains above-chance decoding; sequentially removing the eight highest-weight features leaves reported accuracy 49.78 percent with P=0.617. The saved removal array ends at 49.775 percent.

nodes.name: Proposed neurodynamic organization of pain empathy
nodes.shortDescription: Tan et al. propose a multi-region neurodynamic account linking early IFG activity, regional low-frequency changes and cross-region coupling during vicarious pain perception. Its interpretation as a necessary or minimal empathy architecture remains unresolved.

nodes.name: Cross-region phase-amplitude associations
nodes.shortDescription: Painful pictures produce reported increases in coupling between IFG high-gamma amplitude and selected beta phases in ACC, AI and amygdala, with an additional AI alpha-phase cluster. The main analysis uses 219 ACC-IFG, 459 AI-IFG and 254 amygdala-IFG channel pairs.

nodes.name: Frequency-specific interregional power correlations
nodes.shortDescription: The main analysis reports reduced ACC-AI beta power correlation at 25-32 Hz and AI-amygdala correlation at 18-24 Hz. ACC-amygdala correlation increases at 18-22 Hz and decreases at 25-30 Hz.

nodes.name: Distinct pain, unpleasantness and empathy ratings
nodes.shortDescription: In the sixteen-rater subset, stronger empathy ratings associate with lower ACC alpha and AI low-frequency power differences. Perceived pain and own unpleasantness have distinct associations: AI coefficients are negative for perceived pain and positive for own unpleasantness; the ACC unpleasantness association is nonsignificant.

nodes.name: Picture-related regional iEEG power contrasts
nodes.shortDescription: Painful versus neutral hand pictures elicit reported AI low-frequency power decreases, ACC alpha decreases and beta increases, amygdala beta decreases and IFG high-gamma increases. The main sample contains 297 channels across four overlapping regional patient subsets.

nodes.name: Directional transfer-entropy associations
nodes.shortDescription: The reported beta-power transfer-entropy analysis finds lower ACC-AI values during painful pictures and a direction-by-condition interaction for AI-amygdala. The latter includes an amygdala-to-AI decrease, while AI-to-amygdala has P=0.629. ACC-amygdala effects depend on the beta frequency range.

nodes.name: VIP manipulation and RGL cycle-marker nulls
nodes.shortDescription: The tested five-day VIP-interneuron activation and inhibition comparisons show no significant change in the RGL EdU/MCM2 endpoints. The selected slice controls do not establish that VIP neurons never affect RGLs through other routes or conditions.

nodes.name: Exploratory interareal amplitude-connectivity results
nodes.shortDescription: Exploratory amplitude-based connectivity after removal of the evoked response showed brief content-selective effects differing from the phase-consistency result.

nodes.name: Stimulus-duration neural readouts
nodes.shortDescription: Some posterior iEEG responses track stimulus duration; the preregistered prefrontal onset-and-offset profile was not detected in the reported analysis.

nodes.name: Suprathreshold visual feature decoding
nodes.shortDescription: Suprathreshold feature decoding differs by cortical region, feature and recording modality; category decoding and orientation decoding are not interchangeable.

nodes.name: Visual reliability and height-conflict protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Two-interval height discrimination; aligned stereo and PHANToM haptic stimuli; randomized visual noise and small cue discrepancies; no feedback.

nodes.name: Prespecified interareal phase-consistency results
nodes.shortDescription: The preregistered phase-consistency readout did not support either theory's specified gamma/beta connectivity prediction under the reported analysis.

nodes.name: Learned selective-updating hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Dopamine-dependent gating and reinforcement are proposed to admit task-relevant context into maintained representations and learn when updating is useful. This sketches a possible mechanism for adaptable control; it does not demonstrate a measured closed feedback loop or an exclusive dopamine mediator.

nodes.name: Functional requirements of guided control
nodes.shortDescription: Within Miller and Cohen's theory, guided control requires task-relevant bias, maintenance robust to distraction with selective updating, access to diverse task information and plasticity for learning new goals and means. These requirements define what a candidate model must demonstrate.

nodes.name: Selected macaque visual-memory preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Two macaques supplied 145 prescreened task-responsive PF units from 264 screened units during visual delayed matching. Standard and ABBA task experience differs between animals; ABBA repeats an irrelevant nonmatch while preserving the sample as the final target.

nodes.name: Post-pulse category evidence across task relevance
nodes.shortDescription: In the separate six-person Experiment 3, unattended-category decoding exceeds chance after the first cue, when the item can still matter. After the second cue, when that item is dropped, the corresponding decoding result is nonsignificant.

nodes.name: Category decoding after targeted TMS
nodes.shortDescription: In Experiment 2, unattended-category EEG decoding transiently exceeds chance after TMS. Targeted and nontargeted category conditions both show reported above-chance evidence; the data do not by themselves demonstrate an exclusive target-specific storage site.

nodes.name: Distinct episodic-buffer hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A limited temporary store binding information across modalities and long-term memory is proposed as an episodic buffer. A distinct store versus activated long-term memory remains a mechanistic alternative, and functional binding does not identify a physical buffer or establish consciousness.

nodes.name: Priority-dependent category evidence in fMRI
nodes.shortDescription: In Experiment 1, fMRI category evidence follows the cued item. Evidence for the unattended category approaches absent-category levels and can return after a priority switch. This reports a category-level BOLD readout.

nodes.name: Global evoked metrics do not separate attention states
nodes.shortDescription: Supplementary Figure S6 and Table S1 report no significant attention-state main effects or interactions for significant current density, significant current scatter and perturbational complexity in the category-targeted TMS-EEG preparation.

nodes.name: Latent synaptic storage hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A latent synaptic trace is one proposed account of information that remains potentially accessible when current category decoding is weak. Category-context reinstatement, weak active codes and distributed or dynamic carriers remain alternatives to a uniquely silent synaptic store.

nodes.name: Unattended-item lure errors across TMS groups
nodes.shortDescription: Experiment 4 reports more first-probe unattended-item false alarms in the TMS group than the separate no-TMS group. The corresponding second-probe comparison is nonsignificant. The effect concerns recognition behavior, not EEG recovery of a particular memory item.

nodes.name: Multicomponent working-memory vocabulary
nodes.shortDescription: Baddeley distinguishes phonological storage and rehearsal, visuospatial storage, attentional control by a central executive and a proposed episodic buffer. These are functional model components, not disjoint cell populations or a one-to-one anatomical partition.

nodes.name: Continuous diversity of PF delay profiles
nodes.shortDescription: PF delay activity includes increasing, decreasing and flatter temporal profiles. Within-interval and across-interval indices vary continuously; the illustrated profiles do not establish separate biological cell classes.

nodes.name: PF sample selectivity between distractors
nodes.shortDescription: Forty selected PF units show sample-dependent delay firing; best/worst selectivity reappears between intervening test stimuli. Stimulus-evoked activity interrupts delay firing. Reported six-way classification averages 20.8% against 16.7% chance after excluding the first delay.

nodes.name: PFC guided-activation hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Maintained prefrontal goal and rule representations are proposed to bias processing in other systems. Control is modulatory: the stimulus-to-response path need not pass through PFC, and modeled inhibition can arise through local competition rather than a direct inhibitory PFC command.

nodes.name: PF and IT delay readouts under interference
nodes.shortDescription: Selected PF units preserve a best/worst sample difference across the tested blank intervals, while the selected IT average in Figure 7 distinguishes samples only in the interval used for ranking. IT match responses can still carry prior-sample information after intervening stimuli.

nodes.name: PF enhancement for the remembered match
nodes.shortDescription: Excitatory PF responses can be enhanced for the sample-matching test while repeated irrelevant nonmatches do not produce the same enhancement profile. Enhancement begins before the bar release in the reported response traces.

nodes.name: PF suppression for matching and irrelevant repeats
nodes.shortDescription: A separate response pattern suppresses firing for the remembered match and for a repeated irrelevant nonmatch. Repetition suppression and match enhancement therefore have different selectivity in the ABBA task.

nodes.name: Pooled recognition comparison without a TMS main effect
nodes.shortDescription: Supplementary Figure S4 reports no significant TMS main effect on recognition accuracy in a pooled comparison of twelve TMS participants and twenty-four no-TMS participants; probe and switching demands affect accuracy.

nodes.name: Working-memory task construct
nodes.shortDescription: Working memory denotes temporary retention and use of information during a specified task. A graph instance must identify the material, delay, distraction, required transformation and behavioral readout; storage span, processing demands and executive control are distinct measurements.

nodes.name: Bulk absorption coefficient
nodes.shortDescription: A length-reciprocal coefficient, distinguished from dimensionless flux fractions and from a microscopic carrier count.

nodes.name: Directional reflectance distribution
nodes.shortDescription: A radiometric density under stated geometry and ray-optics assumptions, distinct from a reflected flux fraction.

nodes.name: Measured transmission of IR windows
nodes.shortDescription: Transmitted-light measurements for the stated window samples; not a general channel operator or a complete field reconstruction.

nodes.name: IR sample and measurement boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Incident beam, specified sample and integrating-sphere collection protocol; not an additional generating physical entity.

nodes.name: Measured response of specular IR samples
nodes.shortDescription: Aggregate reflected-light response in the specified Hanssen preparation; no complete directional scattering law is inferred.

nodes.name: Reported pure-water absorption spectrum
nodes.shortDescription: A publication-scoped absorption observation with an explicit unresolved precision dispute.

nodes.name: Conditional atomic-reference calibration
nodes.shortDescription: Adopt the quoted external 199Hg atomic frequency-per-field magnitude and multiply it by the corrected PSI ratio; preserve its shielded-proton-in-water reference chain and the distinct alternative calibration direction.

nodes.name: Adopted mercury atomic reference
nodes.shortDescription: For the absolute conversion, Afach Equation 2 adopts gamma_Hg/(2*pi)=7.590118(13) MHz/T from an external Hg-to-shielded-proton-in-water calibration and reference value. This is a quoted input, not a new PSI measurement of that absolute reference.

nodes.name: Conditional neutron frequency-per-field magnitude
nodes.shortDescription: Multiplying the corrected PSI ratio by the adopted Hg atomic reference gives the published |gamma_n|/(2*pi)=29.164705(55) MHz/T. The absolute scale therefore depends on the external reference as well as the measured ratio.

nodes.name: PSI neutron/mercury precession preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Store polarized UCN and 199Hg atoms together, fit neutron Ramsey fringes against the optically read mercury frequency, and correct the selected field-up/down data for unequal field sampling and frequency shifts.

nodes.name: Corrected neutron/mercury ratio
nodes.shortDescription: The selected PSI analysis reports the positive neutron/199Hg frequency-ratio magnitude 3.8424574(30), or 0.78 ppm relative uncertainty, after the stated corrections. The final uncertainty is the larger of the field-up and field-down errors.

nodes.name: Replayed AlphaGamma calibration arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: The printed thesis inputs give a weighted activity of 23545.129016... per second and uncorrelated uncertainty 4.421378... per second. The body common-error convention gives 6.99106... per second total uncertainty; the Appendix B fraction gives 4.45442... . Displayed-input rounding permits values rounding to the reported mean. The 2018 printed activity quotient is 23540.204... per second, inconsistent with the reported center even under display rounding; Equation 12-derived target corrections agree only within their quoted uncertainty.

nodes.name: Printed AlphaGamma arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Evaluate the ideal rate-transfer identity, printed thesis source-activity combination and rounding envelope, 2018 printed activity quotient and Equation 12-derived target corrections, retaining conflicting source conventions.

nodes.name: Absolute neutron count-rate transfer
nodes.shortDescription: In the ideal AlphaGamma transfer, a calibrated alpha source fixes Omega_AG=r_Pu,AG/R_Pu. A thin boron target transfers that calibration to the gamma response, giving R_n=r_gamma,thick*r_alpha,thin/(r_gamma,thin*Omega_AG) for the totally absorbing target.

nodes.name: Asymptotic freedom in the perturbative domain
nodes.shortDescription: When b0>0, the zero-coupling fixed point is ultraviolet attractive for sufficiently small positive coupling. At fixed flavor number, the one-loop solution alpha_s(mu_R^2)=1/[b0 ln(mu_R^2/Lambda^2)] tends to zero as mu_R grows without bound.

nodes.name: ATLAS 2011-2012 search acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the ATLAS pp data at 7 TeV in 2011 and 8 TeV in April-June 2012, with channel luminosities 4.6-4.8 and 5.8-5.9 fb^-1. Apply channel-specific lepton/photon triggers, object reconstruction, isolation, jet and missing-momentum selections.

nodes.name: ATLAS historical neutral-boson mass fit
nodes.shortDescription: Using the four-lepton and diphoton channels with independently varying signal strengths, ATLAS reports a mass of 126.0 +/-0.4 statistical +/-0.4 systematic GeV for the new particle. This is the original 2012 fit result.

nodes.name: ATLAS historical combined excess and strength
nodes.shortDescription: The full published combination reports local significance 5.9 standard deviations (p0=1.7e-9), and global significance about 5.1 (p0=1.7e-7) over 110-600 GeV. At mH=126 GeV the fitted common signal strength relative to the Standard Model is 1.4 +/-0.3.

nodes.name: ATLAS selected diphoton candidates
nodes.shortDescription: The selected diphoton samples contain 23788 candidates at 7 TeV and 35251 at 8 TeV in 100-160 GeV, divided into ten categories per energy. Figure 4 shows inclusive and model-weighted views with fitted background residuals of these same samples.

nodes.name: ATLAS selected four-lepton candidates
nodes.shortDescription: The reanalysed 7 TeV and new 8 TeV four-lepton selections give the Figure 2 invariant-mass spectrum. In the Table 3 window 120-130 GeV, the reported observed counts are 6 four-muon, 5 mixed-electron/muon and 2 four-electron candidates; modeled signal and backgrounds are separate.

nodes.name: ATLAS 2012 limited Higgs compatibility
nodes.shortDescription: The reported channels support a new neutral boson compatible with the Standard Model Higgs production/decay hypothesis. Diphoton observation disfavors spin one; the paper explicitly requires more information to determine the particle nature in detail.

nodes.name: ATLAS original likelihood and combination
nodes.shortDescription: Profile the stated signal/background likelihood with correlated nuisance parameters. Diphotons use unbinned category likelihoods; WW uses transverse-mass bins for 0/1 jet and an integrated 2-jet contribution. The full Table 6 combination also imports earlier 7 TeV channels, while the mass fit selects the four-lepton and diphoton channels only.

nodes.name: ATLAS response and background conditions
nodes.shortDescription: Use simulated signal acceptance and mass response with data calibration/control corrections; constrain reducible and WW/top backgrounds through the stated control regions and diphoton backgrounds through category-specific mass fits. Retain control-transfer and shared calibration dependence.

nodes.name: ATLAS selected opposite-flavor transverse mass
nodes.shortDescription: The 8 TeV opposite-flavor dilepton selection supplies the Figure 6 transverse-mass distribution. Table 5 separately reports 185,38,0 observed events in the 0-,1-,2-jet categories after its extra mass window; the search likelihood uses a different mT selection.

nodes.name: Correlated atomic-mass fit
nodes.shortDescription: Atomic masses and their differences are inferred from a jointly constrained comparison network. Uncertainty in D-H depends on the covariance as well as both marginal mass errors.

nodes.name: Bali conditional static-energy avoided crossing
nodes.shortDescription: The two-state fit gives an avoided crossing, with the lower energy approaching the two-static-light-meson threshold over the measured range. A quadratic gap fit reports r_c/a=15.00(8) and a*DeltaE_c=0.0217(9); physical-unit conversion and uncertainties retain their declared scale and ensemble.

nodes.name: Bali static string/two-meson correlators
nodes.shortDescription: The study estimates the string, two-meson and cross-channel Euclidean correlators in the shared two-flavor ensemble. The nonzero mixing channel and operator overlaps support a joint spectral analysis.

nodes.name: Bali conditional Euclidean mixing coupling
nodes.shortDescription: The fitted energy gap and mixing angle determine g=DeltaE*sin(2*theta)/2 in the chosen two-state basis. This energy-dimension coupling describes mixing and Euclidean relaxation; real-time evolution of the closed two-state model is oscillatory.

nodes.name: Bali Wilson-loop-only string-breaking null
nodes.shortDescription: At separations beyond the fitted string-breaking region, the Wilson-loop-only data at t<=9a show no visible departure toward the lower two-meson threshold. The full operator matrix is needed to resolve the reported spectrum.

nodes.name: Bali two-flavor static-source computational context
nodes.shortDescription: Four-dimensional Euclidean SU(3) lattice gauge theory with two mass-degenerate Wilson sea quarks, external static sources and the I=0 string/two-meson sector. The 24^3 x 40 ensemble uses beta=5.6, kappa=0.1575 and r0/a=6.009(53); choosing r0=0.5 fm gives a approximately 0.083 fm. The sea-quark mass is slightly below the physical strange-quark mass.

nodes.name: Barnes kaon bubble-chamber acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Expose the BNL 80-inch hydrogen bubble chamber to a mass-separated 5 GeV/c K- beam. The report describes about 100000 pictures and roughly 10^6 feet of kaon tracks, partially analyzed for characteristic Omega decays; this admission concerns its one selected event.

nodes.name: Barnes reconstructed neutral cascade
nodes.shortDescription: Under the stated assignments the report finds a Lambda-compatible p+pi- mass of 1116 +/- 2 MeV/c^2, a two-photon mass of 135.1 +/- 1.5 MeV/c^2, and a neutral Xi-compatible mass of 1316 +/- 4 MeV/c^2. Shared vertex geometry and transverse balance support the proposed Xi0+pi- parent decay.

nodes.name: Barnes conditional Omega identification
nodes.shortDescription: The report conditionally identifies particle 3 with Omega- from Q=-1, inferred S=-3 and reconstructed mass 1686 +/- 12 MeV/c^2, with a production missing mass of 500 +/- 25 MeV/c^2 compatible with K0. The quoted event proper decay time is 0.7e-10 s; no spin/parity or ensemble-lifetime determination is supplied.

nodes.name: Barnes cascade reconstruction assumptions
nodes.shortDescription: Associate the fitted Lambda, two converted photons and the displaced neutral trajectory under Equation 1; use particle-mass hypotheses, transverse balance, production missing mass and alternative-channel tests to interpret the same event.

nodes.name: Barnes selected event track observations
nodes.shortDescription: The selected event has charged-track directions and momenta listed in Table I, gap-density particle-identification information, displaced vertices and two photon conversions shown in Figure 2. These measured inputs precede the neutral cascade and parent-mass interpretation.

nodes.name: First-order baryon-octet mass relation
nodes.shortDescription: Gell-Mann Equation 8.1 states (m_N+m_Xi)/2=(3*m_Lambda+m_Sigma)/4 to first order in unitary-symmetry violation for the baryon octet with common spin and parity. This is a supplied approximate mass relation, not exact equality of all measured masses.

nodes.name: Beam neutron-decay count ratio
nodes.shortDescription: In the ideal corrected beam model, R_p=epsilon_p*N_n/tau and R_monitor=epsilon_0*v_0*N_n/L, so tau=L*epsilon_p*R_monitor/(epsilon_0*v_0*R_p). R_p counts detected proton-producing decays, and epsilon_0 is the monitor efficiency at the reference speed v_0.

nodes.name: Replayed beam calibration arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Equation 1 converts the printed monitor response to 3.109827...e-5. With the adopted zero drifts, the central efficiency-ratio rescaling gives 887.725... seconds, a +1.425... second shift. Diagonal quadrature of the five printed Table II entries gives 2.32379... seconds, rounding to 2.3.

nodes.name: Printed beam calibration arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Evaluate the Equation 1 thermal conversion, Equation 4 central lifetime rescaling with adopted zero drifts, and diagonal quadrature of the five rounded Table II uncertainty components.

nodes.name: Checked MAMI table identities and fit-census mismatch
nodes.shortDescription: The bound tables contain 1422 cross-section rows, 77 unconstrained plus four constrained Rosenbluth entries and 1000 spline evaluations. GE/(GM/mu_p) reproduces the tabulated normalized ratio within 1e-11. Nine Table IV rows admit their displayed reduced chi-square under rounding; the Friedrich-Walcher row does not.

nodes.name: Bound MAMI table verification
nodes.shortDescription: Parse the bound author tables under their distinct column conventions; check counts, shared-factor coverage, form-factor ratio identities and rounded Table IV arithmetic.

nodes.name: MAMI proton elastic-scattering acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Measure unpolarized electron scattering on liquid hydrogen at six beam energies with the three A1 spectrometers; extract acceptance-modeled ratios with the declared radiation, luminosity and normalization treatment.

nodes.name: MAMI-only fitted electric and magnetic form factors
nodes.shortDescription: The selected Mainz-only spline table gives GE, GM/mu_p and mu_p*GE/GM on 1000 Q^2 grid points from 0 to 0.998001 GeV^2, with separate pointwise bands. These are fitted elastic-response quantities conditional on shared normalization and the stated correction model.

nodes.name: MAMI-only Sachs form-factor fit
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the reused MAMI cross-section ratios with the published Mainz-only models and shared normalization parameters, retaining squared-form-factor response, scaled errors and correction assumptions.

nodes.name: MAMI extracted elastic cross-section ratios
nodes.shortDescription: The bound MAMI table contains 1422 cross-section ratios at six incident energies from 180 to 855 MeV, with acceptance-averaged Q^2 from 0.003839 to 0.977245 GeV^2. The ratios already use the spline normalization and scaled point errors.

nodes.name: MAMI dependent Rosenbluth separation
nodes.shortDescription: Reuse the spline-fit normalization and project the same acceptance-averaged cross sections to fixed Q^2 values before the epsilon-linear separation; retain unconstrained results and constrained alternatives separately.

nodes.name: MAMI dependent separated form factors
nodes.shortDescription: The bound Rosenbluth table reports 77 unconstrained GE/GM pairs over Q^2=0.0152-0.5524 GeV^2, plus four low-Q^2 GE alternatives constrained by GM/(mu_p*G_dipole)=1 or 1.05. The separation uses the same acquisition and spline-fit normalization.

nodes.name: Bethe approximate radiative-shift model
nodes.shortDescription: Bethe subtracts the free-electron electromagnetic mass contribution from the bound-electron self-energy. With an assumed cutoff K approximately m c^2, the nonrelativistic model estimates the hydrogen 2S shift as about 1040 MHz.

nodes.name: Binding-energy conversion inputs
nodes.shortDescription: Kessler converts the reciprocal recoil-corrected wavelength using 1.331025045(11)e-15 u per inverse meter or 1.239841870(54)e-6 eV per inverse meter. These are adopted 1999 conversion constants with uncertainties.

nodes.name: Bipartite quantum entanglement
nodes.shortDescription: Relative to H_A tensor H_B, a state is separable if rho = sum_i p_i rho_A_i tensor rho_B_i with p_i >= 0 and sum_i p_i = 1; otherwise it is entangled. For a pure state, separability reduces to factorization.

nodes.name: Bipartite quantum state
nodes.shortDescription: A finite bipartite quantum state is a positive, unit-trace density operator on a declared tensor product H_A tensor H_B. A product state has the form rho_A tensor rho_B.

nodes.name: Experiment-constrained nucleon component ratio
nodes.shortDescription: After additionally using the experimental neutron-proton mass difference, Borsanyi reports (M_n-M_p)_QCD/(M_n-M_p)_QED=-2.49+/-0.23 (statistical) +/-0.29 (systematic). This is a dimensionless, convention-dependent calibrated inference.

nodes.name: Physical-point isospin mass splittings
nodes.shortDescription: Table 1 reports total splittings in MeV with statistical then systematic uncertainties: n-p 1.51(16)(23); Sigma--Sigma+ 8.09(16)(11); Xi--Xi0 6.66(11)(09); D+-D0 4.68(10)(13); Xi_cc++-Xi_cc+ 2.16(11)(17); Coleman-Glashow combination Delta_N-Delta_Sigma+Delta_Xi 0.00(11)(06). The neutron-proton total is 1.51+/-0.16 (statistical) +/-0.23 (systematic) MeV.

nodes.name: Kaon finite-volume response
nodes.shortDescription: For the four enhanced-coupling volumes, Figure 1 reports chi^2/dof=0.86 for the neutral-kaon constant fit and 0.90 for the squared-mass-difference fit with a free 1/L^3 term. The leading 1/L and 1/L^2 terms alone do not describe all four mass-difference points.

nodes.name: Correlated lattice mass-difference fits
nodes.shortDescription: The paper extracts finite-lattice mass differences by fitting Euclidean correlators of isospin partners jointly. Ensemble fit-quality distributions and the selected time windows precede physical-point and cutoff extrapolations.

nodes.name: Convention-dependent isospin components
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected convention, Table 1 gives QCD and QED components in MeV, with statistical then systematic uncertainties: n-p 2.52(17)(24) and -1.00(07)(14); Sigma--Sigma+ 8.09(16)(11) and 0 by convention; Xi--Xi0 5.53(17)(17) and 1.14(16)(09); D+-D0 2.54(08)(10) and 2.14(11)(07); Xi_cc++-Xi_cc+ -2.53(11)(06) and 4.69(10)(17); Coleman-Glashow -0.00(13)(05) and 0.00(06)(02). Equation S38 gives the electromagnetic kaon squared-mass contribution -2250(80)(90) MeV^2.

nodes.name: Enhanced-coupling kaon volume scan
nodes.shortDescription: Four Table S4 ensembles at beta=3.2, bare e=1.00, a*m_u=-0.0859, a*m_d=-0.0792 and a*m_s=-0.0522: L^3*T=24^3*48, 32^3*64, 48^3*96 and 80^3*64. The rounded pion masses are 292, 290, 290 and 289 MeV. The common lattice spacing is about 0.102 fm; Figure 1 describes M_K0 as about 450 MeV.

nodes.name: Four-flavor isospin-breaking ensemble
nodes.shortDescription: Dynamical 1+1+1+1-flavor QCD+QED with tree-level Symanzik gluon action, clover-improved Wilson quarks, three HEX gluon-smearing steps and one APE photon-smearing step. The QED_L prescription, 27 neutral and 14 charged ensembles, four overall lattice spacings and declared mass/charge inputs define the production analysis.

nodes.name: Calibrated diffraction wavelength
nodes.shortDescription: For the first-order angle used by Kessler, lambda_gamma=2*d220*(1-epsilon*p)*sin(theta), with d220 the vacuum spacing at 22.5 C and pressure p in atmospheres. The angle and crystal scale are separate inputs.

nodes.name: Conditional parallel-plate force coefficient
nodes.shortDescription: The main nine-point fit gives C_Cas=(2.34 +/- 0.34) x 10^-28 Hz^2 m^5 and K_C=(1.22 +/- 0.18) x 10^-27 N m^2 through K_C=epsilon0 C_Cas/(4 C_el). Agreement with ideal pressure is conditional on calibration and the declared fit.

nodes.name: Parallel-surface residual frequency shift
nodes.shortDescription: After electrostatic subtraction, the reported squared-frequency shift decreases toward smaller gaps. The readout is a force-gradient-dependent resonance shift, not a direct pressure sensor.

nodes.name: Parallel-surface frequency preparation
nodes.shortDescription: A chromium-coated silicon cantilever faces a rigid coated beam, overlapping 1.2 by 1.2 mm. Interferometry reads the torsional resonance; electrostatic sweeps calibrate gap and residual voltage.

nodes.name: Capture photon and nuclear recoil
nodes.shortDescription: For capture by an approximately stationary proton, the binding energy includes the measured photon energy and the recoiling deuteron kinetic energy. The leading correction is E_gamma^2/(2*m_d*c^2).

nodes.name: Material-dependent Casimir interaction
nodes.shortDescription: A Casimir interaction can be calculated from electromagnetic response and coupling to material sources. Ideal conducting boundaries are a limiting approximation; the external-source formulation does not require an independently measured absolute zero-point energy.

nodes.name: Charged-fermion mass and Higgs coupling convention
nodes.shortDescription: For each supplied charged-fermion mass m_i in the declared mass basis, the tree-level term is -m_i*psi-bar_i*psi_i-(m_i/v)*H*psi-bar_i*psi_i. Defining y_i=sqrt(2)*m_i/v gives m_i=y_i*v/sqrt(2) and the one-Higgs coefficient y_i/sqrt(2)=m_i/v. This reparametrizes independent mass/Yukawa inputs; it does not calculate their numerical hierarchy.

nodes.name: CHSH local hidden-variable model
nodes.shortDescription: With binary outcomes, local responses and a hidden-variable distribution independent of measurement settings, S = E00 + E01 + E10 - E11 obeys |S| <= 2. Stochastic local responses are convex mixtures of deterministic ones.

nodes.name: CMS conditional strong-coupling extraction
nodes.shortDescription: The NNPDF2.1-based fit to R32 over Q=420-1390 GeV gives alpha_s(M_Z)=0.1148 +/- 0.0014 (experimental) +/- 0.0018 (PDF) +/- 0.0050 (theory), with chi^2/dof=22.0/20. The paper combines these uncertainties in quadrature to report 0.1148 +/- 0.0055.

nodes.name: CMS unfolded inclusive-jet ratio
nodes.shortDescription: CMS reports the ratio of inclusive three-jet to inclusive two-jet event yields, unfolded to stable-particle level, over Q=250-1390 GeV. R32 rises as third-jet phase space opens, forms a plateau around 600-1000 GeV and falls at higher Q.

nodes.name: CMS conditional running-coupling comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The three fitted scale regions give alpha_s(Q)=0.0936 +/- 0.0041 at 474 GeV, 0.0894 +/- 0.0031 at 664 GeV and 0.0889 +/- 0.0034 at 896 GeV. These total-uncertainty results, converted with the specified three-loop RGE, are reported as compatible with its scale dependence.

nodes.name: CMS inclusive-jet ratio preparation
nodes.shortDescription: CMS 2011 proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=7 TeV. The trigger samples have effective luminosities 0.15, 0.51 and 5.0 fb^-1 for HLT thresholds 190, 240 and 370 GeV. Particle-flow reconstruction and anti-kT R=0.7 define selected jets; both leading jets must have |y|<2.5 and selected jets require pT>150 GeV.

nodes.name: CMS 2016 tau-pair acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Select the 2016 CMS pp exposure at 13 TeV, 35.9 fb^-1, into tau_h tau_h, mu-tau_h, e-tau_h and e-mu final states with exclusive 0-jet, VBF and boosted categories; apply the stated triggers, object, isolation and charge selections.

nodes.name: CMS reported common-coupling compatibility
nodes.shortDescription: CMS Figure 22 reports contours compatible with the Standard Model point (kappa_V,kappa_f)=(1,1) under the authors' implemented model. This is a conditional interpretation of the same 2016 data with a common fermion modifier, not a separately measured tau Yukawa or a new acquisition.

nodes.name: CMS common-coupling scan conditions
nodes.shortDescription: Reuse the 2016 selections in the reported common kappa_V/kappa_f scan at mH=125.09 GeV, profile the nuisance parameters, and now include H-to-WW as signal. The cited CMS method and generic coupling framework delimit this interpretation without specifying a complete experiment-specific width/loop map.

nodes.name: CMS same-fit sensitive-bin summaries
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 18 regroups observed bins by the expected S/(S+B); Figure 19 displays S/(S+B)-weighted reconstructed-mass summaries of the same data and fitted components. In Table 4, the log10(S/(S+B))>-0.9 subset contains observed counts 11,54,91,207 for e-mu, e-tau_h, mu-tau_h and tau_h tau_h; expected component counts and totals remain reported post-fit quantities.

nodes.name: CMS original tau-rate likelihood
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the selected category bins and control regions jointly with a common H-to-tau-tau signal strength at the adopted mass 125.09 GeV. Profile yield/shape and template-bin nuisances with their stated correlations; treat H-to-WW as background for this rate and significance inference.

nodes.name: CMS 2016 tau-rate and local excess
nodes.shortDescription: For the 2016-only analysis at fixed mH=125.09 GeV, CMS reports mu=1.09 (+0.27/-0.26) relative to the Standard Model tau-pair rate, with local observed significance 4.9 and expected significance 4.7 standard deviations.

nodes.name: CMS tau response and control transfers
nodes.shortDescription: Apply simulated templates with data-constrained tau/object and missing-momentum response; use Drell–Yan, W+jets, QCD and top control regions with their stated transfer assumptions and shared nuisance constraints. Preserve the partial overlap of tau energy-scale calibration and search selections.

nodes.name: CMS selected tau-decay distributions
nodes.shortDescription: The selected data points in Figures 6–17 give channel/category reconstructed distributions for the 2016 exposure. The tau_h tau_h 0-jet input is one-dimensional; the remaining category inputs are two-dimensional. Simulated signal/background components and post-fit overlays are distinct from these observed bins.

nodes.name: Neutron mass and ILL calibration constraint
nodes.shortDescription: CODATA uses dimensionless eta_d=2.90430245(49)e-3 to connect neutron mass, recoil and d220(ILL). Because neutron mass occurs in no other observational equation, this datum does not independently constrain the ILL lattice spacing.

nodes.name: CODATA selected light-ion ratio inputs
nodes.shortDescription: CODATA D15-D18 use 0.503776367670(17), 1.0070527379117(85), 0.9992316600030(43) and 1.0073102639050(200), respectively. Their observational equations retain ionic charge factors, molecular binding and shared mass references.

nodes.name: Unresolved ILL calibration input identity
nodes.shortDescription: CODATA 2018 and 2022 label E13 as ILL/W04 minus one, -20(22)e-9. The cited Kessler tables assign the negative -20(9)e-9 comparison to WS1/NW04 and report different ILL comparisons. The physical identity of E13 has not been reconciled.

nodes.name: Shared carbon ionization inputs
nodes.shortDescription: CODATA Table XXVI correlates the carbon ionization inputs D8/D23, D8/D24 and D23/D24 by 0.9968, 1.0000 and 0.9968. The D15 and D16 equations share the C6+ denominator.

nodes.name: CODATA capture and lattice constraints
nodes.shortDescription: Trace the dimensionless capture input and published lattice comparisons through their observational equations, without reproducing the full adjustment.

nodes.name: CODATA light-ion mass constraints
nodes.shortDescription: Use the selected 2022 adjustment input ratios and observational equations, with explicit shared ionic references and theoretical binding inputs.

nodes.name: Simultaneous coupled-ion frequency readout
nodes.shortDescription: Two ions in coupled magnetron orbits can share a simultaneous phase readout, but obtaining the free cyclotron ratio still requires the trap and interaction model.

nodes.name: Creutz conditional lattice scaling comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The fitted area coefficients show a crossover near beta=2 and a decrease compatible with the leading SU(2) asymptotic-freedom slope under fixed-string-tension renormalization. This is evidence within the finite pure-gauge model.

nodes.name: Creutz conditional string-tension fit
nodes.shortDescription: A constant-plus-perimeter-plus-area fit to finite square loops yields a dimensionless coefficient interpreted as a^2 K. Strong-coupling points require reduced fit assumptions, and above beta=2.5 the area contribution is not accurately resolved.

nodes.name: Creutz simulated square-loop expectations
nodes.shortDescription: The study reports square Wilson-loop expectations across bare couplings and lattice sizes. At beta=3, loops through side five appear stable against the tested size increase to 10^4 sites; larger loops show stronger finite-size effects.

nodes.name: Creutz pure SU(2) computational context
