nodes.shortDescription: One HD+/C4+ pair is compared for seven weeks with changed trap voltage to match axial frequencies. The ground rovibrational state is inferred from cryogenic storage and cooling; excitation and polarizability corrections remain.

nodes.name: Joint LIONTRAP and FSU adjustment
nodes.shortDescription: Add the independently acquired FSU deuteron/proton ratio to the LIONTRAP mass constraints. The quoted neutron mass additionally uses the recalibrated capture binding energy.

nodes.name: Local LIONTRAP mass adjustment
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the published 2019 proton mass, direct deuteron mass and HD+ molecular mass balance together, retaining common electronic, molecular and calibration inputs.

nodes.name: Reactor antineutrino coincidence readout
nodes.shortDescription: KamLAND identifies electron-antineutrino candidates through inverse beta decay, antinu_e+p->e-plus+n. The prompt positron kinetic plus annihilation signal is followed by neutron-capture light, normally a 2.2 MeV gamma from hydrogen. The approximate relation E_antineutrino=E_prompt+T_neutron+0.8 MeV uses neutron recoil kinetic energy and a rounded kinematic offset; energy response and delayed-coincidence selection remain explicit.

nodes.name: Hall A polarized-3He preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare polarized electrons and a polarized 3He gas target with N2 admixture; measure coincidence helicity yields and beam/target polarizations, then form the reported charge- and polarization-normalized Ameas.

nodes.name: Measured polarized-3He helicity asymmetries
nodes.shortDescription: Table II reports Ameas=-0.136, -0.134 and -0.098 at acceptance-mean Q2=1.72, 2.48 and 3.41 GeV2, after the Equation 1 charge and beam/target polarization normalization. Corrected Aen endpoints are a separate computational outcome.

nodes.name: Corrected neutron-asymmetry endpoints
nodes.shortDescription: Table II reports Aen|exp=-0.188, -0.175 and -0.134 after the stated dilution and background treatment of the same three measured asymmetries. Its intermediate Aphys values are -0.148, -0.145 and -0.109. These are correction stages from the same data; the final endpoints are compared with GEA calculations in the ratio extraction.

nodes.name: Conditional neutron electric response
nodes.shortDescription: Using linearly interpolated Lachniet GMn, Table III reports GE_n=0.0236 +/- 0.0017(stat) +/- 0.0026(syst), 0.0208 +/- 0.0024 +/- 0.0019 and 0.0147 +/- 0.0020 +/- 0.0014 at Q2=1.72, 2.48 and 3.41 GeV2.

nodes.name: Polarized-3He correction and neutron-response extraction
nodes.shortDescription: Apply the declared target, accidental, inelastic and proton-background treatment, compare corrected neutron asymmetries with GEA/AV18 calculations, and convert the inferred normalized ratio to GE using external linearly interpolated CLAS GMn.

nodes.name: Inferred normalized neutron Sachs ratios
nodes.shortDescription: Table III reports gn=mu_n*GE_n/GM_n of 0.273 +/- 0.020(stat) +/- 0.030(syst), 0.412 +/- 0.048 +/- 0.036 and 0.496 +/- 0.067 +/- 0.046 at acceptance-mean Q2=1.72, 2.48 and 3.41 GeV2.

nodes.name: Molecular state inference
nodes.shortDescription: A vibrational or rotational ground-state assignment requires a preparation or readout model. Vibrational v=0 alone does not imply rotational N=0, and waiting for modeled cooling is not direct state certification.

nodes.name: Sachs elastic proton form factors
nodes.shortDescription: For unpolarized elastic electron-proton scattering in the ultrarelativistic one-photon approximation, the reduced cross section is epsilon*GE(Q^2)^2+tau*GM(Q^2)^2, where tau=Q^2/(4*m_p^2). GE(0)=1 and GM(0)=mu_p specify reference normalization; the measured cross section does not determine signs by itself.

nodes.name: Schneider corrected proton magnetic moment
nodes.shortDescription: The Science 2017 abstract reports mu_p/mu_N=2.79284734462+/-0.00000000082. The thesis identifies the same result as 2.79284734462(75)(34), with 68.3 percent statistical and separately stated systematic uncertainty, and total fractional precision 295 ppt.

nodes.name: Schneider 2016 acquisition and spin analysis
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare three single protons sequentially, infer initial/final spin states from analysis-trap axial series, and reconstruct free cyclotron frequencies during precision-trap Larmor excitation. Retain selection and shared noise-model assumptions in the reported statistical resonance estimate.

nodes.name: Schneider moment correction and uncertainty
nodes.shortDescription: Apply the signed preparation-specific corrections to the same campaign statistical center. Keep the linear systematic-bound aggregation separate from the reported statistical uncertainty and final total.

nodes.name: Schneider statistical moment estimate
nodes.shortDescription: The thesis reports the selected-campaign statistical estimate mu_p/mu_N=2.79284734500(75), before systematic correction, from 1264 selected ratios. The quoted 268 ppt statistical precision is a source inference, not an independently reproduced likelihood result.

nodes.name: Full-geometry image-charge prediction
nodes.shortDescription: For LIONTRAP at B0=3.764 T, the full-geometry calculation reports a cyclotron correction 475.4(2.1)(3.6) microhertz per charge state, with numerical and geometry uncertainties. The simplified calculations give 488.416(58) and 488.7(2.1); including electrode gaps changes the prediction.

nodes.name: Scoped image-charge comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Schuh Table I compares the extracted 2.291(126) mHz magnetron difference with 2.377(21) mHz from the geometry calculation. This supports the correction at roughly five-percent experimental precision, while the conversion to the distinct Table II experimental value remains unresolved.

nodes.name: Extracted image-charge difference
nodes.shortDescription: Subtracting the stated ideal, magnetic and tilt/ellipticity contributions gives an image-charge magnetron difference 2.291(61)(111) mHz, or 2.291(126) mHz with combined uncertainty, in Schuh Table I and Equation 23.

nodes.name: Measured magnetron difference
nodes.shortDescription: The dedicated image-charge experiment reports nu_minus(C-12(6+))-nu_minus(p)=393.258(61)(77) mHz after voltage correction. This includes the ideal-trap mass dependence and other apparatus shifts, not only the image-charge contribution.

nodes.name: LIONTRAP electrode-geometry calculation
nodes.shortDescription: COMSOL 5.2 finite-element electrostatics and a semianalytical expansion compare simplified electrode models and full LIONTRAP geometry. Field gradients are inferred from 21 ion positions; a long-cylinder reference and geometry perturbations estimate numerical and manufacturing uncertainty.

nodes.name: LIONTRAP dedicated magnetron experiment
nodes.shortDescription: Alternating single p and C-12(6+) ions undergo a Ramsey-like magnetron measurement with two 4.6 ms pulses and deformed-potential axial readout. The 120 cycles over 23 days use 20 or 40 s precision phase evolution. Voltage and tilt corrections enter the extracted image-charge difference.

nodes.name: Schwinger leading electron magnetic anomaly
nodes.shortDescription: The 1948 letter gives delta_mu/mu=e^2/(2*pi*hbar*c)=0.001162 in its Gaussian-unit convention. With alpha=e^2/(hbar*c) this is the positive leading correction a_e^(1)=alpha/(2*pi), or g/2=1+a_e^(1) at that order, using renormalized experimental mass and charge.

nodes.name: Silicon lattice calibration transfer
nodes.shortDescription: A relative Bragg-angle comparison transfers an absolute lattice-spacing reference to a specified silicon specimen under stated temperature, pressure, impurity and geometry conditions. Shared reference standards retain covariance.

nodes.name: SLAC electron-proton measurement
nodes.shortDescription: The measured electron spectra and stated kinematics define the differential cross-section readout; Figure 1 uses a Mott normalization at fixed recoil mass.

nodes.name: Conditional structure-function scaling
nodes.shortDescription: Under transverse virtual-photon dominance, the extracted nu W2 approximately follows one curve in omega; the abstract states q^2>1 (GeV/c)^2 and omega>4. Figure 2 also explores q^2>0.5 and a separate low-q^2 spectrum. Longitudinal dominance does not give the same collapse.

nodes.name: Deep-inelastic electron spectrum
nodes.shortDescription: In the measured deep continuum, the inelastic differential/Mott ratio varies more slowly with q^2 than the plotted elastic/Mott comparator.

nodes.name: SLD model-dependent momentum extrapolation
nodes.shortDescription: The same measured spectra are integrated with correlated systematic errors, then extrapolated over unmeasured xp using the mean accepted fraction from three specified fragmentation generators. The assigned absolute accepted-fraction uncertainty is 0.01 for K0 and Lambda and 0.015 for K*0 and phi.

nodes.name: SLD inclusive neutral-hadron reconstruction
nodes.shortDescription: SLD uses approximately 150000 hadronic events acquired in 1993-1995. The inclusive event selection retains 90213 events; CRID analyses additionally require detector readiness, leaving 79711. K0S and Lambda use displaced charged vertices; K*0 and phi use charged-pair mass fits with kaon identification. The event denominator is corrected for trigger and selection efficiency.

nodes.name: SLD extrapolated neutral-hadron totals
nodes.shortDescription: Table 16 reports all-flavor full-range totals per hadronic Z0 decay: K0/K0bar 2.01 +/- 0.08, Lambda/Lambdabar 0.395 +/- 0.022, K*0/K*0bar 0.707 +/- 0.041 and phi 0.105 +/- 0.008. The quoted errors combine experimental and model-extrapolation contributions.

nodes.name: SLD measured-range neutral-hadron yields
nodes.shortDescription: Tables 6-7 report corrected differential yields in 44 bins. Measured-range integrals per hadronic Z0 decay are K0/K0bar 1.90 +/- 0.02 +/- 0.07, Lambda/Lambdabar 0.37 +/- 0.01 +/- 0.02, K*0/K*0bar 0.647 +/- 0.022 +/- 0.029 and phi 0.0985 +/- 0.0046 +/- 0.0055, with statistical then systematic errors.

nodes.name: SNO pure-D2O acquisition and selection
nodes.shortDescription: Use the pure-D2O first-phase acquisition from 2 November 1999 to 28 May 2001, with 306.4 live days. Reconstruct effective kinetic energy, radius and solar angle from PMT times and hit patterns. Select Teff from 5 to 20 MeV and radius at most 550 cm; include the additional 250 ms veto after events with more than 60 hit PMTs.

nodes.name: SNO jointly inferred active-flavor components
nodes.shortDescription: The SNO-only direct joint analysis reports electron flux 1.76(+/-0.05 statistical)(+/-0.09 systematic) and non-electron active flux 3.41(+/-0.45 statistical)(+0.48/-0.45 systematic), in units of 10^6 cm^-2 s^-1. Under the stated response and B8-shape assumptions, the article reports the non-electron component 5.3 standard deviations above zero, supporting solar flavor transformation compatible with oscillations.

nodes.name: SNO accepted background estimates
nodes.shortDescription: Table I reports 78 +/- 12 accepted neutron-background events and 45(+18/-12) Cherenkov-background events. These estimates use the stated controls, production locations, response and simulation; they are not additional observed solar-neutrino counts.

nodes.name: SNO channel decomposition and normalization
nodes.shortDescription: Fit CC, ES and NC amplitudes by the reported extended maximum likelihood in Teff, cos(theta_sun) and (R/600 cm)^3. Use simulation templates for the standard B8 shape and centrally fixed background amplitudes from calibration. Repeat the decomposition with perturbed response templates for systematics; normalize channel rates using the stated electron-neutrino cross-section convention.

nodes.name: SNO response-normalized channel fluxes
nodes.shortDescription: In units of 10^6 cm^-2 s^-1, the channel-normalized results are CC 1.76(+0.06/-0.05 statistical)(+/-0.09 systematic), ES 2.39(+0.24/-0.23 statistical)(+/-0.12 systematic), and NC 5.09(+0.44/-0.43 statistical)(+0.46/-0.43 systematic). They use the adopted B8 shape and electron-neutrino cross sections for all three channel normalizations.

nodes.name: SNO fitted channel amplitudes
nodes.shortDescription: The three-channel extended likelihood reports CC 1967.7(+61.9/-60.9), ES 263.6(+26.4/-25.6) and NC 576.5(+49.5/-48.9) events. These are fitted channel-yield parameters; the quoted uncertainties here are statistical.

nodes.name: SNO direct joint active-flavor inference
nodes.shortDescription: Analyze the same selected sample and response model directly in electron and non-electron active-flux variables, assuming the standard B8 shape. Use the joint three-reaction information for the no-flavor-transformation null test. Retain note 13 and the source joint probability contours; this is the SNO-only inference before any external Super-Kamiokande solar-ES constraint.

nodes.name: SNO adopted calibration and response inputs
nodes.shortDescription: Adopt the Cf-252 neutron calibration, N-16 energy calibration and simulation, nuclear cross sections and standard B8 spectral input. Use the separately described in-situ/ex-situ U/Th controls, deployed-source response and simulation to estimate accepted backgrounds. Retain 29.9 +/- 1.1 percent uniform-source neutron capture efficiency and 14.4 percent selected detection efficiency as different response quantities.

nodes.name: SNO selected Cherenkov events
nodes.shortDescription: The stated selection yields 2928 events in the reconstructed 5-20 MeV analysis region and fiducial radius at most 550 cm. Their energy, solar-direction and radial response is the shared input to the reported signal decompositions.

nodes.name: Solar neutrino CC, NC and ES response
nodes.shortDescription: In the stated solar-neutrino weak-response model, nu_e+d->p+p+e-minus is the charged-current channel, nu_x+d->p+n+nu_x is the neutral-current channel and nu_x+e-minus->nu_x+e-minus is elastic scattering. CC is electron-flavor sensitive; NC has equal sensitivity to the three active flavors; ES has reduced muon/tau sensitivity. Reconstructed Cherenkov observables distinguish statistical response templates, not individually labeled incoming flavors.

nodes.name: Standard Model field specification
nodes.shortDescription: The Standard Model specifies SU(3) color, SU(2) weak isospin and U(1) hypercharge gauge interactions, quark and lepton fields, and a scalar Higgs doublet. This is a particular quantum field theory.

nodes.name: Mass uncertainty conditional on molecular state
nodes.shortDescription: A mass result conditional on a discrete rovibrational assignment retains separate alternative assignments. The within-branch statistical uncertainty alone does not represent uncertainty over state identity.

nodes.name: Static string and two-meson operator basis
nodes.shortDescription: An I=0 correlation matrix combines a static quark-antiquark string operator Q and a static-light meson-antimeson operator B. Its off-diagonal entries permit mixing in the specified theory with dynamical quarks.

nodes.name: Static-source area-law criterion
nodes.shortDescription: For unscreened fundamental sources, an asymptotically linear potential has string-tension coefficient K. Its large-contour criterion is ln W(C)=-K A(C)+O(perimeter), with A=a^2 times the minimal plaquette count.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande atmospheric acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the reported 33.0 kiloton-year, 535-day exposure in the 22.5 kiloton fiducial volume, with reconstructed vertices more than 2 m from the inner photomultiplier wall. Separate fully contained (FC) from exiting, partially contained (PC) events; use single-ring FC electron-like and muon-like classifications and the stated visible-energy division.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande two-flavor fit context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare the same selected samples with weighted Monte Carlo in five zenith bins and seven momentum bins for each of two particle-type samples. Minimize the 70-bin chi-squared over the oscillation parameters and eight normalization/shape nuisance parameters in corrected Equations 2-4, with alpha free and the seven other nuisance penalties specified in Table II.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande event double ratios
nodes.shortDescription: For R=(mu/e)_data/(mu/e)_MC, Table I reports sub-GeV R=0.63 +/- 0.03 statistical +/- 0.05 systematic and multi-GeV R_FC+PC=0.65 +/- 0.05 statistical +/- 0.08 systematic. The multi-GeV mu-like count includes the partially contained sample.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande conditional atmospheric splitting
nodes.shortDescription: Within the physical two-flavor nu_mu-to-nu_tau model, the reported best fit is sin^2(2 theta)=1.0 and Delta m^2=2.2e-3 eV^2, with chi-squared 65.2 for 67 degrees of freedom. The reported 90% confidence region has sin^2(2 theta)>0.82 and 5e-4<Delta m^2<6e-3 eV^2. These are conditional fit results from the same selected atmospheric acquisition.

nodes.name: Atmospheric flux and Cherenkov response
nodes.shortDescription: Use the report's atmospheric-flux and full-detector Monte Carlo predictions with neutrino interactions, visible-energy response, ring classification and containment. Compare control and alternative-flux inputs; retain flavor contamination, geomagnetic effects and neutrino-lepton angular/energy correlations when interpreting selected ratios and zenith patterns.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande selected FC and PC samples
nodes.shortDescription: The report contains 4353 FC and 301 PC events. The FC single-ring samples used in the oscillation analysis contain 1231 electron-like and 1158 muon-like sub-GeV events, plus 290 electron-like and 230 muon-like multi-GeV events. All 301 PC candidates enter the mu-like class without a single-ring requirement.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande no-oscillation event prediction
nodes.shortDescription: Table I reports no-oscillation Monte Carlo expectations of 1049.1 electron-like and 1573.6 muon-like sub-GeV single-ring events, 236.0 electron-like and 295.7 muon-like multi-GeV single-ring events, and 371.6 PC events. These are predicted event means conditioned on the atmospheric flux and detector/interaction response.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande mu-like zenith asymmetry
nodes.shortDescription: The selected mu-like sample shows a zenith-dependent deficit while electron-like distributions are compatible with the no-oscillation expectation. For multi-GeV FC+PC mu-like events the paper reports A=(U-D)/(U+D)=-0.296 +/- 0.048 +/- 0.01, retaining its two quoted uncertainty components. The multi-GeV electron-like comparison is -0.036 +/- 0.067 +/- 0.02.

nodes.name: Selected proton-decay search counts
nodes.shortDescription: The shared SK-I-IV search reports zero e+ pi0 candidates and one mu+ pi0 candidate, in the SK-IV conventional-volume upper-momentum region. No significant excess is found over the reported atmospheric-neutrino expectations of 0.59 and 0.94 events.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande partial-lifetime inference
nodes.shortDescription: Use the same selected data in the eight-region Bayesian rate construction, marginalizing the stated efficiency, exposure and background uncertainties before inverting each channel-rate bound.

nodes.name: Conditional proton partial-lifetime bounds
nodes.shortDescription: Under the published Bayesian selection and nuisance model, the reported 90 percent lower bounds are tau/B(p -> e+ pi0)>2.4e34 years and tau/B(p -> mu+ pi0)>1.6e34 years.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande signal and background model
nodes.shortDescription: Simulate free and oxygen-bound proton response and atmospheric-neutrino backgrounds under the paper nuclear, detector and interaction assumptions, with phase-specific exposure weighting.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande two-channel search
nodes.shortDescription: Apply the stated channel-specific Cherenkov, fiducial, kinematic and tagging selection to the shared April 1996-May 2018 SK-I-IV data, retaining detector phases and momentum regions.

nodes.name: TASSO charged-track measurement
nodes.shortDescription: The accepted charged-track momenta and specified shape definitions define the planar-event and three-jet readouts.

nodes.name: Hard-gluon interpretation of jet events
nodes.shortDescription: The report interprets the planar three-jet topology as evidence consistent with hard noncollinear gluon radiation in e+e- -> quark antiquark gluon, followed by fragmentation. The comparison excludes the specified collinear two-jet model; it does not determine all gluon properties or establish a free stable gluon.

nodes.name: Excess planar hadronic events
nodes.shortDescription: At high energy, A<0.04 and S>0.25 select 18 planar events versus 4.5 expected in the stated two-jet comparison and 4 in the randomization estimate. Selected events admit three-jet fits.

nodes.name: Three fitted hadronic jets
nodes.shortDescription: The selected coplanar events admit three-jet fits. Figure 6 displays two examples with three separated fitted axes and a two-jet comparator; the mean hadron transverse momentum relative to assigned jet axes is about 0.30 GeV/c in the 18 selected events.

nodes.name: Emulsion tau-neutrino appearance readout
nodes.shortDescription: The OPERA appearance readout identifies charged-current tau-neutrino interaction candidates through the topology and kinematics of the produced tau decay in an emulsion/lead detector. One-hadron, three-hadron, muon and electron decay selections are distinct channels with modeled backgrounds.

nodes.name: Tau-pair decay readout
nodes.shortDescription: In the CMS tau-pair selection, tau_h denotes a reconstructed hadronic tau decay; leptonic tau decays supply electron/muon candidates and missing neutrinos. Visible decay products and missing transverse momentum supply distinct visible-mass and SVFIT tau-pair mass observables.

nodes.name: Conditional transverse two-body mass
nodes.shortDescription: For two effectively massless physical daughter four-momenta from a two-body decay, define mT^2 = 2 pT1 pT2 (1-cos(deltaPhi)); the exact parent invariant mass then obeys M >= mT. Replacing these quantities by reconstructed electron and missing transverse vectors defines an estimator under a single-invisible-daughter assignment. Response errors can make that estimator exceed the true mass, so the exact inequality is not an eventwise detector guarantee. The transverse recoil is the magnitude of the daughter transverse-vector sum; mT is not a fully reconstructed invariant mass.

nodes.name: Two-state static-string mixing model
nodes.shortDescription: Within the two-state approximation, orthonormal string and two-meson basis states mix into energy states |1>=cos(theta)|Q>+sin(theta)|B> and |2>=-sin(theta)|Q>+cos(theta)|B>. A nonzero off-diagonal coupling can produce an avoided energy crossing.

nodes.name: UA1 1982 charged-boson search acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the 30-day November-December 1982 proton-antiproton run at sqrt(s)=540 GeV. The reported exposure is 18 nb^-1 after dead-time and instrumental corrections. Preserve the trigger and offline reconstruction stages preceding the electron and missing-energy searches.

nodes.name: UA1 selected electron and missing-energy candidates
nodes.shortDescription: The report displays six electron candidates A-F: five central-gondola events and endcap event B, with high transverse electron energy and associated imbalance. It restricts the final analysis to the five central events because B has possible asymmetric conversion and opposite muon activity. The separately labeled tau candidate is not another admitted electron-neutrino event.

nodes.name: UA1 conditional W mass interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: Keep the source transverse lower-limit construction separate from mass fitting under W decay kinematics and standard V-A couplings. The chosen fit corrects the transverse W motion event by event and uses Drell-Yan predictions without additional smearing; the full-QCD-smearing spectrum fit is a same-data alternative. Retain the final five-central-event restriction.

nodes.name: UA1 reported W transverse lower limit
nodes.shortDescription: Under the stated event interpretation and source confidence construction, UA1 reports mW > 73 GeV/c^2 at 90 percent confidence level from the transverse-mass lower-bound method.

nodes.name: UA1 historical conditional W mass fit
nodes.shortDescription: The chosen event-by-event transverse-motion correction and unsmeared Drell-Yan fit reports mW = 81 +/- 5 GeV/c^2 with allowance for systematic errors. The same report obtains 74 +/- 4 GeV/c^2 from the electron spectrum with full QCD smearing; this alternative exposes production/recoil-model dependence rather than a second independent mass measurement.

nodes.name: UA1 W response and selection conditions
nodes.shortDescription: Use central tracking, electromagnetic shower shape, hadronic leakage, energy/momentum agreement and the described isolation and jet criteria to select electron candidates. Reconstruct transverse energy imbalance with the calorimeter and use muon/response checks and the reported background controls; preserve the distinct central-gondola and endcap responses.

nodes.name: UA1 overlapping search selections
nodes.shortDescription: The electron-first and missing-energy-first searches recover the same five central electron candidates. The missing-energy search also retains two events removed by the electron energy/momentum match, which the report discusses as compatible with tau hypotheses. Their appearance is not an independent replicated W sample or a confirmed tau-decay measurement.

nodes.name: UA1 derived transverse event quantities
nodes.shortDescription: Table 3 gives derived transverse mass and transverse recoil summaries for all six displayed A-F electron candidates from their reconstructed electron and missing-energy vectors. These event quantities provide inputs to the interpretation; the endcap candidate remains displayed despite its exclusion from the final central-event analysis.

nodes.name: UA1 1983 neutral-boson search acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the four-week April-May 1983 proton-antiproton acquisition at sqrt(s)=540 GeV, with reported corrected exposure 55 nb^-1. Retain the electron, muon, jet and total-transverse-energy triggers and the express-line/offline selection used for the dilepton search.

nodes.name: UA1 constrained dimuon mass summary
nodes.shortDescription: For the one dimuon candidate, Section 5 reports a mass of 95.5 +/- 7.3 GeV/c^2. The source combines magnetic-deflection momenta with a solution using measured muon directions and calorimetric recoil under the no-neutrino assumption, as distinguished in Table 2.

nodes.name: UA1 historical electron-pair Z mass summary
nodes.shortDescription: The report combines its four electron-pair masses to give 95.2 +/- 2.5 GeV/c^2 and adopts that value in its neutral-boson interpretation. The result is retained with the source preliminary-calibration and uncorrected-radiation conventions; the number is not recomputed from rounded table centers.

nodes.name: UA1 original dilepton mass interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: Interpret the selected lepton pairs using the reported invariant-mass reconstruction and background evaluation. Combine the four electron-pair mass determinations as reported; for the dimuon retain the weighted magnetic and transverse-balance momenta conditional on no neutrino. Compare the topology and mass concentration with neutral-boson decay without treating peak spread as an intrinsic width measurement.

nodes.name: UA1 selected electron and muon pairs
nodes.shortDescription: The stated selection yields four electron-pair candidates and one dimuon candidate. Figure 1 shows nested electron selection stages with 152, 6 and 4 events; the dimuon analysis scans 42 events after its offline requirements to identify the single candidate. These are separate channel selections within one acquisition, not five directly observed stable Z objects.

nodes.name: UA1 dilepton response and calibration
nodes.shortDescription: Adopt the central track, electromagnetic shower and penetrating-muon response, test-beam and source calibration, cosmic-muon alignment checks and background estimates described in the report. Preserve electron radiation and geometric response limitations, the unfinished electromagnetic energy calibration and the different magnetic/recoil inputs used for the dimuon.

nodes.name: Polyethylene-covered block loss diagnostic
nodes.shortDescription: A dedicated diagnostic reintroduces the fallen aluminum block, covered in polyethylene foil, at its original trap location. The nearly absorbing covering is used to estimate how often UCN encounter that surface; a separate aluminum-loss model translates this diagnostic to the production contamination.

nodes.name: Material-contact loss diagnostic
nodes.shortDescription: Reintroducing the polyethylene-covered block at the contamination location produces an additional approximately 424 s component in the stored-UCN yield. The authors use this diagnostic surface-incidence estimate in a separate aluminum-loss correction.

nodes.name: Neutron storage and non-decay losses
nodes.shortDescription: The Gonzalez storage model sums an intrinsic decay rate and residual-gas upscattering, depolarization and escape rates. A fitted storage-loss rate can identify the conventional free-neutron lifetime only with the declared non-decay-loss corrections and detector model.

nodes.name: Combined 2017-2018 neutron lifetime
nodes.shortDescription: Gonzalez reports 877.75+/-0.28 (statistical) +0.22/-0.16 (systematic) seconds for the 2017/2018 data. The central estimate is the unweighted mean of the three full-data global fits, with the largest analyzer statistical uncertainty retained.

nodes.name: UCNtau 2017 production preparation
nodes.shortDescription: The 2017 UCNtau campaign loads for 150 s, cleans for 50 s, stores for 20-1550 s and counts in three detector positions for 40, 20 and 150 s. Monitor choices and normalization precede the buffer-volume arrangement used in 2018. Part of the production data was exposed to a fallen aluminum component.

nodes.name: UCNtau 2017 reported lifetime fits
nodes.shortDescription: For the 2017 campaign, Gonzalez Table III reports global-fit neutron lifetimes A 877.68+/-0.30, B 877.78+/-0.34 and C 877.74+/-0.33 seconds. These are three analyses of the same campaign with statistical uncertainties, not three independent experiments.

nodes.name: UCNtau 2018 production preparation
nodes.shortDescription: The 2018 UCNtau campaign adds a buffer/precleaning volume and loads for 300 s. After 50 s cleaning, neutrons are stored for 20-1550 s and counted at cleaner, middle and bottom positions for 40, 20 and 150 s. Monitor detectors sample the changed loading arrangement.

nodes.name: UCNtau 2018 reported lifetime fits
nodes.shortDescription: For the 2018 campaign, Gonzalez Table III reports global-fit neutron lifetimes A 878.06+/-0.49, B 877.80+/-0.46 and C 877.55+/-0.55 seconds. These are three analyses of the same campaign with statistical uncertainties, not three independent experiments.

nodes.name: 2018 uncleaned UCN diagnostic
nodes.shortDescription: In dedicated 2018 runs the cleaner is never lowered before storage. The cleaner detector and primary detector then count UCN above the usual cleaning height; comparison with production conditions is used to assess escaping high-energy neutrons.

nodes.name: Shorter storage in uncleaned 2018 runs
nodes.shortDescription: The deliberately uncleaned 2018 runs show high-position UCN counts and an extracted storage lifetime about 15 s shorter. The authors associate the reduction with an escape rate around 2*10^-5 per second under their loss model.

nodes.name: Combined 2020-2022 neutron lifetime
nodes.shortDescription: Final Musedinovic Table III reports 877.96+/-0.37 seconds for the new 2020-2022 production campaigns, with statistical uncertainty. This current-data estimate uses the reported yearly averaging and correction procedure.

nodes.name: UCNtau 2020 production preparation
nodes.shortDescription: The 2020 UCNtau campaign uses the Fast boron-coated ZnS dagger and roundhouse-dump normalization. An initial dagger with about 1.0 Hz americium-contamination background is replaced by one with about 0.2 Hz background; both belong to the declared campaign analysis.

nodes.name: UCNtau 2020 reported lifetime fits
nodes.shortDescription: For the 2020 campaign, final Musedinovic Table III reports A 879.47+/-0.86, B 879.38+/-0.92 and C 879.32+/-0.90 seconds. The reported yearly average is 879.39+/-0.89 seconds, with statistical uncertainty; the analyzer estimates share the campaign data.

nodes.name: UCNtau 2021 Fast and Slow preparations
nodes.shortDescription: The 2021 UCNtau campaign includes a Fast dagger and a Slow variant with one whole side covered by UCN-reflective aluminum. The shared year result combines those declared configurations after rate and normalization corrections.

nodes.name: UCNtau 2021 reported lifetime fits
nodes.shortDescription: For the 2021 campaign, final Musedinovic Table III reports A 878.41+/-0.60, B 878.40+/-0.59 and C 878.41+/-0.55 seconds. The reported yearly average is 878.41+/-0.58 seconds, with statistical uncertainty; the analyzer estimates share the campaign data.

nodes.name: Uncleaned UCN counting-tail ratio
nodes.shortDescription: The 2022 uncleaned diagnostic reports a background-subtracted 200 s/40 s Pk1 count ratio of 1.76+/-0.15. The ratio corrects high-position counts missed by the short gate before the normal bottom-position counting interval.

nodes.name: UCNtau 2022 segmented-dagger preparation
nodes.shortDescription: The 2022 UCNtau campaign divides the dagger into four vertical strips read by eight PMTs, with additional reflective aluminum strips. Segment photon thresholds are balanced to account for gain differences before the reported combined lifetime is used.

nodes.name: UCNtau 2022 reported lifetime fits
nodes.shortDescription: For the 2022 campaign, final Musedinovic Table III reports A 876.81+/-0.56, B 876.78+/-0.58, C 877.06+/-0.53 and D 877.08+/-0.63 seconds. The reported yearly average is 876.93+/-0.57 seconds, with statistical uncertainty; the analyzer estimates share the campaign data.

nodes.name: Segment-sensitive fitted neutron lifetime
nodes.shortDescription: Four strip fits from the 2022 dagger span about 10 s. Balancing relative photon thresholds across strips reduces the combined fitted lifetime by 0.22 s; the published 2022 result uses balanced gains.

nodes.name: 2022 cleaning-tail diagnostic
nodes.shortDescription: Dedicated uncleaned 2022 runs compare 40 s and 200 s counting gates at the cleaning-height position Pk1. This measures the long tail missed by the shorter gate before the dagger is lowered to the bottom position Pk2.

nodes.name: Combined five-campaign neutron lifetime
nodes.shortDescription: Musedinovic reports a global UCNtau free-neutron lifetime of 877.83+/-0.22 (statistical) +0.20/-0.17 (systematic) seconds from the 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021 and 2022 campaigns. It imports the earlier corrected data and applies the stated current systematic budget.

nodes.name: Ground-state observable variance
nodes.shortDescription: For H=p^2/(2m)+m omega^2 q^2/2, [q,p]=i hbar and m,omega>0, the normalized ground state has Var(q)=hbar/(2m omega), Var(p)=hbar m omega/2, Var(H)=0 and <N>=0. Fluctuation here denotes measurement dispersion in a specified state.

nodes.name: Normalized shape and alpha deformation algebra
nodes.shortDescription: Nine synthetic common-scale checks preserve normalized four-bin fractions, while three nonuniform controls change the shape. Equation 3 gives an added inverse-alpha difference of 0.20473178364144 for the printed reference and slope; the nominal contribution and full reported difference are not calculated.

nodes.name: Effective-alpha algebra calculation
nodes.shortDescription: Use exact rational arithmetic for synthetic four-bin cross-section integrals, common positive rescaling and Equation 3. Adopt only the printed central alpha^-1(0)=137.03599976, S=-0.00036 GeV^-2 and endpoints -2.1,-6.25 GeV^2 for the added-deformation calculation.

nodes.name: Free-field vacuum correlations
nodes.shortDescription: For the real free scalar vacuum in natural units, <0|phi(x)phi(y)|0>=integral d^3p/(2pi)^3 exp[-ip(x-y)]/(2E_p). The spacelike field commutator vanishes even though this two-point function can be nonzero.

nodes.name: External mass shells and exchange-transfer algebra
nodes.shortDescription: All four synthetic external momenta have p^2=16 and conserved total four-momentum. The exchange q=p1-p3=(0,6/5,-12/5,0) has q^2=t=-36/5, with s=100 and u=-144/5, so s+t+u=64=4m^2. Two rational boosts preserve these invariants. Forward scattering permits t=0; generic amplitudes 1 and -1 cancel before squaring.

nodes.name: Synthetic scattering kinematics
nodes.shortDescription: Use exact rational four-vectors with metric +--- and c=1. Set synthetic mass m=4, incoming (5,3,0,0),(5,-3,0,0) and outgoing (5,9/5,12/5,0),(5,-9/5,-12/5,0); check conservation, external mass shells and s,t,u under two rational proper boosts. Include a forward-transfer boundary and generic complex-number interference controls.

nodes.name: Independent electron Yukawa mass relation
nodes.shortDescription: The separately specified real electron coupling G_e in Weinberg1967 multiplies the scalar-lepton term. Replacing the scalar by its chosen background gives M_e=lambda_W*G_e. Changing G_e changes this mass without fixing the gauge couplings or predicting the numerical mass hierarchy.

nodes.name: Historical electroweak lepton-model background
nodes.shortDescription: Weinberg1967 specifies an electron-type chiral doublet/singlet, SU(2) and hypercharge gauge fields and a scalar doublet with kinetic term -1/2*|D_mu phi|^2. In its own convention choose <phi>=lambda_W*(1,0) real, and eliminate the stated scalar phase/charged fields by a gauge transformation before reading the quadratic mass terms.

nodes.name: Historical charged and neutral gauge masses
nodes.shortDescription: In Weinberg1967 conventions the neutral squared-mass matrix in the (A3,B) basis is lambda_W^2/4 times [[g^2,g*gprime],[g*gprime,gprime^2]]. Its massive direction is (g,gprime), its massless photon direction is (-gprime,g), M_W=lambda_W*g/2, M_Z=lambda_W*sqrt(g^2+gprime^2)/2 and e=g*gprime/sqrt(g^2+gprime^2).

nodes.name: Fundamental SU(2) Wilson-loop expectation
nodes.shortDescription: For a closed lattice contour C, W(C)=<one half Tr(product of U along C)> in the SU(2) fundamental representation, with path ordering and orientation retained. The expectation is taken in a specified lattice ensemble.

nodes.name: Thesis source alpha-emission rate
nodes.shortDescription: The thesis reports a total alpha-source activity of 23545.2+/-7.0 per second from its two-stack calibration. Its printed stack estimates and common-error conventions do not uniquely reproduce every reported digit.

nodes.name: Yue two-stack source calibration
nodes.shortDescription: Measure the alpha source with two spacer configurations sharing the Cu-Cu-1 aperture; correct counting losses and combine the source rates with uncorrelated stack errors and a common aperture contribution.

nodes.name: Yue absolute fluence calibration
nodes.shortDescription: Use the absolute calibration completed in 2011 for the same 6LiF monitor against the AlphaGamma neutron-rate transfer, convert its monochromatic response to the thermal reference, and assess transfer to the earlier acquisition through the stated aperture and deposit controls.

nodes.name: Absolute beam monitor efficiency
nodes.shortDescription: The 2011 calibration reports epsilon_0=(3.1098+/-0.0017)e-5 at the 2200 m/s convention. Applying this monitor response to the earlier acquisition uses adopted DeltaOmega=0 and DeltaRho=0, with 0.1 percent deposit-density uncertainty.

nodes.name: Recalibrated beam lifetime
nodes.shortDescription: Recalibrating the same beam acquisition gives a reported lifetime of 887.7 seconds: 1.2 statistical and 1.9 systematic seconds in the abstract, with 2.3 seconds total in the body and Table II. This is a conditional updated inference from the existing acquisition.

nodes.name: Yue same-acquisition lifetime reanalysis
nodes.shortDescription: Rescale the published Nico lifetime by the old-to-new thermal monitor efficiency ratio and adopted aperture and deposit drift factors, retaining the earlier proton corrections and acquisition.

nodes.name: Normalized AlphaGamma monitor efficiency
nodes.shortDescription: The detailed article reports idealized epsilon_0(0,0)=(3.1101+/-0.0018)e-5, with (3.1101+/-0.0010)e-5 from the statistical weighted fit and 5.8e-4 total relative uncertainty. This is a corrected monitor response, not an independently acquired neutron lifetime.

nodes.name: AlphaGamma normalization and uncertainty analysis
nodes.shortDescription: Normalize the measured monitor ratios to a central thermal beam using configuration-dependent detector, transport and target corrections; fit the reported calibration points while propagating common correction uncertainties.

nodes.name: Detailed-article source alpha-emission rate
nodes.shortDescription: The 2018 article reports R_Pu=23538.4+/-4.6 per second for its stated source-metrology preparation. That reported value remains distinct from the quotient of the displayed corrected rate and effective solid angle.

nodes.name: Detailed AlphaGamma measurement preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Use the article-specific alpha-source metrology, thin/thick/thin boron counting cycles and timed background-subtracted detector rates to establish the neutron-monitor transfer on the NG-6m beam.

nodes.name: Transducin and phosphodiesterase activity
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstituted biochemical activity used as one part of the rod-response literature synthesis.

nodes.name: cGMP-dependent rod conductance
nodes.shortDescription: Cyclic-nucleotide control of conductance in rod outer-segment patches.

nodes.name: Cone-evoked synaptic drive
nodes.shortDescription: Cone-selective stimulation and excitatory synaptic responses in the midget-cell preparation.

nodes.name: Ganglion membrane excitability
nodes.shortDescription: Active membrane conductances in the salamander firing study; an electrical state is not itself a resource or sufficient input.

nodes.name: Retinal ganglion spike responses
nodes.shortDescription: Spike dynamics in separately specified ganglion-cell preparations, including synaptic and intrinsic light-response routes.

nodes.name: Specified illumination
nodes.shortDescription: An experimental input specified by spectrum, timing and intensity.

nodes.name: Intrinsic melanopsin ganglion response
nodes.shortDescription: Light response in sampled mouse ganglion cells with rod/cone synaptic drive blocked.

nodes.name: Mouse OFF sustained alpha light-drive protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Rod-preferring stimulation under the explicitly reviewed comparison contexts. This record preserves a protocol-specific boundary; it does not identify a generic receptor response with this preparation.

nodes.name: Mouse OFF sustained alpha measured output
nodes.shortDescription: Excitatory synaptic input to OFF parasol (primate) and OFF sustained alpha (mouse) RGCs before and during LY/APB. This record preserves a protocol-specific boundary; it does not identify a generic receptor response with this preparation.

nodes.name: Mouse transient OFF alpha light-drive protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Rod-preferring stimulation under the explicitly reviewed comparison contexts. This record preserves a protocol-specific boundary; it does not identify a generic receptor response with this preparation.

nodes.name: Mouse transient OFF alpha measured output
nodes.shortDescription: Loose-patch, baseline-subtracted peak firing response of transient OFF alpha RGCs at light offset. This record preserves a protocol-specific boundary; it does not identify a generic receptor response with this preparation.

nodes.name: Ocular optical transfer
nodes.shortDescription: Optical operation in an existing human eye, with aberration correction as a functional perturbation.

nodes.name: Rhodopsin photochemistry
nodes.shortDescription: Light-dependent retinal isomerization in specified rhodopsin preparations; early photoproducts are distinct from later signalling states.

nodes.name: Human photoreceptor topography
nodes.shortDescription: Measured human rod/cone distributions; a structural description without a claim about their developmental generation.

nodes.name: Prepared rhodopsin
nodes.shortDescription: An existing protein/chromophore preparation; its availability is separate from a folding or developmental event.

nodes.name: Primate OFF parasol light-drive protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Rod-preferring stimulation under the explicitly reviewed comparison contexts. This record preserves a protocol-specific boundary; it does not identify a generic receptor response with this preparation.

nodes.name: Primate OFF parasol measured output
nodes.shortDescription: Excitatory synaptic input to OFF parasol (primate) and OFF sustained alpha (mouse) RGCs before and during LY/APB. This record preserves a protocol-specific boundary; it does not identify a generic receptor response with this preparation.

nodes.name: Membrane electrical recording context
nodes.shortDescription: Voltage, ionic and recording conditions needed to interpret measured membrane currents; no energetic-resource label is inferred.

nodes.name: Existing macaque retinal circuit
nodes.shortDescription: Prepared cone/midget circuitry under the recorded photopic conditions; does not represent tissue-type formation.

nodes.name: Midget-pathway surround and opponency
nodes.shortDescription: A macaque cone-driven functional property with measured pharmacological contrasts.

nodes.name: Rod phototransduction response
nodes.shortDescription: An operating rod light response, with biochemical and electrical evidence distinguished by preparation.

nodes.name: Retinal sampling representation
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed registration of optical input and receptor positions; neither an executed sampling model nor a neural retinotopic map.

nodes.name: Layer 6 corticogeniculate perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Selective optogenetic manipulation of layer 6 corticogeniculate projections; behavioral/anesthetic state not verified in the read passages.

nodes.name: dLGN response under cortical feedback manipulation
nodes.shortDescription: Removing cortical input produces increases or decreases depending on cell and contrast; driving input reduces evoked counts.

nodes.name: Frontal eye field perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: FEF stimulation below the saccade threshold with V4 recordings; full methods not reviewed.

nodes.name: Geniculocortical input activity
nodes.shortDescription: The reported functional connections favor matching contrast sign and aligned receptive-field subregions.

nodes.name: Predictive coding hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A family of computational interpretations requiring explicit competing-model tests; no uniquely identified biological prediction-error operation is asserted.

nodes.name: Primate striate feature organization
nodes.shortDescription: The abstract reports distinct columnar organizations for orientation and ocular dominance.

nodes.name: Rat V1 orientation selectivity
nodes.shortDescription: Rat V1 shows orientation selectivity without discernible local organization at the reported scale; the cat comparison concerns area 18.

nodes.name: Retinogeniculate spike transfer
nodes.shortDescription: Closely spaced retinal spikes have different conditional transfer efficacy; the extracellular result does not identify its cellular mechanism.

nodes.name: Cat V1 simple-cell input alignment
nodes.shortDescription: The reported functional connections favor matching contrast sign and aligned receptive-field subregions.

nodes.name: V4 response modulation
nodes.shortDescription: Retinotopically corresponding stimulation enhances V4 responses; noncorresponding stimulation can suppress them.
